Ask what makes position x not identical to position y if nothing could distinguish them by occupying them differently. The answer can’t be intrinsic properties of positions. Take either line. On relationalism, positions have no intrinsic properties apart from their relational structure. On substantivalism they do have an intrinsic identity, but that identity does no individuating work without the relational structure tying it to the rest of the manifold. Either way, what distinguishes one position from another runs through how they stand to one another, not through any content that distinguishes them independently. The answer must be that the positions sustain distinct possibilities: something could be at x without being at y, and could move between them. Sustaining distinct possibilities requires directed succession as the temporal order within which *at x then at y* has content. Without succession, the *distinctness* of positions collapses into labels that differ in no operative way.

Which line bears the most weight depends on what the reader resists. The traversability and interval-reality lines are decisive for anyone who grants that real structure must be operative rather than notational. The asymmetry-location and position-individuation lines are decisive for anyone who grants the relata but resists the realizer: they close the remaining gap by locating where the contested feature must reside.

What about sequences that aren’t spatial, or structures without time? Three stock objections press: primitive thisness, primitive asymmetric dependence, and *non-spatial* sequences. Primitive thisness may individuate the states nonqualitatively, but if it does so it is differentiating structure under Structural Individuation; that alone still does not supply their order. The transition additionally requires them to occupy differentiated source and uptake positions in one directed relation—the narrower work of the S-limb (§2.4.7). If the after-state depends primitively on the before-state, the dependence relation itself supplies those differentiated positions (dependent and depended-upon), confirming rather than blocking the relational carrier. The third objection is conceded at the scope boundary: logical order (the natural numbers under <, say, or Prior’s 1967 tense-logic operators) is a genuine ordered structure with neither T nor S in the operative sense—nothing happens in it, nothing occupies it, nothing excludes anything from it. It stands outside the domain the biconditional quantifies over, engaged at §8.1.5, rather than being reclassified as concrete extension.

The fuller tests belong with §8.1.5, where four Platonist positions (Frege-Gödel classical Platonism, Shapiro’s *ante rem* structuralism, Maddy’s naturalized Platonism, and Balaguer’s plenitudinous Platonism) are put under load individually, and where Benacerraf’s (1965; 1973) multiple-reduction and access results close the residue.

*Scope.* The extension required here isn’t necessarily physical space in the recognizably Newtonian sense; the succession required isn’t necessarily physical time. Each is the structural role of which physical space and physical time are this universe’s realizers. But the framework-invariance runs over *media*—structures that host, occupy, exclude, and carry—not over relational structure as such. Any medium hosting ordered succession must exhibit real relational extension, and any medium hosting real, occupiable extension must exhibit ordered succession. Physical spacetime realizes both; abstract order and pure geometry aren’t media in this sense, and the biconditional doesn’t quantify over them.

*Lifting to the triconditional.* Each of the four lines argues T↔S, but each line already deploys Φ in its argument: Φ appears not as a separate premise but as part of the operative work T↔S requires to run. The traversability line invokes travel; travel requires a traveler that persists across the crossing (Φ). The interval-reality line invokes traversal across the interval; traversal requires the same. The asymmetry-location line invokes the asymmetry being carried forward by the after-state; that carrying-forward requires Φ-persistence. The position-individuation line invokes positions sustaining distinct possibilities across the succession that makes them distinct possibilities; the sustaining is Φ at the level of position-bearing.

The reverse direction runs the same way. A Φ-persistent being with no Temporality has no succession to persist through; a Φ-medium with no S has no positions to bear; a Φ-relation between cause and effect requires direction (T) and interval (S) to be more than self-relation. The four lines therefore deliver Φ↔T alongside T↔S, as part of the same realizer move read from the T pivot.

The pairwise biconditional T↔S arrives already engaging Φ; the same lines deliver T↔Φ; the cross-entailment Φ↔S follows from the symmetric work from the S pivot established at §2.6.3. The result is T ↔ (S ∧ Φ): succession can’t stand without both extension and being, and the conjunction can’t stand without succession.

*Duration* presents as temporal vocabulary: the span of an interval. But the result already reached runs in ordinary language before any formal analysis arrives. Duration requires a persistent being (Φ): without something that endures, there is no duration *of* anything, only a labeled interval with no occupant. The occupying has a name: *Holding* (§1.4.3), the requirement that the carrier-role be genuinely occupied rather than standing empty. It is what makes an interval a duration *of* something. It requires relational extension (S): without somewhere for the being to be, the interval can’t be located, and an interval without location isn’t a span but a label. Strip either Condition and the word stops applying. Duration isn’t a temporal word that happens to imply the others. It is a triconditional word built around the succession pivot: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ) embedded in a single noun.

*Convergence.* Four lines, one move, three Conditions, with the price now fixed once: operative T requires differentiated positions and a bearer in the same realizer; operative Φ requires an ordered interval; operative S requires an ordered crossing when it functions in a change-realizer. None of those follows from the thin predicate alone. They follow when the Operative-Role Bridge is applied and the role is claimed to do concrete work. Three sides of one structural fact are thereby recovered inside the target domain, with the same fact read from the extension and persistence pivots at §2.6.3–2.6.4.

**[Lemma]**

**Succession’s Realizers** · *Lemma*

Under the Operative-Role Bridge, directed succession is biconditional with relational extension and persistent bearing in the same change-realizer: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ). Succession doing concrete work requires differentiated positions across its order and a bearer that carries the order between them. Conversely, extension operating as a crossable medium and occupied by a bearer persisting across its positions supplies the ordered crossing that T names. The claim is restricted to operative Conditions in concrete change-realizers; thin modal-core predicates and static structures are not its antecedent.

**Depends on:** Operative-Role Bridge; the directed-succession, differentiated-position, and bearer criteria defended in this section
**Feeds into:** Mutual Containment (§2.6.5 Mutual Containment)

*Tested against.* The Humean denial of necessary connection between distinct existences, the canonical opponent of the realizer move’s real reading (§8.2.2); Sider’s stage theory and temporal-parts ontology, pressing on what makes succession real (§8.3.2); Platonism about non-spatial sequences (Frege–Gödel, Shapiro, Maddy, Balaguer), the principal order-without-extension opponent (§8.1.5); emergent time, pressing on whether T is fundamental enough to enter the biconditional (§8.1.2); and Tegmark’s mathematical universe, on whether order-without-extension is enough (§9.9).

### 2.6.3 Extension’s Two Conditions
*The realizer move, applied to S ↔ (T ∧ Φ).* Under the Operative-Role Bridge, relational extension functioning as a concrete medium is biconditional with directed succession and persistent bearing: S ↔ (T ∧ Φ). State the scope before the lines run. Static geometry and abstract relational structure can be real without occupants, exclusion, or crossing; so can a concrete spatial configuration considered only at an instant. None is refuted, and none is the operative antecedent. Within the target domain, the Φ→S direction runs on the distinctness and interaction lines; the S→Φ direction runs on occupancy and traversal premises stated openly as premises about a medium doing change-realizing work, not as consequences of extension alone. The same move is worked from the succession and persistence pivots at §2.6.2 and 2.6.4; the three vantages, with their scopes, are gathered at §2.6.5.

*Direction 1: Φ→S.* Two lines converge on the same result: Φ operating across differentiated terms in a concrete transition requires S. This is a result of the bridge plus the lines below, not an analytic truth about every thin bearer.

*First, the distinctness line.* For causation to be real, its source and uptake terms must be genuinely distinguishable, not merely two names for one undifferentiated state. This need not require two numerically distinct beings: one persisting system may occupy the causal roles at different stages. A primitive haecceity may contribute nonqualitative individuating structure, but it does not by itself order one term as source and the other as uptake. That ordering is a relation with differentiated roles—*from* and *to*, cause and effect—and it is the Spatiality-role the causal process instantiates. The argument does not infer that the haecceity itself is spatial. It infers that causation requires relationally differentiated causal positions in addition to whatever individuates the relata.

*Second, the interaction line.* Causal exchange isn’t a bare relation between two labels. It requires transmission from a source-state or role to an uptake-state or role. The interval need not be a distance between two beings; internal causation may run between distinguishable states of one persisting system. What cannot be removed is relational separation between the causal terms: without any distinction between source and uptake, there is no path or articulation by which influence could run, only one undifferentiated event described twice. The relational interval that distinguishes the causal terms is the Spatiality-role invoked here.

Whether one approaches from the distinctness of the relata or from the interaction between them, Substantiality without Spatiality collapses: either the relata aren’t genuinely distinct, or the causation has no path. A being that carries influence needs somewhere to carry it. The interval doesn’t merely lie between them; it is what makes them two things at all.

*Direction 2: S→Φ.* Now the reverse. Two lines converge from the other direction: S operating as a concrete change-medium requires Φ. The Operative-Role Bridge, not extension alone, carries that antecedent.

*First, the occupancy line.* A load-bearing structural feature of Spatiality is exclusive occupancy—the fact that two things can’t occupy the same position—the point where Spatiality’s positions meet Substantiality’s work. But exclusion is a causal act in the broad sense: to exclude is to prevent, to resist, to block, and preventing, resisting, and blocking are things only a causally active medium can do. A primitivist about exclusion may read it as a primitive structural fact rather than a canonical-causal one. That view inherits the same medium-work under different vocabulary, by the argument of §2.4.8. Whatever makes a primitive exclusion *do* exclusion-work must operate across the foreclosure interval. That cross-interval operation is what Φ names, whether read as canonical causation or as primitive foreclosure performing the same structural function.

A position that nothing *could* occupy functions as an abstract coordinate label, not a position *in a medium*. The premise doing the work here is stated openly: what makes a medium’s positions positions rather than mathematical indices is their occupiability—and occupiability is a premise about media, not a consequence of relational structure as such. A pure geometry owes nobody occupants; a medium’s extension is constituted by what could stand in it and exclude from it. The argument doesn’t deny that *empty* regions of physical space are real: empty regions are real precisely because they are occupiable; something *could* occupy them, even when nothing currently does. The reality of an empty region rests on the occupiability of its positions, not on the presence of actual occupants at every position. What collapses into a coordinate label isn’t the empty region but the would-be position that nothing could ever occupy. And occupiability requires something capable of occupying: a medium with the causal capacity to occupy and to exclude other occupants. That medium is Substantiality. Exclusive occupancy without a being is exclusion with nothing doing the excluding.

*Second, the interval line.* A relational interval between two positions is real only if something can traverse it. An interval that nothing crosses, nothing bridges, nothing moves through is a notation, not a distance. The reality of the interval consists in its traversability, and traversability requires a medium that persists through the crossing. The medium that makes spatial intervals real rather than abstract (by being what crosses them and persists through them) is Substantiality.

Whether one approaches from the occupancy of positions or from the reality of intervals, Spatiality without Substantiality collapses: either exclusion has no excluder, or intervals have no medium to make them real. The pressure is symmetric: just as Substantiality without Spatiality had no path for its causation, Spatiality without Substantiality has no medium to make its positions real. Each is the other’s internal requirement, not its external correlate.

*Lifting to the triconditional.* Each of the four lines runs on more than the pair it names. Causal exchange (the interaction line) requires transmission, and transmission across an interval is travel, already temporal. Exclusive occupancy (the occupancy line) is exclusion, and exclusion is a causal act that runs in time. Distinctness (the distinctness line) presupposes positions whose differentiation can’t be static: a being that excludes another at a position must endure long enough to do so. The pairwise biconditional S↔Φ arrives already engaging T; the four lines deliver S↔T as part of the same argument. The result is S ↔ (T ∧ Φ): extension can’t stand without both succession and being, and the conjunction can’t stand without extension.

*Movement* presents as spatial vocabulary: traversal of distance. But movement requires directed succession (T): without before and after, there is no moving, only occupying: being at a position rather than arriving at it. It requires a persistent being (Φ): without something that moves, there is no movement, only position change: a difference between two states with no owner of the difference. Strip either Condition and the word stops applying. Movement isn’t a spatial word that happens to imply the others. It is a triconditional word built around the extension pivot: S ↔ (T ∧ Φ) embedded in a single noun.

*Convergence.* Within the domain of media—concrete, occupiable, exclusive extension—extension without a being is empty, a being without extension has no positions to occupy, and neither has its work to do without succession to do it through. Outside that domain the biconditional makes no claim: static geometry and abstract structure are real, unrefuted, and engaged in Chapters 8 and 9. Three sides of one structural fact, read from the extension pivot at its stated scope. The remaining link is the one that feels obvious, which is precisely why it must be proved.

**[Lemma]**

**Extension’s Realizers** · *Lemma*

Under the Operative-Role Bridge, relational extension functioning as a concrete change-medium is biconditional with directed succession and persistent bearing: S ↔ (T ∧ Φ). Static extension, however real, is not the operative antecedent.

**Depends on:** Relational Distinctness (§2.4.7); Operative-Role Bridge
**Feeds into:** Mutual Containment (§2.6.5 Mutual Containment)

*Tested against.* Mereological nihilism, the canonical anti-S opponent—no composites, hence no relational structure beyond simples (§8.3.4); structural realism (Ladyman, French), which agrees on relational fabric and diverges on what the relations consist in (§9.10); Sider’s structuralism, on spatial structure (§7.2.8); bundle theory and tropes, on whether positions are anything beyond their occupants (§8.3.3); and Tegmark, on whether relational extension is mathematical rather than substantive (§9.9).

### 2.6.4 Persistence’s Two Conditions
*The realizer move, applied to Φ ↔ (T ∧ S).* Under the Operative-Role Bridge, persistence doing the work of connecting differentiated stages in a concrete transition is biconditional with directed succession and relational extension: Φ ↔ (T ∧ S). The two halves carry different prices. The T↔Φ half runs on bearing across an ordered interval and succession borne as one passage. The S half concerns concrete change-realizers: the bearer persists across differentiated states or positions in the same medium. It is not a claim that every abstract bearer, field at an instant, or merely enduring object is spatial-and-temporal by definition. Within the stated domain, the interval across which Φ operates is the differentiated extension that S names. The following lines defend that deployment rather than borrowing a field-level conclusion.

*Direction 1: T→Φ.* Two lines converge on the same result: T operating as one concrete succession requires Φ. The claim is not analytic of the thin ordering predicate.

*First, the continuity line.* Think of a relay race. The baton must be carried from one runner to the next: if it vanishes at the handoff and a new baton appears, nothing was relayed. Directed succession works the same way: something must carry influence from before-state to after-state. Without a persistence medium, what produced the before-state leaves nothing behind, and the after-state arrives from nowhere. That isn’t directed transition. It is replacement. The distinction between transition and replacement is constitutive, not a matter of degree. A before-state that transmits nothing forward doesn’t produce an after-state. For succession to be causally structured rather than merely sequential, something must persist across the transition as the vehicle of causal transmission. That persistence medium is Substantiality.

*Second, the identity line.* For there to be a subject that changes, something must persist as the same subject through the change. If nothing endures from the before-state into the after-state, there is no subject that underwent the transition; there are two disconnected states with nothing in common. Change requires a thing that was one way and is now another. Remove the thing and the change goes with it: what remains is two descriptions with no owner.

Whether one approaches from the continuity of causal influence or from the identity of the changing subject, Temporality without Substantiality collapses: either succession has no vehicle, or change has no subject. Persistence isn’t what survives change. It is what makes change possible: the invariant through which variation has content. What flashes and vanishes hasn’t passed through time at all. That is replacement, not succession.

*Direction 2: Φ→T.* Two lines converge from the other direction: Φ operating across stages of a concrete transition requires T. A bearer or field considered without that operation is outside the antecedent.

*First, the persistence line.* Persistence isn’t a static property. It is persistence through: through transitions, through changes, through the passage from before to after. A medium that never stands in an earlier/later order isn’t persisting through anything. It exists at no moment, endures across no interval, and sustains nothing from one state to the next. To persist is to be the same thing at a later time as at an earlier time. Remove the temporal ordering and there is nothing for persistence to consist in. Substantiality without Temporality is the word *being* with no structural content, not a being in a reduced mode.

*Second, the causation line.* Causal capacity (the ability to affect and be affected) requires asymmetric ordering. The cause precedes the effect. The affecting comes before the being-affected. Without temporal direction, there is no fact distinguishing which is the cause and which is the effect. The causal relation becomes symmetric, and symmetric causation isn’t causation but mere correlation. The asymmetry isn’t a feature added to causation from outside. It is what causation consists in: an influence that runs from source to recipient, not a symmetric correlation between co-occurring states. Remove the temporal direction and the influence has no arrow, and an arrow without direction isn’t an arrow.

Whether one approaches from the persistence of the medium or from the directionality of its causal relations, Substantiality without Temporality collapses: either persistence has no succession to persist through, or causation has no direction.

Succession needs a persistence medium. The persistence medium needs temporal direction. They empty together. The argument that derived them ran on both.

*Lifting to the triconditional.* Each of the four lines argues T↔Φ, and each visibly deploys S when its subject is a concrete bearer in a medium: a baton is carried between positions, an enduring subject of physical change endures across differentiated states, causal asymmetry runs from one role-position to another, persistence spans an interval. This is the local derivation of the S-conjunct for the domain the theorem spends, not a transfer from a field-level result. The result, at that stated scope, is Φ ↔ (T ∧ S): within change-realizing structures, persistent bearing can’t stand without succession and differentiated extension, and the conjunction can’t stand without a bearer. Whether any bearer stands outside that domain—non-spatial minds, abstract endurers—isn’t settled here and isn’t assumed; those rivals are met case by case: abstract endurers under Mathematical Platonism (§8.1.5), non-spatial minds under Idealism (§9.5), and atemporal grounding under the changeless-ground treatment (§10.2.3).

*Interaction* presents as causal vocabulary: things affecting one another. But interaction requires relational extension (S): without distinct positions, there is no between, and without a between, what appears to be exchange is a single event described twice. It requires directed succession (T): causal influence runs from before-state to after-state; without that direction, what appears to be affecting is correlation, not causation. Strip either Condition and the word stops applying. Interaction isn’t a causal word that happens to imply the others. It is a triconditional word built around the persistence pivot: Φ ↔ (T ∧ S) embedded in a single noun.

*A dynamic supplement.* The realizer lines establish Φ↔(T∧S) conceptually: persistence can’t stand without succession and extension, and the conjunction can’t stand without a being. That derivation is the load-bearing argument for the biconditional; what follows is characterization of Φ’s further texture, not additional derivation. The same persistence is available as first-person datum, and three further observations sharpen what kind of host Φ is.

*Persistence hosts change.* A thought held in attention spans changes that proceed around it: the room’s air exchanging, the page’s light scattering, the body’s blood circulating. The thought spans the changes; the changes don’t erase it. This doesn’t require an unchanged host. A process may alter its own bearer while enough continuity remains to carry the process and its effects. Substantiality is the bearing continuity through which change occurs, not an invariant configuration that change can never affect.

*Persistence admits hold-and-proceed.* Breath suspended, heartbeat continuing, neural firing continuing, manuscript resting on the desk: one change-process is held while sibling processes proceed at their own rates. The temporal order of change isn’t totally serial. There is no master succession running the world with everything else as derived sub-steps. Substantiality is the condition under which many change-processes can run concurrently and one can be suspended without arresting the others.

*Persistence is grain-independent: it admits processes at different temporal grains.* A held thought spanning an interval and blinks occurring periodically across the same interval are persistence-bearing processes within the same Substantiality. The observation isn’t that the cadences are mathematically incommensurable, but that no master cadence is given in the data as constitutively fixing both. Their temporal relation is contingent; their co-occurrence within one persistence-bearing structure is the point. Substantiality is the condition under which processes at different grains are co-hosted at all.

*What the supplement adds.* The realizer lines establish Φ↔(T∧S); these three observations characterize what Substantiality further is. Substantiality is hosting, plural, and grain-independent: a host that change operates within rather than upon, a manifold that admits concurrent suspension, a condition that doesn’t impose a master cadence on what it hosts. §3.3.1 catches the denier of change at the token level; the supplement characterizes what the catch is catching the denier inside of. The denial is hosted, runs alongside sibling processes, and proceeds at a cadence the denier did not select.

*Where the three triconditionals stand.* Each pivot has been worked in both directions: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ) in §2.6.2, S ↔ (T ∧ Φ) in §2.6.3, Φ ↔ (T ∧ S) here—each under the Operative-Role Bridge. T doing succession-work requires differentiated positions and a bearer; S doing medium-work requires an ordered crossing and an occupier; Φ doing transition-work requires an ordered interval and differentiated states. Abstract order, static geometry, and non-operating bearers remain outside the antecedent. Within the target domain, operative instantiation of any one Condition reveals the other two as internal requirements rather than external correlates.

*Convergence.* Three Conditions, three triconditionals, and one structure read through all three. What that structure amounts to (as one fact rather than three) is what follows.

**[Lemma]**

**Persistence’s Realizers** · *Lemma*

Persistent bearing is biconditional with directed succession and relational extension: Φ ↔ (T ∧ S). The two halves carry different prices and are paid separately. The T↔Φ half is the pivot’s own work, four lines running two in each direction, each refuting a distinct deflationary mimic. The S half is not derived from persistence as such and is carried on its own terms.

**Depends on:** Cross-Interval Persistence (§2.4.8); Operative-Role Bridge (§2.6.1)
**Feeds into:** Mutual Containment (§2.6.5 Mutual Containment)

*Tested against.* Eliminativism and illusionism, which oppose the identity line by denying persistence (§9.2); Sider’s stage theory, which reads persistence as concatenation of stages rather than endurance (§8.3.2); bundle theory and tropes, on whether there is a persistent subject beyond the bundle (§8.3.3); idealism, which accepts persistence but reads it as mental rather than as Substantiality (§9.5); Russellian monism, which posits intrinsic categorical natures behind the persistence-medium (§9.3); and the Humean denial of necessary connection, pressing at the persistence-vehicle for causal transmission (§8.2.2).

### 2.6.5 Mutual Containment
The three pivot derivations of §2.6.2–2.6.4 are now in hand, and they compress into a single result:

**[Corollary]**

**Mutual Containment** · *Corollary*

Under the Operative-Role Bridge, the three relations establish that T, S, and Φ are not detachable in a concrete change-realizer. The co-requirement is earned locally in the pivots: T’s operative succession requires differentiated positions and a bearer; S’s operation as a crossable medium requires an ordered crossing and an occupier; Φ’s operative persistence requires an ordered interval and differentiated states. Each conclusion predicates the other Conditions of the same realizer in which the first is doing its characteristic work. The result is a domain-indexed necessary co-requirement, not analytic containment among the thin definitions and not a field-to-local transfer.

**Depends on:** Operative-Role Bridge; Succession’s, Extension’s, and Persistence (§2.6.4)’s Two Conditions

The medium at issue is the broad sense fixed at §2.4.8, and the independent criteria are those of §1.4.

The entailment claimed isn’t that T, S, and Φ happen to co-occur with metaphysical necessity, as though they were three independent features that every possible world happens to contain. It is the intersection of what the three pivot derivations actually established: T↔(S∧Φ) at §2.6.2, S↔(T∧Φ) at §2.6.3, and Φ↔(T∧S) at §2.6.4. Each pivot supplies one bilateral entailment in the same realizer at its stated price: the occupancy, traversal, ordering, and bearing premises carry the weight. Countermodels outside the domain are conceded and routed. The convergent lines of §§2.6.2–2.6.4 are derivations, not inductive observations of co-occurrence, and they are one same-realizer move read from three pivots, not three independent arguments that happen to compose.

The distinction matters: field-level co-occurrence alone would leave the Conditions internally unrelated. The earned co-requirement makes their separation fail when any one is operative in a concrete change-realizer. Logical orders, static geometries, abstract endurers, and a concrete spatial configuration considered at an instant may instantiate thin or static counterparts without satisfying that antecedent. They are therefore not counterexamples to the domain-indexed theorem, and the theorem is not evidence against their reality.

A causal power with no position has nothing to act on and nothing it acts from; a position with no persistence is no one’s position, because nothing is there long enough to be somewhere; persistence with no succession is a state that never transitions: all of the subject, at once, nothing changed. Each role, taken by itself, is trying to describe something only the other two make describable. Mutual definitional containment, stripped of its vocabulary, is the claim that a thing is the three roles working at once, or it is nothing at all.

What happens if one Condition is removed **from a proposed change-realizer**? Remove Substantiality and ask what bears the change: succession indexes unrelated entries and extension contains no continuing process. Remove Spatiality and the proposal loses the differentiated operative positions across which the transition is meant to run. Remove Temporality and it leaves a snapshot with no before or after. Each removal destroys the alleged change-realizer. It does not follow from this local test alone that every isolated abstract or static structure collapses; field-level necessity is the separate theorem of §2.5, and absolute structural absence is tested at §2.7.

*The physics-register line.* The mutual entailment also receives confirmation from inside physics. Noether established that every continuous symmetry of a physical system corresponds to a conservation law (1918): symmetry in Temporality yields energy conservation, symmetry in Spatiality yields momentum conservation. Each conservation law is a statement about what persists across transformation: Φ, named in the vocabulary of physics. Within Lagrangian dynamics, T and S as continuous symmetries entail Φ as a conservation consequence. The line is confirmation rather than independent derivation: it presupposes the action principle and the Lagrangian framework that licenses the symmetry-to-conservation move, both of which are results within physical theory rather than premises of the present argument. The biconditional is derived from inside logic (the three logical steps establishing mutual entailment); Noether confirms it from inside physics. The conservation line is developed at full length at §4.5.3.

Every step of any derivation moves from one state to the next, an ordering that can’t be reversed without losing the argument. Every proposition occupies a position the preceding one didn’t, a distinction inference requires to advance. Across those steps something must persist, a medium that holds derivation taut across all three coordinates. Inference doesn’t describe the Triconditional Cross-Entailment; it instantiates it. A directed succession of thoughts, through a manifold of distinct propositions, sustained by a medium that persists from premise to conclusion, isn’t a description of the structure but an instance of it.

One structural fact, read from three directions. The next section delivers it as the Modal Identity, the biconditional that combines the Structural Requirement (§2.4.5–2.4.9) and the converse (§2.4.10). The Modal Identity and the Ontological Identity (§2.6.6, 2.6.8) don’t add a new structure on top of that result; they name the one this derivation has already forced.

*Tested against.* The objections to the Mutual Containment claim (the denial that T, S, and Φ are independently separable) are engaged in Chapters 7–9: bundle theory and tropes, which deny compositional unity (§8.3.3), mereological nihilism, which denies that any joint instantiation runs deeper than the simples (§8.3.4), Sider’s structuralism (§7.2.8), and structural realism (§9.10).

### 2.6.6 Modal Identity
The next three sections read the same T∧S∧Φ structure from three sides:

| Reading | Question answered | Direct result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Modal** (§2.6.6) | What does Change-possibility require? | □(◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ) |
| **Nomological** (§2.6.7) | How do the Conditions implicate one another when operative in a concrete change-realizer? | T↔(S∧Φ), S↔(T∧Φ), Φ↔(T∧S), domain-indexed by the Operative-Role Bridge |
| **Ontological** (§2.6.8) | What does being in Nature consist in? | T∧S∧Φ in operation |

The Modal Identity begins from the side of possibility: the possibility of change points at the triconditional structure.

The two directions carry Change under one structural description, as fixed at §1.3 and made explicit at §2.4.10: ordered succession between genuinely distinct states with cross-interval bearing. Left to right, actual tokens of Change expose those requirements. Right to left, their joint instantiation cannot remain a succession in which no state ever differs, so Change is possible. Every downstream use of the biconditional inherits that single referent.

There remains an evidential asymmetry, but no semantic one. The forward route starts from a reflective token and an independent movement token; the converse starts from the Conditions. Reflection and movement distinguish the witnesses, not Change itself. Nor are Change’s structural requirements additional to Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality: ordered phases are Temporality, positional distinction is Spatiality, and cross-interval bearing is Substantiality. The two arguments approach one content from opposite sides, so the biconditional does not trade a feature-rich Change for a thinner successor relation.

The Modal Identity concerns the full Conditions where they function as a genuine change-realizer. Its modal force isn’t an unrestricted claim that every abstract order, geometry, or bearer instantiates all three. It is the claim that any configuration R has the capacity to admit as a change-realizer instantiates the mutually implicating T, S, and Φ structure, and that the canonical derivation establishes those Conditions as constitutive of Range(R). The Modal Identity reads the joint structural result from the side of change-possibility rather than reducing it to a feature of modal vocabulary.

The ladder has three rungs. The forward conditional, together with □◇C, proves □(T∧S∧Φ) (§2.3; §2.4.5–2.4.9). The independently argued converse at §2.4.10 adds the earned biconditional and forecloses frozen structure. The no-surplus argument adds identity: one structural fact under two descriptions. Chapter 3 inherits these results rather than re-deriving them (§3.4).

The distinction matters because the bare formula □(◇C ↔ (T∧S∧Φ)) could be obtained merely by pairing two necessary truths—just as either could be paired with the Pythagorean theorem. That free co-extension proves no identity. Here the converse is separately earned through Moment-Individuation, and the identity claim is hyperintensional: if neither side carries individuating content the other lacks, there is no surplus by which two facts could be told apart. A reader resisting that last step retains the biconditional and every result that spends it, but not the one-fact ontology fixed by the No-Surplus Criterion at §2.6.9.

That identity is resolution-bound. It concerns the full change-realizing Conditions, not thin abstract analogues of order, difference, or bearing. At that resolution, the specifications close in both directions: Temporality is ordered succession, Spatiality relational extension, and Substantiality cross-interval bearing; Change is succession between distinct states borne across the interval. The role-definitions of §1.3–1.4 and the converse, not an appeal to conceivability, establish the foreclosure. The difficulty of thinking either side without the other illustrates the identity but does not ground it.

This isn’t Kripke’s water-and-H₂O identity. It shares the analytic-identity form Kripke himself distinguishes from mere necessary biconditional, but operates at the structural level where the surface/essence seam he exploits doesn’t open. The contrast is handled directly at §7.1.1 and §7.1.2. Here it suffices that the biconditional doesn’t hold because two independent facts require each other. It holds because the independence was never there.

The identity reading is pressed by the B-theoretic block. A four-dimensional manifold in which all events stand in tenseless earlier-than relations has, on the standard analytic reading, T (the temporal ordering), S (the spatial extension), and Φ (whatever fills it) all instantiated, yet nothing on the picture succeeds, nothing yields, nothing carries forward. Every event is just there.

The B-theorist will press: this is structure without change-as-becoming. The Conditions and change-possibility, on this scenario, come apart at exactly the seam the identity reading was supposed to seal.

The full engagement belongs to §8.1.4, where the perspectival-versus-structural-becoming distinction is taken up in full along with the further questions (the phenomenology of becoming, presentism-versus-eternalism, and growing-block alternatives); here only the narrower point needs to land for the Modal Identity—that tenseless ordering meets the specification of Temporality at §1.4.

Does tenseless ordering count as Temporality in the sense the Conditions invoke? That is the whole of the pressure, and the structural answer is yes.

Temporality as defined at §1.4 and derived at §2.4.6 is asymmetric, transitive ordering of states. The B-theoretic ordering relation is exactly that, viewed from outside the block rather than from within it. The richer features the A-theorist misses—passage and direction as causal weight—belong to the realization tier engaged at §8.1.4 and §4.2, and aren’t part of what the Conditions invoke here. From no point inside the block does succession fail to obtain; from every point, the ordering is precisely the before-and-after the Conditions name.

What the B-theorist’s static description subtracts is the perspective from within (the experience of becoming), and the experience of becoming isn’t what the Conditions consist in. The Conditions are the structural shape that makes both the within-perspective and the without-perspective coherent descriptions of the same Nature.

Take the block reading and the identity holds: structure *is* what change-possibility *consists in*, viewed from outside; change-possibility *is* what structure does, viewed from inside. The B-theorist who rejects change-as-becoming hasn’t separated the Conditions from change-possibility; they have specified change-possibility at the level the block describes. The identity survives the deflation.

Fine’s {Socrates}/Socrates asymmetry requires two items with distinct essential profiles: the set carries an essential tie the member lacks. Between the full Conditions and change-possibility, every specification of either supplies the other, leaving no corresponding individuating surplus. The warrant is that absence of surplus, not their holding across the same worlds.

The formal vocabulary for this kind of identity is available in the contemporary grounding and essence literature. Schaffer establishes grounding as a primitive ontological relation distinct from supervenience and reduction (2009); Rosen (2015) and Correia and Skiles (2019) develop the formal tools for claims of the shape *x and y are the same fact described at different levels*.

The Modal Identity is one such claim. The possibility of change and the structural Conditions aren’t grounded in each other; grounding asymmetry would require the two entities that aren’t here. They are the same structural requirement under two descriptions. This is closer to what Correia and Skiles call generic identity than to standard grounding: one fact, two readings, no residue on either side.

Nor do the modal and structural formulations supply independently graspable Fregean senses. To grasp change-possibility at this resolution is to grasp directed succession among distinct persisting states; to grasp that full structure is to grasp the availability of transition. The two readings approach one content from opposite sides.

**[Theorem]**

**Modal Identity** · *Theorem*

Nature read from the side of possibility: within the domain of full change-realizing structure, the possibility of change and the joint Conditions are one structural fact under two readings. □(◇C ↔ (T∧S∧Φ)), with the biconditional ranging over full Condition-instantiation rather than thin abstract analogues. (The necessitation in the Modal Identity is real / metaphysical: necessity in the modal structure, not closure of primary conceivability or epistemic openness. The two-dimensional question whether the biconditional remains primarily conceivable as false even where the secondary structural identity holds is engaged at §7.1.2.)

The Modal Identity licenses a further field-level reading: if the triconditional structure and change-possibility are one fact, then what are traditionally termed possible worlds are configurations evaluated within one necessary natural ground, not rival modal domains. The *Reality–Nature Identity* at §2.8 carries that reading to maximal-totality scope; Convergence later inherits and diagnoses that reading rather than establishing it afresh (§3.4). This doesn’t decide whether modal plurality is wholly combinatorial; candidate semantics remain part of the Chapter 7 engagement.

*Necessity without collapse.* The Modal Identity fixes the stage, not the play: □◇C concerns the modal status of a capacity, not the necessity of any actuality. Reality necessarily retains the capacity for Change, while the modal status of any scene, law-pattern, or physical realization requires independent evidence (§2.9.4). Necessary structure therefore does not entail necessary history.

The capacity has no unstructured existence behind the Conditions. Before and after are its temporal articulation; genuinely distinct positions its spatial articulation; cross-interval bearing its substantial articulation. By the Modal Identity, Reality’s capacity for Change is not something T, S, and Φ possess but what they are when read from the side of possibility. The idiom adds no ontology and fixes no particular expression. Chapter 4 elaborates the physical confirmations of that structure.

*Tested against.* Modal collapse, the necessity-without-collapse worry the Modal Identity theorem draws (§8.2.5); alternative structuralist readings of the identity claim, from Sider’s structuralism (§7.2.8) and structural realism (§9.10); and the rival frozen-structure-as-mathematical-universe candidate the identity reading forecloses, pressed by Tegmark (§9.9) and the changeless-ground picture (§10.2.3).

The Modal Identity is the first of three readings of the Triconditional Identity (§2.6.10).

### 2.6.7 Triconditional Cross-Entailment
The realizer move was worked three times at §2.6.2–2.6.4, each pivoting on a different term, and gathered at §2.6.5. Its exact form matters. Each Condition has an independent modal-core criterion fixed at §1.4, and none of those thin criteria analytically contains the other two. The additional Operative-Role Bridge asks what must be realized when the criterion does concrete work. The pivots answer: T-at-work requires differentiated positions and a bearer; S-at-work in a change-realizer requires an ordered crossing and an occupier; Φ-at-work requires an ordered interval and differentiated states. One **operative** Condition in, three Conditions in the same realizer out—by an explicit bridge plus the pivot derivations, not by definition. Abstract orders, static geometries, and abstract bearers may satisfy thin analogues without satisfying the operative antecedent; they are outside this theorem without being declared unreal.

Pure mathematical abstraction isn’t a counterexample to the restricted theorem. A Kuratowski ordered pair, ⟨a, b⟩ := {{a}, {a, b}}, can instantiate abstract ordering and distinctness without temporal succession, spatial extension, or causal persistence. The theorem grants that point because a pure ordered pair isn’t a realizer of genuine change.

The deflationary move becomes relevant only when the ordered pair is offered as a complete account of an actual succession. Then an interpretation must identify its elements as states, their order as a before-and-after, and their connection as what makes the sequence one change rather than two unrelated entries. Those additional realizer conditions—not the set-theoretic pair by itself—bring the restricted T, S, and Φ domain into view.

Run the same-realizer route through each Condition in turn. From T: a real ordered succession is one whose positions differ in their occupying states, whose order is borne as one succession rather than two entries. The differentiated positions instantiate S in that succession, and their bearing as stages of one order instantiates Φ there (§2.6.2). A succession without real distinction between its states isn’t a thinner T; it fails the individuation its own order requires.

From S: concrete extension carries crossability-in-principle on its independent criterion (§1.4.2). A crossing is ordered from one position to another and is borne by what occupies and traverses the interval, so T and Φ are instantiated in the same extended medium (§2.6.3). Pure geometry, which owes nobody occupants or crossings, doesn’t meet the criterion and isn’t in the theorem’s subject matter.

From Φ: bearing is bearing across an ordered interval of differentiated states. The order instantiates T and the articulated interval instantiates S in the same persistence-bearing realizer (§2.6.4). A bearer with nothing to persist through isn’t a reduced Φ; it fails the role’s own specification.

Within any structure that realizes genuine change, the three Conditions therefore form one realizer complex rather than three detachable ingredients—not because ‘realizer’ was defined as the three together, but because each Condition, on its own criterion, requires the other two in the same bearer, medium, or succession. The cross-entailment isn’t a theorem about arbitrary abstract structures. It is a theorem about full Condition-instantiation on the independent §1.4 criteria: remove any role and what remains no longer meets its own specification, let alone realizes change.

The three axes converge on one structural fact, and the cross-entailment can now be stated.

**[Theorem]**

**Triconditional Cross-Entailment** · *Theorem*

Nature read from the cross-entailment among the three operative roles: when Temporality, Spatiality, or Substantiality does its characteristic work in a concrete change-realizer, the Operative-Role Bridge and the succession, extension, and persistence pivots co-instantiate the other two in that same realizer. The roles are mutually implicating there without being reducible to one another. Formally, for any realizer g in the operative domain: T(g) ↔ (S(g)∧Φ(g)), S(g) ↔ (T(g)∧Φ(g)), Φ(g) ↔ (T(g)∧S(g)). No unrestricted biconditional among thin abstract predicates is claimed.

**Depends on:** Operative-Role Bridge; Mutual Containment

Conversation illustrates rather than establishes the result. An exchange requires temporal direction, distinct positions of address and uptake, and persistence of the participants across turns. Remove any one and what remains is not a simpler conversation but no conversation: between substances, across space, through time. The example stays within the theorem’s operative domain; an abstract order, geometry, bearer, or static extension outside a change-realizer does not trigger the entailment.

One consequence carries further, since the argument of §3.1.5 (Actuality Extends to the Ground) leans on it: the cross-entailment licenses not only that the three Conditions stand or fall together, but that anything in which even one of them is *actually present* thereby instantiates all three. Reaching the ground requires one further premise, stated rather than folded into that theorem.

**[Premise]**

**State–Realizer Instantiation** · *Constitutive Premise*

If a structural feature is actually instantiated in a concrete state, and that state is a state of realizer g, then the feature is instantiated by g in that state. This does not transfer represented content: a state that represents F need not instantiate F in its own occurrence. The premise applies only where F structures the state itself rather than what the state is about.

Apply that premise to the same-realizer theorem just earned. An actually instantiated Condition carries the other two in its state; if that state is a state of its ground, the joint structure is the ground’s own. That composition yields the following corollary.

**[Corollary]**

**Constitutive Instantiation** · *Corollary*

Where one of the Conditions is **operatively present in an experiencing**—doing temporal, spatial, or bearing work rather than merely represented in content—the Operative-Role Bridge and Triconditional Cross-Entailment co-instantiate all three in that experiencing. Where the experiencing is a state its ground is in, State–Realizer Instantiation carries that structure to the ground itself. Mere actuality of a thin Condition-predicate does not trigger this corollary.

**Depends on:** Operative-Role Bridge; Triconditional Cross-Entailment (§2.6.7); State–Realizer Instantiation

The derivation from the cross-entailment to the ground runs in five steps:

**[Argument]**

**Triconditional Cross-Entailment** · *The Ground’s Instantiation*

1. Three things must be kept apart: the representation itself, its represented content, and the instantiation of what is represented. To instantiate a structural feature F is for F to be actually present; to encode F is to bear a representation whose content is F while F itself is absent. A two-dimensional engine encodes three-dimensional space without occupying it: the distinction is what the result turns on, and it is this three-way form that the book uses wherever representing is contrasted with instantiating (*The representation distinction*)

2. The operative instantiation of any one Condition-feature in that experiencing carries the conjunction of the other two with it under the Operative-Role Bridge (*Triconditional Cross-Entailment*)

3. An experience in which the Conditions are actually present is a state its ground is in, not a content it merely hosts and not a free-floating fact; State–Realizer Instantiation therefore makes the instantiation the ground’s own rather than a structure the ground merely represents.

4. ∴ A ground of actually-structured experience instantiates T, S, and Φ. One that merely encoded them could underwrite a representation of such experience, but not an experience in which the structure is actually present, and it is the latter that The Witness and Its Ground (§3.1.5) requires.

*Scope.* Whether weak or strong, emergence may relocate where a feature is first instantiated; it cannot convert actual instantiation into mere encoding. Once the feature is actually present, step 2 fires.

*The encoding dilemma.* A critic may deny that experience is a state its ground is in and say the ground merely encodes the experienced structure. The state horn uses State–Realizer Instantiation. The encoding horn reaches the same ground directly: an encoding that sustains a live experience is a tokened process whose steps are ordered (T), whose vehicle-elements occupy differentiated operative positions (S), and whose medium bears the token across those steps (Φ). A game engine may encode a third dimension without instantiating it, but its live rendering still runs frame by frame, across distinct vehicle-elements, in a persisting substrate. The represented feature can be absent; the Conditions carrying the representation cannot.

The limit is exact. A frozen, never-read encoding need not succeed in time, so the line covers grounds of *actual, ongoing* experience, not untokened abstractions. It requires neither a grounding-priority premise nor a field-to-local inference: the state horn uses the named premise, while the encoding horn uses the same-realizer criteria of §§2.6.2–2.6.4.

**[Proposition]**

**The Encoding Dilemma** · *Proposition*

Take any candidate ground of an actually structured experience. Either the experience is an actual state of that ground, in which case State–Realizer Instantiation carries its structure to the ground, or the ground merely encodes the structure attributed to the experience. An encoding that grounds a live experience is a tokened activity: its processing steps instantiate T, its differentiated vehicle-elements instantiate S, and its medium bearing the token across those steps instantiates Φ in that same ground. Either horn therefore delivers a ground instantiating all three Conditions. Its limit is the processing step, which restricts it to grounds of *actual, ongoing* experience; a frozen, never-read encoding is not covered.

**Depends on:** the encoding/instantiation fork; State–Realizer Instantiation; the same-realizer criteria of §§2.6.2–2.6.4

The operative restriction in the proposition prevents thin labels from being promoted into the Conditions.

At the level of logic, the same fact: temporal logic, spatial logic, and substantial logic aren’t three logics in coordination but one logic read along three axes: the metalogical architecture is developed at §2.11.

The cross-entailment the Triconditional Cross-Entailment names structurally is shared logical form. To be one of T, S, Φ is already to share the logical aspect the other two are: what reads as succession from one axis, as distinction from another, as carrying-through from the third, *is* the same logic showing its three faces.

A consequence follows that governs the rest of the argument. A coordinate doesn’t have an essence that it then expresses. It essentially expresses. What the coordinate does viewed as static property is its essence; what the coordinate does viewed as activity is its expression: the same structural fact from two directions. Neither direction reaches something the other misses.

Essence without expression is a coordinate without axes: the phrase retains its grammar but has lost its referent. The bridge to the essence / expression collapse runs through the realizer move of §2.6.1: what makes a structural feature a structural feature, rather than a labeled placeholder, is its operativity within the structure it figures in.

A coordinate that has no axes to figure in is a label, not a coordinate; an essence that has no expression to be the essence *of* is a name, not an essence.

At the structural level the operativity is constitutive of the feature: the essence doesn’t stand behind the expression as a further determinable, because the expression *is* what the essence consists in. There is no hidden what-it-is behind the expressing, because the expressing is the what-it-is.

This is what makes the severances of Chapter 11 total rather than partial: negating what the Conditions do isn’t stripping away an outer layer to reveal a residual essence beneath. It is negating the essence itself.

*Tested against.* The Humean denial of necessary connection between distinct existences, pressing directly at the cross-entailment site (§8.2.2); conventionalism about laws at §7.1.4; Quine’s denial of the analytic–essential distinction the cross-entailment relies on at §7.1.3; and Sider’s structuralism on lawlike structure at §7.2.8.

### 2.6.8 Ontological Identity
The Ontological Identity reads the same structure from the side of being: T∧S∧Φ as what being in Nature consists in. Its scope is exactly that—beings within the realizer-level structure of genuine change. It doesn’t assert here that every possible being is a change-participant; abstracta, atemporal entities, and non-spatial minds are candidate outsiders whose cases are argued, not presupposed closed: abstracta under Mathematical Platonism (§8.1.5), non-spatial minds under Idealism (§9.5), and atemporal grounding under the changeless-ground treatment (§10.2.3, with §10.2.1 where simplicity carries the weight). Chapter 3 tests the same candidates at role level only (§3.1.4), and the field-level result is at §2.9.6. Within its scope, no gap opens at the structural level between how a being presents and what it consists in, because the Conditions aren’t surface features with a hidden essence but the being’s essence itself. The facthood line at Something Must Be (§2.4.4) reaches the same constitutive conclusion from the side of what any concrete, tensed state of affairs requires, at that section’s stated scope.

A being isn’t a substrate on which T, S, and Φ are imposed from outside. A being is something that persists (Φ), distinct from other things (S), across transition (T). A Φ that doesn’t persist across any S or T is no being. An S that doesn’t separate any Φs across any T isn’t a space. A T that doesn’t host any Φ succeeding across any S isn’t a time. The three Conditions aren’t a set of requirements beings meet. The three Conditions *are* what *being* *consists in*.

This yields the Ontological Identity.

**[Theorem]**

**Ontological Identity** · *Theorem*

Nature read from the side of being: to be in Nature is to instantiate Time, Space, and Substance (T∧S∧Φ). Not to match T, S, and Φ as a necessary condition; to be T, S, and Φ in operation as a being. What has being in Nature is T, S, and Φ in operation; what T, S, and Φ are in operation, has being. No residue on either side.

Ontic Structural Realism provides the contemporary philosophical ally. Ladyman et al. argue that fundamental physics describes relational and structural features rather than intrinsic natures (2007): that the ontology physics delivers is structure, not substance-in-the-classical-sense. French develops the same position for quantum mechanics (2014).

The Ontological Identity isn’t Ontic Structural Realism, but it is continuous with it: where Ontic Structural Realism is an interpretive thesis about what physics describes, the Ontological Identity is a modal thesis about what any being must be. The structural realist, asked what fundamental reality consists in, answers with the relational fabric physics specifies; the present account answers with T, S, and Φ as the minimal structural conditions any being must instantiate. The two positions converge on the same fact from opposite directions: physics ends up with relational organization because relational organization is what there was to be.

A theist, idealist, or dual-aspect realist can keep their vocabulary: insofar as what they propose is a being *in Nature*—a participant in the change-hosting structure—it instantiates T∧S∧Φ, and instantiating T∧S∧Φ is what being in Nature means here. Whether their candidate can stand *outside* Nature is the live question, and the Ontological Identity theorem doesn’t settle it by definition: the atemporal ground is put under load at §2.9.6 and again at §10.2–10.3, the Platonist at §8.1.5, the non-spatial mind at §9.5. Within Nature, the being-question isn’t a substrate choice to be disputed; it is the structural shape of any being at all. The Modal Identity, the Triconditional Cross-Entailment, and the Ontological Identity converge at the *Triconditional Identity* in §2.6.10: three readings, one Nature, under three logical lenses; the thesis is drawn at §2.9.3.

*Tested against.* Chapters 8 and 9 engage the being-side reading of the Ontological Identity theorem: that T∧S∧Φ is what being in Nature consists in. Idealism makes being a mode of mind rather than structure (§9.5), Russellian monism posits intrinsic categorical natures behind the relational fabric (§9.3), bundle theory and tropes read being as bundle rather than Φ-in-operation (§8.3.3), and mereological nihilism denies the composites the being-reading addresses (§8.3.4); structural realism agrees on structural priority but diverges on what fundamental reality consists in (§9.10). The classical-theist reply (that God is being itself, held exempt from instantiating T∧S∧Φ rather than counted as a being that instantiates it) is taken up under divine simplicity, on which God is identical with subsistent existence rather than a being that has it (§10.2.1), Neoplatonism and the One held to be beyond being (§10.3.2), and the via negativa, which withholds positive structural predication of God (§10.2.2).

### 2.6.9 Triunity of Nature
The modal, nomological, and ontological readings are now in hand. Do they pick out three facts, or one?

The Triconditions are the same in each. The Temporality that appears in the Modal Identity (◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ) is the same Temporality that appears in the Triconditional Cross-Entailment and the same Temporality the Ontological Identity names as the being-condition of anything within its stated scope.

No equivocation runs across the three uses: each letter names the same Condition—though not everywhere at the same resolution, since the realizer lines of §§2.6.2–.4 run at the realization tier while the Modal Identity spends only T’s modal core (§2.4). Same Condition, read at two depths, isn’t equivocation; it would become equivocation only if the deeper reading were allowed to discharge a step the theorem states at the shallower one.

The co-extension established across §2.6 is the co-extension of these Conditions, not of three different trios of Conditions that happen to share notation.

*Co-extension isn’t what makes them one, and the point generalizes across the family.* The three readings are necessarily co-extensive, and by itself that settles nothing at all. Each of T, S, Φ, and ◇C has already been established as necessary, and necessary truths are necessarily co-extensive with one another whatever their subject matter; a demonstration that the three readings never come apart is therefore available without any of them having the least thing to do with the others.

This isn’t a weakness peculiar to the Triunity. It runs through the whole family: the Modal Identity (§2.6.6), the Triconditional Cross-Entailment (§2.6.7), the Ontological Identity (§2.6.8). Each states in biconditional notation a claim whose content isn’t modal covariation.

What the arguments in those sections establish is that specifying either side already specifies the other, and that nothing remains over on either side once it has: the no-residue claims made in the statement that follows and argued at length at §2.6.6. Those are hyperintensional claims. The biconditionals are their shadow, not their content.

Two things follow, and both favor the argument rather than costing it. First, the modal notation *understates* these results: what is claimed is stronger than necessary equivalence, not weaker, and a reader who reads only the operators will have read past the theorem rather than into it. Second, the shape of any refutation is fixed in advance. An opponent can’t separate the readings by exhibiting a world in which one holds and another fails, because on the book’s own commitments no such world is available for any pair of necessary truths, including pairs with nothing whatever to do with each other. The only live attack is against the no-surplus claim: to show that one side carries individuating content the other lacks. That is the argument made at §2.6.6, and the one a critic has to engage.

**[Principle]**

**No-Surplus Criterion** · *Principle*

Where both relata of a claimed identity have already been established as necessary, their modal co-extension is uninformative. It follows from the necessity of each, it holds between any two necessary truths whatever, and it therefore distinguishes nothing.

The content of an identity claim between such relata is exhausted by the absence of individuating content on either side: that specifying either already specifies the other, with nothing left over to mark them as two.

Two consequences follow. The biconditional notation *understates* such a result rather than overstating it, so a reader who reads only the operators has read past the claim. And a refutation must target the no-surplus claim directly; exhibiting a world in which the two sides come apart is unavailable in principle rather than merely difficult.

The criterion governs the identity family across §2.6.6–2.6.10. It is stated here because §2.6.9 is where the three readings are collected, but it governs each of them separately, and §2.6.6 is its principal worked instance. It is a criterion for reading results of this shape, not a further result about Reality: it adds no commitment the identity arguments didn’t already carry, and spends nothing beyond the necessity of the relata that §§2.3 and 2.5 establish.

*The three layers.* What the three differ in isn’t the three Conditions but the layer. The Ontological Identity takes the three Conditions at the being layer: T, S, and Φ *are* what a being within the change-realizing structure *consists in*, what any concrete change-realizer is, across distance, through time. The Triconditional Cross-Entailment takes them at the lawful-structure layer: any regularity is a regularity in what persists (Φ), across distinction (S), through succession (T)—the three Conditions in lawful operation. The Modal Identity takes them at the logical layer: what can be the case is what can host T, S, and Φ together—the three Conditions in modal form. Three layers, the same three conditions.

The reduction runs from the being layer up. A concrete change-realizer is a being acting across distance through time: it is Φ distinguished in S and succeeding in T. That isn't a description of a concrete change-realizer; it *is* what being such a realizer *consists in*. There is no residue after the three Conditions specify the being: no further constituent that makes it a concrete change-realizer in some way the three Conditions didn’t capture. The Ontological Identity is the claim that being a concrete change-realizer and instantiating T∧S∧Φ *are* the same fact, not two facts that match.

*Tested against.* Whether the thin Conditions granted to an atemporal ground at §2.6.3—mere priority, distinctness, and dependence—descend to the loaded reading of directional succession and causal carrying is **not** settled in-chapter. The limit should be read off §2.9.7 as that section states it rather than as a binary.

The Exclusivity of Nature theorem is relative to that grounding role and closes two horns on owned Chapter-2 machinery: the Triconditional Cross-Entailment (§2.6.7) and the Incoherence of ∅ (§2.7.2). A candidate that instantiates T, S, and Φ in the loaded sense is structure under another description; a candidate that withdraws every thin content by which it differs, stands, orders, or sources is a variant of the Null State.

What it expressly doesn’t close is the third position: a ground retaining thin or analogical content while denying the loaded Conditions isn’t thereby the Null State, and carries a contact burden forward instead of being refuted in Chapter 2. Named formulations are tested at §10.2.1 (Divine Simplicity), §10.3.2 (Neoplatonism), and §10.2.2 (The Via Negativa).

The next reduction follows at the level of lawful structure. A law of nature constrains what concrete change-realizers do; on a regularity account, it is described through patterns in that activity, while governing and primitivist accounts deny that laws reduce to regularities. Either way, its instances involve distinguishable states (S) of beings or realizers (Φ) across transitions or dependency-order (T). Physics isn't a substrate beside the beings it describes: the nomological reading describes the lawful organization of the same structural field the ontological reading describes from the side of being. The Triconditional Cross-Entailment is the Ontological Identity read through law, not a commitment to a regularity theory of laws.

*The logical layer.* The final step reaches the logical layer, and here the claim must be stated carefully. ◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ doesn’t add possibility to the three Conditions as a further property; it says the possibility of change and the instantiation of the three Conditions are necessarily co-extensive, on the earned biconditional (§2.4.10).

Possibility isn’t thereby a third domain floating free: what must hold for change to be possible is the same structure the other two readings describe. Whether that necessary co-extension amounts to the Modal Identity *being* the Ontological Identity described as possibility—one fact—or to two necessarily co-grounded facts about one structure is exactly what §2.6.10’s identity criterion must decide. The Triunity banks the co-grounding and leaves the naming to the theorem that owns it.

*Taking stock.* The three readings are readings of one Nature: the *Triunity of Nature*. The claim, stated at its earned strength, is a sameness of ground, not yet a numerical identity of facts. What makes ◇C true, what any lawful regularity holds of, and what any being in Nature consists in is the same structural complex—the three Conditions—approached from possibility, from law, and from being.

Shared vocabulary alone wouldn’t license even this much. What licenses it is that each reading was derived from the same theorems about the same structure (§2.4, 2.6.5–2.6.8), not merely described with the same letters. Whether the three readings name one fact or three necessarily co-grounded facts about one structure is a further question requiring an identity criterion stronger than co-grounding; that criterion is the business of §2.6.10, and this section doesn’t presuppose its answer.

The compression here doesn’t mean empirical physics reduces to formal logic; it means the lawful structure physics describes and the modal structure logic names are grounded in the same three conditions. This much is established here for Reality as the change-hosting structural complex: one structure, three lenses.

Whether any candidate necessary ground could stand outside it—particularly the classical theist’s atemporal ground, granted only the thin Conditions at §2.6.3—isn’t assumed here but tested at §2.9.7, and tested rather than closed. The Exclusivity of Nature theorem is relative to one role: for the role of grounding concrete change-realizers, a candidate instantiating the three Conditions in the loaded sense is structure under another description, and one withdrawing every thin content is a variant of ∅. A candidate that keeps thin or analogical content while denying the loaded Conditions is neither, and is carried forward with its burden rather than refuted there.

*No modal collapse.* A modal-collapse worry has to be flagged and disarmed. The Triunity says the three readings converge on one structural ground, while possibility and being remain distinct categories: some things are possible without being actual, and *being possible* isn’t the same property as *being actual*.

The Triunity doesn’t collapse this distinction at the level of individual propositions. It compresses at the level of the three structural Conditions: what makes the possibility of Change true, what any actual change-realizing being is, and what any lawful regularity describes is the same Temporality–Spatiality–Substantiality complex under three logical-categorical readings. These are three readings of the three Conditions, not three properties of one proposition.

The distinction between *being possible* and *being actual* therefore survives at the propositional level. The compression operates between *what makes possibility possible* and *what makes actuality actual*: at that structural level, the answer is the same three conditions, read under modal, nomological, and ontological lenses.

*Two axes.* That shared structure is logical form. These three are logical-categorical readings of one Nature, drawn from the three primary lenses analytic metaphysics has developed: necessity, law, being. The three logics of the Conditions (succession, distinction, carrying-through) and the three logics of the readings (necessity, law, being) are two independent axes of the same logical form.

The two axes carry different warrants, neither a stipulation. On the Condition side, the three enumerate what change requires, and any proposed fourth collapses into one of them or fails the role—the Condition-Individuation of §2.6.11, delivered there as a burden-shift rather than an a priori exclusion. On the readings side, necessity, law, and being are the categorical lenses the tradition has developed, and no candidate fourth reading has resisted resolution into one of the three—a standing challenge rather than a closed proof.

The Conditions and the readings articulate one logical form along two independent axes. Logic isn’t a fourth result alongside the Modal Identity, the Triconditional Cross-Entailment, and the Ontological Identity. It is the perspective from which the three are readings, and the shape they share: what makes their convergence intelligible at all.

A further consequence is available conditionally. *If* Triconditional Identity (§2.6.10) delivers the one-fact reading, the descriptions can’t come apart at the register line: any description in any register already deploys the vocabulary of every register, because the fact it describes is the fact every register describes. On the weaker co-grounding reading, the registers remain three coordinated descriptions of one structure—inseparable in subject matter even if not collapsed as facts.

On the stronger one-fact reading, a physical description *is* already a nomological description *is* already a modal description: not by translation, but because the registers are angles on one fact. On the weaker co-grounding reading, the descriptions remain distinct but can’t come apart in subject matter.

To point at a stone in the physical register is to point at what persists through time (Φ), stands across distance (S), and holds in succession (T). The same pointing, in the modal register, points at what can be the case. On the stronger reading, no phenomenal description, unpacked, turns out not already analytical; no analytical description, grounded, turns out not already phenomenal.

Sellars called the separable given a myth (1956). McDowell pressed the conceptual all the way into experience (1994). The inseparability they noticed at the epistemic level is what the cross-entailments force at the structural level: the registers can’t come apart in subject matter, because each describes the same three conditions.

*Tested against.* The Triunity claim (that the modal, nomological, and ontological readings are one Nature rather than three independent layers) is engaged in Chapters 7–9. Modal collapse is the worry the Triunity must disarm at the propositional level (§8.2.5), Lewis reads modal realism as a three-layer picture (§7.2.3), Sider’s structuralism (§7.2.8) and structural realism press on what the convergence consists in (§9.10), and Quine’s anti-distinction pressure targets the layer-as-reading move (§7.1.3).

What that one fact is, named, is delivered at §2.6.10.

### 2.6.10 Triconditional Identity
Sections §2.6.6–2.6.8 established three claims about the same full change-realizing complex: its necessary biconditional with Change-possibility, its cross-axis entailments, and its being-side articulation. The Triunity of Nature (§2.6.9) established that the three are co-grounded in one T∧S∧Φ structure. This section asks the stronger question deferred there: whether the readings name one fact or three necessarily co-grounded facts.

The answer turns on the no-surplus criterion argued at §2.6.6: at full Condition resolution, two descriptions name one fact when neither carries an individuating surplus over the other. That criterion is stronger than necessary co-extension. A reader who declines it keeps every biconditional and the co-grounding, and forgoes only the one-fact gloss. The name for that stronger reading is the *Triconditional Identity*.

**[Theorem]**

**Triconditional Identity** · *Theorem*

Nature is triconditional in two strengths that must remain visible. Unconditionally at field level, Nature is by definition the jointly necessary complex T∧S∧Φ: N ↔ (T∧S∧Φ), with its necessity earned independently in §2.5. Within concrete change-realizers, the Operative-Role Bridge and the three pivots establish the stronger same-realizer cross-entailments. The Modal and Ontological Identity readings add the no-surplus premise at their stated domains. The resulting biconditionals may be read as generic identity only on that no-surplus argument: N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ), N ↔ □◇C, □(T∧S∧Φ) ↔ □◇C. A reader who declines the operative bridge or the no-surplus step retains the necessary conjunction while forgoing only the corresponding stronger reading.

**Depends on:** Triconditional Necessity; Operative-Role Bridge; No-Surplus Criterion

The necessity predicated of N is earned separately, in the Necessity of Nature theorem at §2.9.6.

These biconditionals don’t all earn identity the same way, and one doesn’t earn it by definition at all. *Nature* was introduced at §1.4.4 and fixed again at the opening of Chapter 2 as the joint structural complex T∧S∧Φ; its necessity is stated at §2.9.6 in the Necessity of Nature theorem. The clause relating Nature to that complex is therefore a strict *definitional* identity: its right-hand side *is* the definiendum of *Nature*, not a predicate that merely happens to be co-extensive with it across all worlds.
