Inputs: §5.3, §5.7, §5.11, §5.14, Institutional Bearer, The Chapter 6 Premises. Used downstream: §6.2–6.12, §6.13, §6.15.

**6.2 Belonging** — The social form of shared exposure: the body in which persons hold each other in being. Inputs: §4.8, §5.2, §5.14. Used downstream: §6.3–6.12, §6.13.

**6.3 Representation** — The structural form of distributed orientation across persons. Inputs: §6.1, §6.2. Used downstream: §6.13.

**6.4 Information** — The conditions under which the reporting channel for felt-state evidence stays open: free speech, freedom of association, freedom from retaliation, and protections against manipulative advertising at coercive scale. Inputs: §5.4, §5.12, §6.1. Used downstream: every following §6 section; §6.13.

**6.5 Environment** — The underlying conditions persons depend on for throughput. Inputs: §4.8, §6.2. Used downstream: §6.6.

**6.6 Agriculture** — Institutional form of throughput-management at scale. Inputs: §6.5, §5.12, §5.13. Used downstream: §6.7.

**6.7 Economy** — Institutional form of distributed exchange among persons; coordination of specialized modal maps. The Legacy identification from §5.9 becomes an intergenerational non-domination constraint: inheritance may secure and widen a descendant’s field, and contributions may outlast contributors, but posthumous vehicles may not convert a deceased holder’s direction into indefinite unanswerable authority over living subjects. Monumental, dynastic, controlling, and generative legacy are distinguished by what persists, who can revise it, and whether the living field widens. Inputs: §5.4, §5.9, §5.12, §6.6. Used downstream: §6.8.

**6.8 Housing** — Institutional form of secure, non-displacing dwelling and the social infrastructure that makes belonging materially available. Inputs: §6.1, §6.2, §6.7. Used downstream: §6.9–§6.13.

**6.9 Education** — Institutional form of transmitting self-modeling capacity across generations; institutional cultivation of modal depth. Inputs: §5.4, §5.10, §5.13, §6.2. Used downstream: §6.13.

**6.10 Healthcare** — Institutional form of maintaining self-modeling capacity. Inputs: §4.8, §5.2. Used downstream: §6.13.

**6.11 Defense** — Institutional form of structural protection from external threat. Inputs: §5.11, §6.1. Used downstream: §6.12.

**6.12 Enforcement** — Institutional form of structural protection from internal threat, derived from §5.6 (Reasoning), §5.11 (Will), and §5.14 (Morality). Inputs: §5.6, §5.11, §5.14, §6.1, §6.11. Used downstream: §6.13.

**6.13 Justice** — Institutional form of restoring conditions persons require when violated. Inputs: §5.11, §5.14, §6.1, §6.12. Used downstream: §6.14.

**6.14 Convergence (Distributed Correction)** — Per-domain convergences consolidated: every domain in §6.1–6.13 traces back to what structural persistence requires for persons under the conditions maximum possibility requires. The Distributed Correction result identifies the political function of that convergence: representation, public information, plural institutions, and review enable people affected by an arrangement to correct the shared public model guiding it. Downstream Does Not Discharge is earned here: suppressing, managing, or concealing the visible expression of an unmet condition does not discharge the obligation it created, and competing interventions are compared across the whole causal sequence, with no layer winning by its label. Inputs: §6.1–6.13, especially §6.3 and §6.4. Used downstream: §6.15.

**6.15 Implementation** — What putting the chapter’s constraints into practice requires. Inputs: §6.14. Used downstream: Conclusion.

## §7: Modality

The chapter engages challenges to the argument’s own semantic and modal machinery, prior to any question of a rival ground or a changing world. Its central diagnostic is whether a rival eliminates Time, Space, and Substance or redescribes them. None of the results of §§7–9 enters Chapters 4–6 as a fresh premise, but each closes a class of objection that would otherwise reopen the proof.

**7.1 Modal Semantics and Its Skeptics** — Tests whether semantic theories and skeptical programs undermine the modal vocabulary the proof uses. Seven subsections engage rigid designation, two-dimensional semantics, Quinean modal skepticism, modal conventionalism, modal expressivism, metaontological deflationism, and Wittgensteinian quietism. The Self-Application Fork presses the reflexive question: a global deflation of modality owes an account of its own modal status, and neither branch is free—contingent, and it owes why a configuration at which it fails does not unmake it; necessary, and the object-language/meta-theory distinction must be drawn before that necessity is treated as an exception. Inputs: §1.2 (Modal Status), §2.1 (the S5 pipeline), §2.6.6 (Modal Identity). Used downstream: §7.4.

**7.2 The Grounds of Modality** — Tests rival accounts of what makes modal facts hold. Eight subsections engage the source of possibility, dispositionalism, modal realism, linguistic ersatzism, combinatorialism, modal fictionalism, necessitism, and Sider’s structuralism. At §7.2.1, No Unconditioned Essence combines Way–Possibility Convertibility, Conditioned-Nature, Reality–Nature Identity, and No Non-Configurational Remainder: essence may explain modal truths about a thing, but no essence is structurally prior or additional to Nature. Inputs: §1.2 (Modal Status), §2.1 (Range(R)), §2.6.6 (Modal Identity), §3.3.3 (Against Fictionalism), and §2.8. Used downstream: §7.4, §10.1.2, and §11.10.

**7.3 Modal Logic and Modal Knowledge** — Tests the logic and epistemology by which the modal conclusion is reached. Four subsections engage impossible worlds and relative modality, the remoteness objection, Chisholm’s chained-origin paradox, and Gasking’s parody. Inputs: §2.1 (the S5 pipeline), §2.1.5 (the S5 Bottleneck), §3.5.4 (the non-S5 route). Used downstream: §7.4.

**7.4 What the Rivals Carried** — Divides the chapter’s rivals into two kinds: those proposing a rival source for possibility (dispositionalism, modal realism, ersatzism, and the rest of §7.2), and those contesting the semantic or epistemological apparatus itself rather than any source (§§7.1, 7.3). Neither kind is refuted outright; no candidate source escapes the structure it was introduced to ground, and no apparatus objection reaches the scope the argument actually occupies. Inputs: §7.1–7.3. Used downstream: framing of Chapters 8–9.

## §8: Metaphysics

The chapter takes up rivals that grant the argument’s machinery and press instead on what change, contingency, and objecthood themselves require, rather than on the apparatus by which the argument reaches them.

**8.1 Time, Change, and the Changeless** — Tests whether change can be absent while a real world remains. Five subsections engage Shoemaker’s time without change, emergent time, the unreality of time, the block universe, and Platonism. Inputs: §1.3 (Change), §2.3 (Necessary Possibility of Change), §2.4.11–2.4.12 (frozen-world and masking tests). Used downstream: §8.4, §11.3.2 (Eternity).

**8.2 Contingency, Necessity, and Nothingness** — Tests demands for sufficient reason, brute contingency, informational foundations, necessary existence, and modal collapse. Five subsections engage the Principle of Sufficient Reason, Humean contingency, information-theoretic foundationalism, Pizzi’s impossibility of nothingness, and the modal-collapse objection. Inputs: §2.5 (Triconditional Necessity), §2.7 (Incoherence of ∅), §2.9.4 (contingency within necessity). Used downstream: §8.4.

**8.3 Objects, Parts, and Identity** — Tests whether rival accounts of persistence, composition, and individuation evade the three Conditions. Five subsections engage temporary intrinsics, stage theory, bundle and trope theory, mereological nihilism, and haecceitism. Inputs: §1.5 (Existence and the operators), §2.4.7–§2.4.8 (Spatiality and Substantiality), §3.2.4 (bare simples). Used downstream: §8.4.

**8.4 What the Rivals Carried** — Groups the chapter’s verdicts by the kind of move each rival makes: denial attempts (the null state, onset-from-absence, strict monism, strict temporal unreality) collapse into incoherence or an act-side/object-side split; the priority attempt (a changeless ground) leaves a structural burden deferred to Chapter 10’s theological engagement; the insufficiency attempt (the block universe) is compatible at role-resolution with an open dispute over objective passage; Pizzi’s impossibility of nothingness converges with the book’s own closure of ∅. Inputs: §8.1–8.3. Used downstream: framing of Chapter 9.

## §9: Physics and Mind

The chapter takes up rivals that grant the three conditions outright and ask whether they are rich enough—objections from consciousness, process metaphysics, and the fit between mathematics and physical reality. Ten subsections cover the hard problem, eliminativism and illusionism, Russellian monism, cosmopsychism, idealism, Whiteheadian process metaphysics, non-locality and branching, mathematical applicability, the Mathematical Universe Hypothesis, and structural realism. Inputs: §2.6 (Triconditionality of Nature), §3.2.3 (Structured Content), §3.2.4 (bare simples). Used downstream: §9.11.

**9.11 What the Rivals Carried** — The chapter’s rivals converge on one verdict type: each concedes the structure is there and argues it’s insufficient, differing in what each says is left over rather than in kind. Process metaphysics realizes the bearer-role while disputing persistent causal being as a type; the Mathematical Universe Hypothesis and structural realism remain compatible pending a physical-realizer identity claim; the hard problem finds no escape from structure, its closure conditional on the Chapter 5 identity. Inputs: §9.1–9.10. Used downstream: framing of Chapter 10.

## §10: Rival Ultimates

Engages candidate ultimates—classical-theistic and non-classical alike—at full strength, deferring the structural inversion to Chapter 11. Four sections organize the engagement: §10.1 (Theistic Arguments for a Divine Ground) presses arguments in epistemic order, including divine conservation at §10.1.6, simultaneous causation at §10.1.5, and the result that fine-tuning leaves an actuality question at §10.1.9; §10.2 (Doctrines of the Divine Nature) takes up divine simplicity, the via negativa, and the changeless ground; §10.3 (Non-Classical Ultimates) engages Spinozist pantheism, Neoplatonism, process theology, Madhyamaka emptiness, and axiarchism; and §10.4 (What the Rivals Carried) accounts for what survives each engagement. There, the Grounding-Contact Trilemma places abstract grounding within Nature and concrete grounding in T, S, and Φ in determinate operation; No Outside Selector establishes that a real selector and its operative relation are aspects of Reality–Nature, so selection can explain an internal subconfiguration but can’t supply total actuality from an exterior or surplus position. Inputs: §2.6 (the three readings), §2.7 (Preclusion of ∅), §2.8, No Unconditioned Essence (§7.2.1), §3.5.6 (Modal Availability Can’t Be Tuned), §4.5.5 (Metaphysics–Physics Continuity), and Chapters 7-9’s rival-clearing. Used downstream: framing of Chapter 11, No Divine Addition, and No Supernature (§11.10).

## §11: Reclaiming Greatness

The classical theistic attributes are taken one at a time and tested by the kind of structure each claim actually requires. Concrete operations are T, S, and Φ in determinate operation; determinate atemporal grounding is an abstract structure of Nature; strictly content-stripped predicates face the ∅-like specification failure. The chapter runs from §11.1 through twenty-three attribute tests grouped into seven clusters plus Life (§11.6), and closes at §11.10 with No Divine Addition, No Supernature, and the strict-set no-referent corollary. The *discriminating-content burden* (§11.2.1) presses the static attributes, while the conditions of concrete operation—the Concrete-Entity Test (§2.4)—govern concrete agency, reach, contact, and moral action. Life stands between the two, and impassibility, static in type, does its work on the active arm.

**11.1 Greatness (No Supernature theorem; Aseity Forfeiture conditional theorem)** — The classical conception of atemporality, aspatiality, immateriality, simplicity, and pure actuality creates a pressure when it retains determinate cognition, agency, causality, or relation. Retaining those predicates spells out the Conditions at the resolution appropriate to them; withdrawing all differentiating content creates an ∅-like specification problem. The analysis does not make every classical or apophatic God-concept definitionally identical with ∅. On the structured side, Necessary Occupancy and the Triconditional Identity identify a concrete deity as Nature in determinate operation; it therefore forfeits classical exterior aseity without becoming contradictory. Inputs: §2.6.7, Necessary Occupancy, Triconditional Identity, classical attribute definitions (Glossary). Used downstream: every section in §11; §11.10.

**11.2 Constitution** — Groups the constitutive attributes—simplicity (§11.2.1), unity (§11.2.2), infinity (§11.2.3), perfection (§11.2.4)—the static predicates fixing what the divine being is held to be in itself, each pressed by the discriminating-content burden seated at §11.2.1. Inputs: §11.1. Used downstream: §11.3–11.9, §11.10.

**11.2.1 Simplicity** — The classical doctrine of divine simplicity, that God is identical with the divine essence, faces a differentiation burden: one simple truthmaker may ground many nonsynonymous truths, but the account must still explain their distinct correctness conditions, modal profiles, and differentiated concrete effects. The simplicity/differentiation analysis is the chapter’s hinge, releasing the attributes to be taken one at a time without treating predicate plurality alone as a proof of parts. Inputs: §11.1, §2.6.6 (Modal Identity), §3.2 (Way–Possibility Convertibility). Used downstream: §11.3.1 (Necessity), §11.2.2 (Unity).

**11.2.2 Unity** — Unity names the structural fact that the triconditional structure is necessarily one: there is exactly one system of conditions within which any possible occupancy and exchange happens, because *two systems* would require a more comprehensive system within which they differ. The Triconditionality of Nature is unique because its three conditions are required by any possible world: any candidate alternative either shares T, S, Φ and is therefore the same Nature, or fails to share them and is therefore not a Nature at all. Inputs: §11.1, §11.2.1 (Simplicity), §2.6.10 (Triconditional Identity). Used downstream: §11.2.4 (Perfection), §11.10.

**11.2.3 Infinity** — Infinity must run *along* a dimension; stripped of magnitude, number, and degree, the relocation to unlimited *esse* forks (via the *ipsum esse* → ∅ result of §11.2.1) into a scale or the Null State, so what is bounded by nothing outside is the structural conditions themselves. Inputs: §11.1, §11.2.1 (Simplicity), §2.7 (Preclusion of ∅), §10.3 (the actual infinite). Used downstream: §11.10.

**11.2.4 Perfection** — Perfection names the structural feature of necessity: what can’t fail to be what it is. Nature is *perfectus* in the etymological sense (*thoroughly made*, *completed*), not by a maker’s act on a making but by the modal-structure fact that the conditions of any possible world are the conditions of any possible world. The standard-of-perfection horn and the perfect-creator horn dissolve at the level of Nature: there is no separation of standard and bearer, and the *analogia entis* is a vertical reach within Nature rather than a relation between two beings of different kinds. The perfect-being engine produces the structural inversions of §11.2.1–11.9.2 faithfully: each great-making property the driving premise selects points at a structural feature the driving premise then attributes to a bearer defined as lacking it. Inputs: §11.1 and the attribute transfers §11.2.1–11.9.2, §2.6.10 (Triconditional Identity). Used downstream: §11.10.

**11.3 Aseity & Modal Standing** — Groups the modal-standing attributes—necessity (§11.3.1), eternity (§11.3.2), immutability (§11.3.3), impassibility (§11.3.4)—the predicates fixing the divine being’s mode of holding; each pressed by the discriminating-content burden (§11.2.1), with impassibility crossing to the active arm. Inputs: §11.1. Used downstream: §11.4–11.9, §11.10.

**11.3.1 Necessity** — A divine necessity specified only by withdrawal of every structural articulation risks the ∅-like failure; a structured necessary being instead owes the distinction between its modal standing and Nature’s necessary field. The section applies that dilemma without identifying every classical account of divine necessity with ∅. Inputs: §11.1, §2.6.10 (Triconditional Identity). Used downstream: §11.3.2 (Eternity), §11.10.

**11.3.2 Eternity** — Boethian *tota simul* eternity keeps *life* in its formula, and life modifies an extent. Where the simultaneity preserves the asymmetric structure the relational predicates need, T is present at that contact; a timeless mode must instead supply its own relational semantics and its contact with temporal order, which doesn’t by itself identify eternity with T’s modal status. Inputs: §11.1, §8.1, §10.2.3. Developed at: §4.2 (Time). Used downstream: §11.3.3 (Immutability), §11.8.1 (Presence).

**11.3.3 Immutability** — Immutability names the structural status of the modal structure: *does not change*, in the only sense that survives the doctrine’s pressures, names the necessity of the conditions of any motion. The classical doctrine attaches the predicate to a being lacking all potency to change; the structural reading attaches it to □(T∧S∧Φ), the triconditional structure within which directed transitions of substances happen, and assigns the action-language the believer’s life rests on (creation, providence, response, incarnation) to Nature in its operational aspect. Inputs: §11.1, §11.3.2 (Temporality), §2.6.5 (directed transition). Used downstream: §11.3.4 (Impassibility), §11.10.

**11.3.4 Impassibility** — Impassibility names the structural status of Φ: the substance/persistence condition as the carrier of events. *Not acted upon*, in the only sense that survives the doctrine’s pressures, names the structural feature of being-the-carrier-of-events, which is the condition of any reception at all. The believer’s God receives prayer, loves creatures, and suffers on the Cross because the carrier of those events is the substance within the necessary frame, and Nature is what is operating as that substance. Inputs: §11.1, §11.3.3 (Immutability), §2.6.6 (Modal Identity). Used downstream: §11.8.2 (Relatability), §11.10.

**11.4 Cognition** — Groups the cognitive attributes—awareness (§11.4.1), knowledge (§11.4.2)—pressed by the discriminating-content burden (§11.2.1): cognition requires an inside, and the conditions for an inside live in Nature. Inputs: §11.1. Used downstream: §11.5–11.9, §11.10.

**11.4.1 Awareness** — Awareness minimally requires articulated subject–content structure and a bearer. A temporal stream, spatially distinct poles, and ongoing persistence enter only under the richer claims the doctrine adds—modulation, second-personal relation, or an unfolding encounter—not from awareness by definition. Inputs: §11.1, §11.2.1. Developed at: §4.8 (Life), §5.3 (Feeling). Used downstream: §11.4.2 (Knowledge).

**11.4.2 Knowledge** — Omniscience can be proposed as non-temporal apprehension of temporal truths, so temporal content alone does not transfer the content’s mode to the knower. The remaining burdens concern the positive account of timeless bearing, the indexical and acquaintance content retained by *known now* and *known personally*, and how one simple actuality grounds a differentiated manifold of truths. The Encoding Dilemma applies only where the knowing is held to be actual and ongoing, not to inert encoding as such. Inputs: §11.1, §11.4.1 (Awareness), §11.2.1. Used downstream: §11.7.1 (Power).

**11.5 Intrinsic Value** — Groups the value attributes—holiness (§11.5.1), beatitude (§11.5.2)—pressed by the discriminating-content burden (§11.2.1). Inputs: §11.1. Used downstream: §11.6–11.9, §11.10.

**11.5.1 Holiness** — Holiness (being set apart, the wholly-other) is a contrastive structural fact: to be set apart is to be marked off *from* a field of other relata (S), across an act of consecration that holds the marking (T, Φ). The classical doctrine raises set-apartness to absolute otherness while denying the divine being any field to be set apart within; read within Nature, which hosts it, *holy* names the contrastive distinctness Nature sustains, and the structural result is *Divine Indistinction*: absolute otherness with no field to differ within collapses into no-difference. Inputs: §11.1, §11.2.1 (Simplicity). Used downstream: §11.2.4 (Perfection, which surveys every attribute transfer), §11.10.

**11.5.2 Beatitude** — Blessedness is the satisfaction of a being that could have wanted; the satisfaction-trilemma (universal love, complete blessedness, invariance) does not compose, and *blessed* (*autarkēs*) names Nature’s self-sufficiency, with no outside to lack or want. Inputs: §11.1, §11.3.1 (Necessity/aseity), §11.3.3 (Immutability), §11.3.4 (Impassibility), §11.2.4 (Perfection). Used downstream: §11.10.

**11.6 Life** — The classical *living God* requires the self-movement (immanent operation, contemplation, responsiveness) that immutability, pure act, and simplicity deny; *living*, in the only surviving sense, is a carrier (Φ) in directed transition (T) among differentiated states (S), which is Nature in act. Life stands between the static and active arms—billed as a constitutive perfection but inverting as the self-activity of Substance in time. Inputs: §11.1, §11.2.1 (Simplicity), §10.2 (analogical predication), §10.3.3 (Process Theology). Used downstream: §11.10.

**11.7 Agency** — Groups the active attributes of agency—power (§11.7.1), causality (§11.7.2), interaction (§11.7.3), sovereignty (§11.7.4)—tested by the Concrete-Entity Test (§2.4): a concrete act runs from a source to a term across S, along T, borne by Φ. Inputs: §11.1. Used downstream: §11.8–11.9, §11.10.

**11.7.1 Power** — Omnipotence either operates through the structural medium or supplies no determinate operation. Necessary Possibility adds that no exercise of power confers or withdraws a target’s real modal standing: creation may actualize an already necessarily available possibility but can’t enlarge Reality’s range. No Outside Selector adds that a real selector and its selection relation are articulations of total actuality, so selection may explain a subconfiguration but not the actuality of the whole from beyond it. No Unconditioned Essence closes the attempt to relocate modal legislation into an essence structurally prior to Nature. Inputs: §11.1, Necessary Possibility (§2.1.10), No Unconditioned Essence (§7.2.1), No Outside Selector (§10.4). Developed at: §4.4 (Substance). Used downstream: §11.7.2 (Causality).

**11.7.2 Causality** — Concrete actualization differentiates a realized condition from what preceded it, and strict Pure Act contains no such transition. That doesn’t by itself disprove atemporal agency: an atemporal account owes a distinct agency-making difference, while concrete, directed causal action incurs the Conditions at the operation (Concrete-Entity Test, §2.4). Inputs: §11.1, §11.7.1 (Power). Developed at: §4.7 (Cosmic History; type/token). Used downstream: §11.7.3 (Interaction).

**11.7.3 Interaction** — The doctrine of divine interaction requires sequence, bilateral responsiveness, persistent relata, affective tracking, mind-change, physical contact, contingent efficacy, and incarnational unity-of-subject—every feature the classical conception (timelessness, immutability, impassibility, simplicity) denies of the divine side and relocates to the creature. *Inter*, mutual driving, can’t be borne by a side that can’t itself be moved; the structural result is *Divine Inertness*, and the interactive structure of reality is what Nature bears in property mode. Inputs: §11.1, §11.3.3 (Immutability), §11.3.4 (Impassibility). Used downstream: §11.7.4 (Sovereignty), §11.10.

**11.7.4 Sovereignty** — Governance is a relation to a domain. A governor within Nature forfeits classical exterior aseity; a timeless decree offered as the invariant ground of temporally differentiated effects owes the contact by which one act explains these outcomes rather than others. Nothing governs Nature from a second concrete domain. Inputs: §11.1, §2.7. Used downstream: §11.8.2 (Relatability), §11.10.

**11.8 Reach & Contact** — Groups the active attributes of reach—presence (§11.8.1), relatability (§11.8.2), describability (§11.8.3), revelation (§11.8.4)—tested at the contact each attribute claims. Inputs: §11.1. Used downstream: §11.9, §11.10.

**11.8.1 Presence** — Divine presence-everywhere either is spatial (S reinstated) or is metaphor for causal availability (Φ reinstated); either way, the negation of S is forfeit. Inputs: §11.1. Developed at: §4.3 (Space). Used downstream: §11.10.

**11.8.2 Relatability** — Relation simpliciter doesn’t require reciprocal alteration, but the devotional relations the tradition makes central—being heard, answered, loved, met—are bilateral, and a bilateral connection incurs the Conditions at the contact it claims. Inputs: §11.1, §11.3.4 (Impassibility), §2.6.8 (Ontological Identity). Used downstream: §11.8.3 (Describability).

**11.8.3 Describability** — Every classical attribute, read strictly enough to preserve its denial and concretely enough to retain determinate content, either evacuates that content or reinstates what it was meant to negate. Inputs: §11.2.1–11.8.2. Used downstream: §11.8.4 (Revelation), §11.9.1 (Benevolence), §11.10.

**11.8.4 Revelation** — The deliveries the tradition identifies as revelation are temporally local, spatially local, and culturally fingerprinted across Φ; they bear every mark of a from-within-Φ transmission and none distinctive of a from-outside-Φ one, while hiddenness, content-error, and modal contradiction undercut the sufficiency the doctrine claims. What is universal and decisive is not a punctual delivery but the availability of the world to inquiry, a feature of Nature spanning every cross-section of T, S, and Φ; the structural result is *Divine Occultation*. Inputs: §11.1, §11.4.2 (Knowledge), §11.8.3 (Describability). Used downstream: §11.9.1 (Benevolence), §11.10.

**11.9 Moral Act** — Groups the moral attributes—benevolence (§11.9.1), righteousness (§11.9.2)—the manner-of-acting predicates: a manner of acting requires an act, and acting requires T, S, Φ. Inputs: §11.1. Used downstream: §11.10.

**11.9.1 Benevolence** — The moral predicates the tradition applies to God (*benevolent*, *just*, *merciful*, *loving*, *patient*, *faithful*, *gracious*) are manner-of-acting predicates: adverbial in grammar and requiring an act for the manner to modify. Acting requires the structural conditions of action: a substantive agent (Φ), a target distinct from the actor (S), succession from not-acting to acting (T). Stripping T, S, Φ strips what concrete exercises—commanding, judging, forgiving, protecting—run on; character and standard readings remain available, but each owes the bridge to concrete exercise (Character, Standard, and Exercise). The Latin compound *bene volens* (well-willing) names, traced honestly, what Nature is when subjects act on subjects to keep each other in being under symmetry-of-extraction. Inputs: §11.1, §11.7.1 (Power), §11.7.2 (Causality), §2.4 (Structural Requirement). Developed at: the Subsistence identification (§6). Used downstream: §11.9.2 (Righteousness), §11.10.

**11.9.2 Righteousness** — *Just*, *merciful*, *equitable*, *fair*, and *righteous* may describe standards, characters, institutions, verdicts, or acts. Their concrete exercise requires an agent, a recipient-field, and directed action; character and standard readings remain available but owe the bridge to concrete verdicts and acts. **The Missing Party Problem** exhausts the placements available to necessary exercised justice: external and necessary, external and contingent, internal and necessary, or unnecessary because the predicate has been revised to intrinsic character or standard. The section separately tests transfer across attributes and bearers, constancy across administrations, skeptical access, and the demographic distribution of eternal stakes. Its destructive pressure does not itself derive Chapter 6’s positive political identification of justice. Inputs: §11.1, §11.3.4 (Impassibility), §11.9.1 (Benevolence), Relational Distinctness, Necessity Permits Contingency. Used downstream: §11.10.

**11.10 What Remains of God?, the Conditional Closure** — No Divine Addition combines actuality/necessity-to-possibility, Way–Possibility Convertibility, Reality–Nature Identity, and No Unconditioned Essence: any possible divine referent is Nature, Nature in determinate operation, or an abstraction of such an articulation—never an independently constituted being outside or added inside it. No Supernature combines that result with concrete operation, no determinate content, and No Outside Selector. CG₀, the description that withdraws T, S, and Φ while refusing every thinner or analogical truth-condition for its active predicates, is impossible by specification failure (The Contentless God Has No Referent). Revised and analogical descriptions may survive only as natural articulations whose personal predicates must be earned. Rejection of universal structural conditioning remains a premise challenge requiring an alternative account, not a third ontological location. Inputs: §11.1–11.9.2, §2.7, §2.8, §2.9.6, No Unconditioned Essence (§7.2.1), and §10.4. Used downstream: §12 (the attribute results its doctrines inherit).

## §12: Exodus

For the length of this chapter, grants the opposite of the preceding chapters’ conclusion: that there is a God, that this God is the personal, transcendent, sovereign creator the Abrahamic traditions confess, and that the existence question is not being reopened. Two lines of argument run separately throughout: an internal argument asking whether the granted doctrines and their own texts sit together, which owes the preceding argument nothing; and an imported-result argument applying an earlier structural result (will, knowledge, identity, morality, or divine predication), which is conditional on that result and exited if the result is rejected. The chapter’s own account of the creature is checked against §5 throughout, which is why that chapter is the reference point here rather than the Chapters 1–3 proof directly. Inputs: §5 (the account of belief, will, and knowledge doctrine is checked against), §10.4 (the Grounding-Contact Trilemma, reused for the sign-source and creation-fork dilemmas), §11.1–11.10 (attribute results doctrines inherit). Used downstream: framing of the Conclusion.

**12.1 Origins, Fall, and Salvation** — Runs from creation (§12.1.1), which supplies the world the arc presupposes, through Genesis as primeval history (§12.1.2), which fixes what kind of human past the text may hand forward, the *imago Dei* (§12.1.3), the Fall (§12.1.4), original sin (§12.1.5), inherited guilt (§12.1.6), and atonement (§12.1.7), to what applies the repair in salvation (§12.1.8). Inputs: §5 (the creature’s capacities for belief, will, and moral standing), §10.1.2 (the Creation Fork), §10.1.5 (the Sustaining Relation’s Own Dilemma), §10.4 (the Grounding-Contact Trilemma). Used downstream: §12.2 (the historical stage the messianic claims presuppose).

**12.2 Messiah and the Last Things** — The promised office is weighed against Jesus (§12.2.1); only the Christian branch adds the incarnation (§12.2.3) and the resurrection (§12.2.4), while Judaism and Islam exit those two claims differently. The branches converge again on eternal life (§12.2.5) and final judgment (§12.2.6). Inputs: §12.1 (the history the messianic claim is staged against), §5.9 (the Legacy identification, engaged against eternal life’s numerical-survival claim).

**12.3 Divine Governance, Authentication, and Moral Standing** — Opens with governance—providence (§12.3.1), prayer (§12.3.2), and miracles (§12.3.3)—distinguishing meticulous control, concurrence, general governance, and publicly identifiable signs; continues through the authentication problem for scripture (§12.3.4) and prophecy (§12.3.5), divine hiddenness (§12.3.6), and faith and belief (§12.3.7); and closes on moral standing—the Four Insufficiencies (§12.3.8), the Moral Gap (§12.3.9), Borrowed Moral Capital (§12.3.10), Divine Command Theory (§12.3.11), and divine punishment (§12.3.12). The Moral Gap and Divine Command Theory entries import §5.14’s structural-relational grounding directly. Inputs: §10.1.16 (the Sign–Source Dilemma, canonical there and reused at §12.3.3), §5.14 (Morality), §5.11 (the Three Frustrations of Will, engaged against faith-as-a-choosable-state).

**12.4 Problems of Good and Evil** — Identifies the distinct forms of evil a creator theology must answer before offering a defense: teleological evil built into the world’s design (§12.4.1), harm written into standing law (§12.4.2), and targeted harm ordered outright (§12.4.3). These are pressures a theodicy inherits, not rival theodicies themselves. Used downstream: §12.5.

**12.5 Theodicies** — Stages the tradition’s replies as an escalation: Greatest Good (§12.5.1) fixes the standard every reply must meet; Free-Will Theodicy (§12.5.2) and Soul-Making Theodicy (§12.5.3) offer instrumental accounts; Redemption Theodicy (§12.5.4) turns to non-instrumental defeat; Skeptical Theism (§12.5.5) appeals to reasons beyond knowledge; and Evil God Redux (§12.5.6) closes the arc by reversing the whole defensive repertoire against a hypothesized evil or indifferent creator. Inputs: §12.4 (the pressures being answered), §5.11 (the Three Frustrations of Will, engaged by the Free-Will Theodicy).

**12.6 The Passover of Christ** — A single paired construction rather than one doctrine at a time: The Greatest Loophole (§12.6.1) separates whether pre-accountability beatitude is guaranteed, how that ranks against a life exposed to possible final loss, and what authorizes acting on the ranking; The Greatest Sacrifice (§12.6.2) then takes the branch supplying the guarantee and tests its figure against irrevocability as a measure of sacrificial greatness. The second argument is downstream of a named branch of the first, not a free-standing verdict about every account of the cross. Inputs: §12.6.1 (for §12.6.2 specifically).

**12.7 A Novel God, the Final Retreat** — A closing challenge rather than a continuation of the doctrine-by-doctrine sorting: granting that some argument for God succeeds, on any route, what further premise identifies what that mind wants? Tests curiosity as an alternative motivational add-on to the tradition’s worship-and-moral-perfection set, and asks whether the costs it avoids are simply traded for others. Inputs: §10 (grants any of its arguments their conclusion, for the sake of the challenge).

## C: Conclusion

The Conclusion synthesizes rather than extends the derivation. It presupposes the Chapter 1–2 proof as the canonical strict route; Chapter 3 as calibrated overdetermination; Chapter 4’s empirical identifications and cycle-shaped constraint with their physical limits; Chapter 5’s fit-based account of experience; Chapter 6 conditional on equal standing, effective exercise, and institutional duty-allocation; and Chapters 7–12 only for the particular rival, attribute, and doctrinal verdicts it reports. Its cross-traditional recurrence claim is conjectural and selection-sensitive. Acceptance of the proof does not import every downstream identification, and the Conclusion introduces no new spine premise. Used downstream: nothing; this is the terminal synthesis.

## Convergence

Every claim in the argument either (i) appears in the role-definitions of §1.3–1.4 and the modal premises of §2.1–2.5, (ii) follows by stated derivation from those definitions and premises, (iii) closes a class of objection in Chapters 7–9 without itself entering Chapters 4–6 as input, or (iv) is a modal account of experience (Chapter 5) or the collective application of that account (Chapter 6), conditional on the account of closure-and-throughput in §4.8 rather than a fresh deduction from the proof. Accepting the proof of Chapters 1–3 does not commit a reader to every identification downstream; the dependency structure makes clear where fresh assumptions enter.



# Appendix D: Empirical Predictions


This appendix consolidates claims that connect the book’s structural framework with empirical inquiry. The rows differ sharply in status: some state the book’s formal framework; some are explanatory hypotheses that add substantial auxiliary assumptions; and some are ordinary empirical predictions. A scientific result can challenge an auxiliary hypothesis, an interpretation, or its application without automatically falsifying the Chapter 2 modal proof.

The classifications are therefore:

1. **Structural framework claims**: claims about the role vocabulary and the book’s modal model. They aren’t empirical predictions by themselves.

2. **Framework-guided hypotheses**: claims combining the framework with abductive, theoretical, or empirical auxiliary assumptions. Their Basis and Status columns matter decisively.

3. **Empirical predictions**: claims testable by ongoing research programs; the Status column records their standing.

The final table records positions the book treats as under pressure within its framework. It shouldn’t be read as a list of positions refuted by empirical evidence alone. This is exposed to empirical contact through its auxiliary hypotheses and identifications, but that exposure must be stated at the appropriate register.

## How evidence bears

Evidence bears differently on the three classes. A structural theorem is assessed by its derivation; observation can expose a bad application, equivocal definition, or false bridge premise without functioning as a direct laboratory test of validity. A framework-guided hypothesis earns support when it discriminates between live alternatives, not merely when it’s compatible with the data. An empirical prediction needs an operational measure, comparison, time window, relevant controls, and a stated result that would count against it.

Converging reports aren’t automatically independent evidence. Shared data, common sources, inherited models, cultural transmission, translation, sample selection, and common coding can make several apparent witnesses one evidential route. Historical and cross-cultural comparisons therefore have to separate recurrence from independence: documented borrowing can support transmissibility and uptake while weakening a claim of independent convergence. A Bayesian claim requires a stated hypothesis space, likelihoods, priors or a justified measure, and relevant selection effects; without those, the appropriate conclusion is qualitative support, tension, or underdetermination rather than a posterior probability.

Failure propagates only along the dependency actually used. Evidence against a consciousness marker bears on that marker and on conclusions that require it; it doesn’t by itself reach the Chapter 2 modal proof. Conversely, the validity of the modal proof cannot certify an empirical identification whose auxiliary bridge fails. This appendix keeps the routes visible so agreement isn’t double-counted and failure is neither quarantined nor over-propagated.

## Tier 1: Structural framework claims

*These are the formal claims the book argues at the role/modal level. They aren’t empirical predictions, and no physical observation is listed as a direct confirmation of them.*

- **The possibility of concrete change requires Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality.** *Source: §2.4 · Status: Framework theorem-premise.*
- **Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality are necessarily co-instantiated.** *Source: §2.5, §2.9.6 · Status: the Necessity of Nature theorem within the book’s modal framework.*
- **At full Condition-instantiation, each Condition co-requires the other two in the same realizer through the priced succession, extension, and persistence routes.** *Source: §2.6.2–2.6.7 · Status: the Triconditional Cross-Entailment theorem within its stated scope.*
- **Laws divide by status: profile-constitutive invariants, effective laws, and regularities without a sufficiency proof.** *Source: §3.5.6 · Status: the Physical Invariance theorem. Nomological necessity is stated within the one modal field as □(L → Q), the antecedent marking the profile held fixed, rather than as quantification over law-varying worlds.* This is a claim about how a law’s necessity is stated and what carries it, not a prediction that any particular law is invariant. Which laws are profile-constitutive is settled by physics and proof, not by the framework.

Cosmological, physical, origin-of-life, quantum, and consciousness claims don’t belong in this tier. Each combines the framework with auxiliary assumptions and is classified below. A failure in those bridges bears on the application, not automatically on the formal spine.

## Tier 2: Framework-guided hypotheses

*These combine the framework with auxiliary legs. The Basis column marks whether that leg is abductive, interpretive, or empirical; the Status column carries evidential standing. Unless a row identifies a genuinely operational test, its final bullet is labeled “Discriminating evidence,” not “Falsifies if.” Specialist review is still required for the cosmology, origin-of-life, quantum-foundations, and consciousness rows.*

- **A stable zero-extension terminus is unavailable.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6 · Basis: the No Stable Zero-Extension theorem, strictly modal and independent of the physics of compression, plus an interpretive bridge to singular models · Status: Strict as a modal theorem; its application to physical singular models is contested / specialist review required.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: zero extension in a physical model represents absolute structural absence rather than a boundary, breakdown, or non-spatiotemporal successor regime.
  - Discriminating evidence: a mathematically controlled, empirically adequate model with a stable zero-extension state and well-defined observables would count against the application.
- **Black-hole evaporation preserves information—compatible with the framework, not predicted by it.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6 · Basis: Physical hypothesis, not a consequence of ∅-preclusion · Status: Active theoretical support.*

  - Evidence: Page-curve and quantum-extremal-surface programs (Page 1993; Penington 2020; Almheiri et al. 2020).
  - Operational test: an empirically supported evaporation model yielding irrecoverable non-unitary loss, with competing recovery mechanisms excluded, would defeat this application.
- **Cosmic history has no first physical moment, given productive explanation and the contingency of any alleged first state.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6, §2.1.3, §2.2 · Basis: Metaphysical-to-cosmological bridge · Status: Conditional result at §4.6, exact on its stated premises (productive explanation and the contingency of any alleged first token); not established by the Chapter 2 theorem alone.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: physical time realizes T without a boundary or emergent regime; a first moment is treated as prior changelessness rather than a boundary of the temporal manifold.
  - Discriminating evidence: a coherent, empirically adequate first-boundary or emergent-time model that doesn’t posit a prior changeless state would defeat the inference from T to past-eternity.
- **The earliest life was metabolically self-feeding rather than dependent on prior organisms.** *Domain: Origin of Life · Source: §4.8 · Basis: Conceptual constraint on “first” plus empirical reconstruction · Status: Plausible, not structurally proven.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: “autotrophic” is used broadly for abiotic resource capture; LUCA is an informative proxy for much earlier pre-LUCA systems.
  - Discriminating evidence: a viable origin pathway in which the first evolving system depends on a pre-existing nonliving feedstock network in a way not usefully classified as autotrophy would force revision of the label or claim.
- **The first energy-harvesting system was most likely non-photic, and chemical or redox in character.** *Domain: Origin of Life · Source: §4.8.2 · Basis: Abductive evolutionary-order claim · Status: Open.*

  - Supporting evidence: alkaline-hydrothermal-vent chemiosmosis (Martin and Russell 2007; Lane 2015) and reconstructed LUCA metabolism (Weiss et al. 2016), with LUCA treated cautiously as a proxy for earlier systems.
  - Auxiliary assumptions: complex extant photosynthetic machinery is representative of all possible photic capture and no simpler prebiotic photochemistry could precede templated evolution.
  - Discriminating evidence: a demonstrated prebiotic photochemical system capable of sustaining heritable self-maintenance before complex photosystems would count against the non-photic claim; a demonstrated prebiotic energy-harvesting pathway that precedes redox-dependent self-maintenance would count against the historical-order claim.
- **Early heredity most likely coupled catalysis and template-readability, with production, energy, and information cycles co-developing.** *Domain: Origin of Life · Source: §4.8.2 · Basis: Abductive synthesis of RNA-world, metabolism-first, and chemoton programs · Status: Open.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: extant ribozyme evidence and laboratory pathways constrain the historical route; “co-emerge” allows staged chemical precursors but denies a fully living isolated cycle.
  - Discriminating evidence: a reproducible origin pathway with long-lived evolution through separated specialized catalysts/templates or an independently living single cycle would count against the synthesis.
- **Relativistic spacetime, field mediation, conservation, and symmetry are physical realizations of the T/S/Φ roles.** *Domain: Structure of Physics · Source: §4.5 · Basis: Interpretive bridge from metaphysical roles to current physics · Status: Compatible with established physics, not confirmed as a unique metaphysical interpretation.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: current relativistic/QFT structures are role-realizers rather than contingent implementations among alternatives; quantum gravity will preserve the relevant bridge.
  - Discriminating evidence: successful empirically supported physics with non-spatiotemporal fundamental structure, non-field mediation, or revised conservation would undercut one or more identifications without directly refuting the role-level theorem.
- **Cosmological history may be cyclic at the macro-scale.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6 · Basis: *The Cycle* (§4.6.5), a theorem on the named premise *No Final Exercise*; the mechanism rests on an abductive family of models · Status: Return argued on a premise; mechanism speculative / contested.*

  - Supporting programs: LQG bounce at Planck density (Ashtekar and Singh 2011); Penrose CCC; Steinhardt–Turok ekpyrotic; Brandenberger–Peter matter bounce; Ijjas–Steinhardt new cyclic; Poplawski Einstein–Cartan torsion; Baum–Frampton phantom, retained for completeness rather than as current support, since it requires an equation-of-state parameter more negative than minus one and current supernova and baryon-acoustic-oscillation constraints run the other way.
  - Turnaround routes short of a cyclic model: a thawing scalar can carry the expansion rate through zero without phantom energy if its potential runs negative, which is unsettled (Scherrer and Sen 2008). Backreaction programs that deny a dark-energy component altogether (timescape, Lane et al. 2025; Seifert et al. 2025) would remove the expansion-driven obstruction to aggregation rather than supply a bounce; their standing is contested, and the program still owes a baryon-acoustic-oscillation reduction that doesn’t assume an FLRW metric and a fit to the acoustic-peak heights in the microwave background. A turnaround is a necessary condition for a macro-cycle, not a cyclic model by itself.
  - Auxiliary assumptions: at least one bounce or cyclic model is mathematically coherent, observationally adequate, and able to address entropy accumulation and perturbation transmission.
  - Discriminating evidence: observations that exclude the viable parameter space of specified cyclic or bouncing models count against those models; eliminating one program doesn’t falsify cyclicity as a family.
- **If macro-cycles occur, some structural regularities may recur across them.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6 · Basis: Conditional Phase Recurrence—□(K → E) where a maximal-compression phase-class K is metaphysically sufficient for entry into an expanding phase, so a later dynamically equivalent realization yields another expanding phase; the recurrence of K is itself a further physical premise · Status: Open.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: the bounce transmits enough structure or lawlike constraint for comparable large-scale development; Modal Invariance alone doesn’t entail identical histories, stars, or observers.
  - Discriminating evidence: a successful cyclic model whose successive cycles have materially different macro-trajectories would defeat the same-trajectory application while leaving cyclicity intact.
- **No interval of positive duration is changeless, so a permanently quiescent far future is unavailable as a *stretch*.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6 · Basis: the No Changeless Duration lemma, strict within the framework · Status: Framework-internal; not an independent empirical prediction.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: relationalism about instants—moments are individuated by a discerning difference in the T∧S∧Φ state they index. The lemma is strict given that premise, which the book’s account of Temporality already supplies; a substantivalist individuating moments by primitive temporal haecceity declines that account upstream rather than defeating the lemma from within it.
  - What it doesn’t settle: the two horns leave the order-type question open. A dilute phase that genuinely elapses is differentiated and so not changeless; one that doesn’t elapse has zero duration and collapses to a single moment, which isn’t the infinite changeless stretch denied. Whether that single moment could stand as a bare terminus is left open—□◇C remains globally true without giving that state a locally available successor.
- **Type–token coupling is proposed as an explanatory seam rather than an artifact of incomplete physics.** *Domain: QM & Type/Token · Source: §4.7 · Basis: Interpretive / abductive · Status: Underdetermined by current physics.*

  - Relevant programs: Penrose–Diósi gravity-induced collapse (Penrose 1989; 1996; Diósi 1989), decoherence (Zurek 2003), and consistent histories (Griffiths 2002; Omnès 1994) address different parts of the measurement problem and don’t jointly confirm one metaphysical seam.
  - Discriminating evidence: a successful theory deriving determinate token outcomes from the complete physical state without an independent token-level contribution would count against this application.
- **Token outcomes aren’t pre-fixed by the preparation type on its indeterministic application.** *Domain: QM & Type/Token · Source: §4.7 · Basis: Interpretive application of the empirical distribution · Status: Open.*

  - Evidence: repeated identically specified preparations yield distributed outcomes governed by the Born rule.
  - Scope: the distribution doesn’t by itself exclude deterministic nonlocal, hidden-variable, or superdeterministic interpretations; it underdetermines whether the complete physical state fixes the token.
  - Discriminating evidence: an empirically superior theory supplying a complete token readout from the prior physical state would defeat the indeterministic application.
- **Life may be a favored attractor under sustained energy gradients and suitable chemistry.** *Domain: Origin of Life · Source: §4.8.1, §4.8.4 · Basis: Abductive · Status: Speculative.*

  - Supporting considerations: dissipative-structure theory (Schrödinger 1944; Prigogine and Nicolis 1977; England 2013) and Earth’s early-emergence datum (Mojzsis et al. 1996; Bell et al. 2015).
  - Scope: one inhabited planet, uncertain habitability dates, survivorship selection, and unknown transition probabilities don’t establish a general attractor law.
  - Discriminating evidence: repeated well-characterized environments with sustained gradients, suitable chemistry, and geological time but no biosignatures would lower the hypothesis’s plausibility; one null case wouldn’t by itself settle it.
- **Sustained chemical disequilibrium raises the probability of life elsewhere under the framework-guided origin hypothesis.** *Domain: Origin of Life · Source: §4.8.4, §2.9.5 · Basis: Conditional extrapolation · Status: Open.*

  - Targets: ancient Mars, Europa, Enceladus (Hsu et al. 2015), and Titan, each with materially different uncertainties about duration, chemistry, accessibility, and preservation.
  - Scope: Modal Invariance doesn’t by itself supply the contingent chemistry or transition probability.
  - Discriminating evidence: adequate missions establishing long-lived suitable disequilibrium with strong preservation conditions but no biosignatures would count against the extrapolation in proportion to search completeness.
- **Integrated dissipative self-modeling is proposed as a marker of consciousness.** *Domain: Consciousness · Source: §4.8, §5.1 · Basis: Abductive constitutive identification · Status: Speculative research program.*

  - Auxiliary assumptions: the architecture is operationally specified independently of reports; self-modeling, integration, and dissipative maintenance jointly track phenomenal vantage rather than only cognition or control.
  - Operational tests: preregister architectural thresholds; compare report, metacognitive discrimination, flexible generalization, perturbational complexity, and lesion/anesthesia transitions across systems. Robust dissociation between the proposed architecture and this convergent marker set would count against the identification.
  - Limit: phenomenal absence isn’t directly observable, so “demonstrably lacks a vantage” isn’t an operational falsifier.
- **The same proposed marker is substrate-independent.** *Domain: Consciousness · Source: Substrate-Neutrality of the Living Constraint (§4.8), §2.4 · Basis: Conditional extrapolation · Status: Open.*

  - Operational tests: test non-biological systems that independently satisfy the preregistered architecture for the same convergent marker set, while controlling for trained verbal imitation. Persistent architecture/marker dissociation would count against substrate independence, not prove absence of experience.
- **Bacteria are proposed as minimal-marker cases; Bénard cells and hurricanes as negative controls.** *Domain: Consciousness · Source: §4.8 · Basis: Interpretive classification · Status: Speculative.*

  - Operational tests: compare adaptive learning, memory-dependent behavioral flexibility, self/non-self regulation, integrated perturbation response, and counterfactual control. The classifications should be revised if negative controls meet the preregistered marker profile or bacteria systematically fail it.
  - Limit: the tests discriminate its markers, not vantage directly.
- **Phenomenology is proposed to track organizational structure.** *Domain: Consciousness · Source: §5.1, §5.3 · Basis: Abductive identity claim · Status: Supported in part but underdetermined.*

  - Supporting evidence: psychoactive intervention, split-brain cases, dose-dependent anesthesia, and developmental trajectories constrain the dependence of reported experience on organization.
  - Scope: these dependencies don’t uniquely establish the book’s constitutive identity claim.
  - Discriminating evidence: robustly identical organization paired with systematically different phenomenology, or stable phenomenology across materially different relevant organization, would count against the proposed mapping, subject to the limits of report and measurement.
- **Deep self-modeling is predicted to increase hard-problem-style reports or cognate metacognitive puzzlement.** *Domain: Consciousness · Source: §5.4 · Basis: Abductive meta-problem hypothesis · Status: Open.*

  - Research route: the meta-problem program (Chalmers 2018), developmental and comparative probes, and artificial systems with independently measured self-inclusive modeling.
  - Operational test: preregister measures of reflective depth and report content while controlling for training, language exposure, and imitation. A stable dissociation in either direction would count against the proposed relation.
- **Sufficiently deep self-modeling lineages are predicted to develop structurally analogous registers, not identical cultural categories.** *Domain: Consciousness · Source: §5.17 · Basis: Abductive universality conjecture · Status: Open.*

  - Research route: comparative cognition, independently developed artificial systems, and any future astrobiological evidence.
  - Discriminating evidence: a demonstrably deep self-modeling lineage whose functional and phenomenological organization lacks analogues of the proposed registers would count against universality; translation failure or different vocabulary alone wouldn’t.
- **A non-corrosion floor should recur across genealogically distant moral traditions more reliably than any one positive account of flourishing.** *Domain: Comparative morality · Source: §5.14.3–§5.14.4 · Basis: Framework-guided cross-cultural hypothesis · Status: Provisionally supported.*

  - Research route: compare prohibitions, reciprocity rules, sanctions, and care practices across traditions using construct-equivalent coding, negative cases, and explicit genealogical and contact models.
  - Scope: recurrence within a transmission network tests retention and uptake, not independent convergence; translation and archive survival can also make unlike norms look alike or hide functional analogues.
  - Discriminating evidence: sufficiently independent, sustained societies of mutually exposed subjects that reliably coordinate without functional analogues of non-corrosion would count against the universality claim. Variation in the persons protected, the justification offered, or the positive ideal of flourishing wouldn’t by itself.
- **Experiences classified as spiritual should display recurrent phenomenological functions without requiring one culture-independent theology or sequence.** *Domain: Comparative religion and anthropology · Source: §5.16.3–§5.16.4 · Basis: Framework-guided comparative hypothesis · Status: Open.*

  - Research route: compare boundary alteration, dependence, awe, presence, ineffability, attentional training, and self-model modulation across religious and nonreligious settings.
  - Controls: measurement invariance, translation, practice history, expectation, institutional transmission, ecology, political structure, and observer coding.
  - Discriminating evidence: if the proposed experiential functions disappear when those controls are applied, or track one inherited doctrine rather than modifiable self-modeling across settings, the general structural interpretation loses support. Recurrence alone doesn’t identify a metaphysical object.
- **Independent cumulative inquiries are predicted to converge at invariant structural nodes without repeating one another’s representations or histories.** *Domain: Epistemology · Source: §5.4, §5.17 · Basis: Abductive convergence prediction · Status: Open.*

  - Research route: compare independently developed scientific traditions and artificial systems on shared domains now; extend the comparison to independently evolved lineages if such evidence becomes available.
  - Discriminating evidence: stable, successful navigation of the same domain by mature inquiries that require incompatible deep modal structures would count against convergence. Different notation, ontology, discovery order, or explanatory route alone wouldn’t.

## Tier 3: Empirical

*Testable by ongoing experimental programs; the Status column carries each result’s current standing.*

- **Primordial gravitational-wave spectrum and non-Gaussianity distinguishable from slow-roll inflation.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6 · Status: Active.*

  - Confirmation evidence: LiteBIRD, CMB-S4, Planck follow-ups; expected to discriminate within the decade
  - Falsifies if: Observation rules out bouncing-cosmology spectra in favor of slow-roll inflation only, with no surviving cyclic mechanism
- **CMB Hawking-point anomalies as previous-aeon signatures.** *Domain: Cosmology · Source: §4.6 · Status: Contested.*

  - Confirmation evidence: An et al. (2020)—one result, not two, since the 2018 arXiv preprint and the 2020 MNRAS paper are the same study at two stages. Meissner and Penrose (2025) is a theoretical consolidation rather than new observational support: it remains an unrefereed preprint, and it accounts for the observed angular diameter of the spots, about twice the expected value, by positing a gravitational-wave-dominated epoch just after the crossover
  - Falsifies if: Robust statistical re-analysis eliminates the signal once ring size is marginalized over (Jow and Scott 2020 already find it weaker; Bodnia et al. 2024 add an independent machine-learning search and flag a statistical pitfall from a few unusual bright or dark WMAP pixels)
- **Bell-local factorization is incompatible with the observed correlations, given the standard auxiliary assumptions.** *Domain: Quantum Foundations · Source: §4.7 · Status: Confirmed at the Bell-test level; interpretation underdetermined.*

  - Confirmation evidence: Bell-inequality violations (Bell 1964; Aspect et al. 1982; Hensen et al. 2015 loophole-free).
  - Scope: Bell tests don’t by themselves confirm token indeterminacy. They exclude the conjunction of Bell locality, the relevant independence assumptions, and predetermined local outcomes; deterministic nonlocal and superdeterministic interpretations remain logically available at stated costs.
  - Operational reversal: a reproducible loophole-free experiment satisfying the independence and detection conditions while obeying the relevant Bell inequality would overturn the empirical verdict.
- **Penrose-Diósi gravity-induced collapse predicts a mesoscopic threshold.** *Domain: QM & Type/Token · Source: §4.7 · Status: Active.*

  - Confirmation evidence: Tabletop tests of mesoscopic superpositions currently underway
  - Falsifies if: Mesoscopic superpositions persist past the Penrose-Diósi mass threshold without reduction
- **Near-death experiences are modeled as integrative-flow destabilization rather than departure.** *Domain: Consciousness · Source: §5.9 · Status: Hypothesis / underdetermined.*

  - Supporting evidence: residual or resurgent cortical activity around arrest; phenomenology compatible with hypoxia, disinhibition, reconstruction, and disrupted self-modeling.
  - Operational test: prospectively time-lock hidden targets, high-density neural monitoring, perfusion/oxygenation measures, and later reports. Veridical target recovery reliably time-locked to instrument-defined absence of the neural activity needed by the model would count against it.
  - Limit: “zero brain activity” is always relative to instrument sensitivity and sampled regions; it isn’t a metaphysical observation of total absence.

## Positions Under Structural Pressure

*The book’s framework treats these positions as facing specified conceptual or explanatory burdens. This table doesn’t claim that all are empirically refuted or that every rival formulation has been exhausted.*

- **Stable singularity (permanent zero extension).** *Source: §4.6.*

  - Pressure: If zero extension is interpreted as absolute structural absence, it conflicts with its ∅-preclusion. Boundary, breakdown, and non-spatiotemporal-successor interpretations remain live and were already separated.
- **Permanent information destruction at singularities.** *Source: §4.6.*

  - Pressure: The framework is compatible with information-preserving applications and predicts none of them, but permanent non-unitary loss doesn’t straightforwardly entail that Space is eliminated. This remains a physical hypothesis to be decided by quantum-gravity and evaporation models.
- **Block-universe fatalism (eternalism → fatalism).** *Source: §4.7.*

  - Pressure: Eternalism doesn’t entail fatalism. Its directional-flow account resists the added fatalist inference, while leaving the broader metaphysics of passage contested.
- **Strict Laplacean determinism (type fixes token exhaustively).** *Source: §4.7.*

  - Pressure: Its type–token application opposes exhaustive token fixation. Bell violations exclude Bell-local predetermined accounts under the standard assumptions, not deterministic nonlocal or superdeterministic interpretations.
- **Strict superdeterminism.** *Source: §4.7.*

  - Pressure: Superdeterminism rejects or revises measurement independence and therefore bears a substantial methodological and explanatory burden; it isn’t rendered logically unintelligible by that cost alone.
- **Strict Nietzschean eternal recurrence (token-level).** *Source: §4.6, §4.7.*

  - Pressure: Even if macro-cyclicity is granted, token-level recurrence doesn’t follow. Repeated tokens are treated as an additional hypothesis rather than a consequence of cyclicity.
- **Type-level fine-tuning (calls for external selector).** *Source: §2.7.3, §10.1.9.*

  - Pressure: The framework rejects ∅ as a physical contrast state, but fine-tuning arguments may use other modal or theoretical contrast classes. The external-selector inference therefore faces the comparison-class and likelihood burdens developed in §10.1.9 rather than simple empirical refutation.
- **Agency as readout of pre-settled computation.** *Source: §4.7.*

  - Pressure: Self-modeling configurations are proposed here as loci of token-level causal contribution. Competing deterministic accounts remain live unless the independent type–token application succeeds.
- **Substance dualism for consciousness.** *Source: §5.1, §9.1.*

  - Pressure: The self-modeling account claims explanatory sufficiency and places an added-work and detection burden on a second substance. Absence of a distinctive signature is a parsimony pressure, not a deductive disproof.
- **Strong panpsychism (consciousness all the way down).** *Source: §4.8, §9.3, §9.4.*

  - Pressure: If dissipative self-inclusion marks consciousness, strong panpsychism loses the arbitrary-threshold motivation addressed here. Panpsychists may deny that marker or assign it a different explanatory role, so the pressure is conditional on the constitutive identification.
- **Eliminativism / strong illusionism about consciousness.** *Source: §5.1, §9.2.*

  - Pressure: The functional transition to self-including modeling is a real activity that any account here is required to preserve. Illusionists can accept that activity while denying further phenomenal properties, so the dispute concerns what the function explains rather than whether the function exists.
- **Heterotrophic origin of life.** *Source: §4.8.*

  - Pressure: Strict biological heterotrophy presupposes prior organisms, but origin models may posit dependence on abiotic feedstocks without using heterotrophy in that strict sense. The first-system claim therefore constrains terminology and dependency structure rather than foreclosing every externally supplied pathway.
- **Photosynthetic origin of life.** *Source: §4.8.2.*

  - Pressure: Extant chlorophyll-based photosystems are downstream evolutionary products, which weighs against their priority. Simpler prebiotic photochemical energy capture remains an empirical possibility and is the discriminating alternative already named.
- **Sequential cycle emergence (metabolism-first or replicator-first).** *Source: §4.8.2.*

  - Pressure: The chemoton application predicts functional coupling before a system counts as fully living, but allows staged chemical precursors. Metabolism-first and replicator-first programs remain live accounts of that staging unless an independently living isolated cycle is required.

A reader who finds that an empirical result defeats a stated auxiliary hypothesis, identification, or application is reading correctly. The framework isn’t protected from empirical contact, but the target of a result must be identified precisely. A cosmological, biological, or consciousness hypothesis may fail without automatically refuting the global-capacity modal framework. Conversely, repeated failure of its best applications would substantially weaken its broader explanatory ambitions.



# Appendix E: The Mathematical Research Program


Chapter 2 located mathematics inside Nature’s articulation. It did not turn metaphysics into a
substitute for proof. A mathematical consequence holds wherever its profile is realized because a
realization lacking the consequence would not realize that profile. That is Invariant
Realization (§3.5.6). The theorem transfers an invariant after mathematics has established it; it
does not establish the invariant, select the profile, or show that the profile has a concrete
realization.

The limit creates a further question. If Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality are not merely
features found in one world but the necessary structure within which anything real can obtain,
what does that result contribute to mathematics itself? It may explain why mathematical
consequence binds concrete realizations without changing which consequences mathematics proves.
Or the structural account may admit a formalization strong enough to exclude models, determine
invariants, and produce theorems unavailable without it. The first achievement is a metaphysical
ground for mathematics. The second would be a mathematically generative foundation. They are not
the same result.

This appendix states what would distinguish them. It records the mathematical research program
opened by the proof, not additional conclusions already contained in it. Its conjectures are
conjectures, its formal targets require formal proof, and its applications remain conditional on
bridges that have not yet been supplied.

**[Note]**

**Status of this appendix.** The Necessity of Nature, the Modal Identity, Configurational
Necessitation, Condition-Individuation, and Invariant Realization are inherited results of the
manuscript. The formal language, representation theorem, minimality result, exhaustiveness
result, universal factorization, and realizability criterion for real possibility proposed here
are open work; the reconstruction program and domain applications are developed in the working
research notes. Nothing receives theorem-status merely by being a
mathematical restatement of the metaphysical claim.

One result from this program is an exception, and its status should be read precisely. *Exponential
Crossing Ambiguity* is proved, unconditionally, within an explicitly stated finite model, and is stated
with its proof in [Appendix F](https://inversionofgreatness.org/formal-results). It is not a
restatement of the metaphysical claim: it is a lower bound on what a pairwise description omits,
and it answers a narrower question than any of the targets above. Its weight rests on the model
being faithful to the modal core, which is argued where it is stated and not assumed here.

## What the argument already gives mathematics

Four results set the starting conditions.

*First, mathematics is performed within the structure it describes.* A proof is an actual change:
symbols are distinguished, steps are ordered, and content is retained across an inference. The act
therefore instantiates T, S, and Φ. That performative fact does not make the conclusion true. It
identifies the conditions under which proving, calculating, recording, and checking can occur
(§3.5.6).

*Second, a mathematical profile fixes its consequences internally.* A profile specifies elements
or positions together with the quantitative, relational, or operational conditions that
individuate the structure. Where every admissible realization of a profile M satisfies Q, a real
configuration cannot realize M while lacking Q. The necessity lies in the conditional:

$$
M\models Q\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Box\forall x\bigl(\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)\rightarrow Q(x)\bigr).
$$

Mathematical proof carries the left side. Invariant Realization carries the consequence into any
real realization.

*Third, the structural floor does not select a higher-resolution mathematics.* Temporality does not
select one temporal logic beyond every context; Spatiality does not select a dimension, topology,
or metric; Substantiality does not select a material bearer, conservation law, or field equation.
The three Conditions constrain any concrete realization while leaving its determinate profile to
be established. Linear orders, region calculi, manifolds, groups, algebras, and dynamical systems
may articulate parts of the structure without any one of them being identified with Nature entire
(§4.1).

*Fourth, logical and mathematical necessity do not pass into their subject matter without a
bridge.* A formal truth may describe a contingent configuration. A necessarily available
apparatus need not have a necessarily instantiated object. The bridge for a particular result is
therefore never resemblance alone. The profile must be specified, its consequence proved, and its
realization established at the resolution the conclusion requires.

These results give mathematics an ontological location and explain the application of proved
invariants. Whether they also give mathematics new theorems is the open question.

## The Chapter 2 inheritance map

The formal program should use the entire Chapter 2 result chain, not only the three Condition
names. Each inherited result supplies a different constraint or bridge.

| Inherited result | What it contributes here |
|---|---|
| Ordered Succession | Fixes the T-target as asymmetric, transitive ordering at modal-core resolution, not mere edge orientation. |
| Relational Distinctness | Fixes the S-target as occupiable, exclusive, crossable relational extension, not inequality or arbitrary graph separation. |
| Cross-Interval Persistence | Fixes the Φ-target as coherent bearing through a transition, not similarity between endpoint descriptions. |
| Structural Requirement | Sets the coverage conjecture: every adequate model of the fixed registered-change witness must carry all three loaded roles. |
| Sufficiency of Structure | Sets the reverse construction: the full triad must admit generic change, without pretending to recover the richer reflective witness. |
| Mutual Containment and Triconditional Cross-Entailment | Require co-instantiation in one realizer. Formal weak-role independence is a baseline below this loaded domain, not a refutation of the chapter. |
| Condition-Individuation | Requires both irreducibility and existence-axis exhaustiveness. Pairwise non-definability can address the first but not the second. |
| Conditioned-Nature | Locates mathematics as the quantifiable articulation of Nature; it interprets formal structures without selecting one formal theory. |
| Invariant Realization | Transfers every proved profile invariant into every real realization of that profile. |
| Three Logical Strata | Sets the proof-theoretic target: coordinated T-, S-, and Φ-calculi over a shared classical floor, with translation loss tested rather than assumed. |

This inventory reveals that the argument has already solved one of the hardest philosophical bridge
problems. If a mathematical profile M entails Q, Invariant Realization yields

$$
M\models Q
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Box\forall x\bigl(\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)\rightarrow Q(x)\bigr).
$$

The appendix does not need to invent a second account of why proved invariants bind real
realizations. It must do the mathematical work on the left and independently establish the
realization premise.

Apply that bridge to the rigid registered profile developed below. Let R name the finite systems
whose occurrence order, descriptors, descriptor dynamics, and comparison relations meet the
stated hypotheses; let $Q_R$ say that the system carries the canonically reconstructed temporal
order, bearer functor, and comparison metric. The mathematical theorem gives $R\models Q_R$.
Invariant Realization therefore supplies

$$
\Box\forall x\bigl(\operatorname{Realizes}(x,R)\rightarrow Q_R(x)\bigr).
$$

If an R-realization is genuinely possible, Necessary Possibility (§2.1.10) and Physical
Invariance (§3.5.6) further give necessary availability of an R-with-$Q_R$ realization. If R is
actually realized, the invariant is actual there. What remains open is exactly what should remain
open: whether the fixed reflective change-witness realizes R, and whether $Q_R$'s formal
structures meet the loaded criteria for T, S, and Φ rather than thin namesakes.

That last requirement is **role adequacy**. A reachability order must satisfy Ordered Succession at
the relevant resolution; a relational metric must support the occupancy and crossability demanded
by Relational Distinctness; a descriptor-induced functor must represent numerical bearing rather
than merely a sequence of qualitatively matching contents. The central bridge conjecture is that
registered change admits a presentation meeting all three adequacy tests naturally—independently
of arbitrary renaming or representational choice. Proving it would allow the new mathematical
reconstruction theorem and the inherited Chapter 2 modal machinery to compose.

Mutual Containment adds a separate design constraint. If it is rendered as three predicates with
the same extension, the roles collapse; if any two role-values uniquely calculate the third, the
formalization replaces co-requirement with functional reducibility. A three-sorted incidence
relation avoids both errors. Its triples record T-, S-, and Φ-instances meeting in one realizer.
Co-requirement says every admitted role-token belongs to such a triple. Irreducibility says each
pairwise projection is noninjective: forgetting one coordinate identifies full realizations that
the complete triple distinguishes.

These demands are mathematically compatible. For three copies of $\mathbb Z_3$, admit exactly the
triples satisfying $t+s+p\equiv0$ or $1\pmod3$. Every pair of coordinates permits two values of the
third, so no role is a function of the other two; all roles nevertheless occur only in complete
triples, and the admissible relation is a proper subset of the Cartesian product. The construction
does not model Nature—the modular rule is only a finite consistency witness. It proves that “one
same-realizer structure” and “three non-reducible roles” are not mutually contradictory formal
requirements. The substantive task is to derive the right incidence relation from registered
change and show that its lost coordinates correspond to the chapter’s loaded distinctions.

## Grounding and generation

A metaphysical foundation can matter without enlarging a formal theory. It may explain why logic
