number at most $2^d$; exchange of bearers flips all choices simultaneously and fixes none when
$d\ge1$, so the classes number at most $2^{d-1}\le2^{m-1}$. Attaining $2^{m-1}$ would require every
time to have two occupied positions and all $2^m$ choices to share one bearer-position shadow. But
two choices differing at a single time exchange the bearers there, so unless the occupied pair is
the same at every time their position-sets differ and the choices fall into different shadow
classes. With the pair constant, the choice holding a bearer at one pole gives it a single position
and is excluded by that shadow, removing exactly one class. ∎

## What follows

*The shortfall is unbounded.* With $m$ steps of succession, order and distinctness together leave
$2^{m-1}-1$ mutually indistinguishable histories, and only the persisting bearer separates them.
As §2.4.6 states, a bare
ordering "doesn't yet supply a subject persisting across the replacement." The theorem measures the
gap so described. It is not a constant to be absorbed once: it doubles with every step of temporal
depth.

*Enlarging space does not help.* The bound is independent of the number of positions. More room
creates more ambiguous cases but never a larger one, so the worst-case shortfall is governed by
temporal depth alone. Whatever a pairwise description fails to fix about which bearer went where, it
fails at a rate set by how many steps of succession there are and by nothing else.

*The three Conditions are not interchangeable at this resolution.* That is the sharper form of the
same point. The deficit is indexed to Temporality, repaired by Substantiality, and Spatiality is
silent about it. A formalism that treats the three as three columns of one table cannot exhibit this,
because it cannot tell the columns apart. The asymmetry is visible only once each Condition is given
the logical type the manuscript assigns it.

None of this establishes that the Conditions are necessary, which is Chapter 2's work and not an
appendix's. What it establishes is narrower and worth having on its own: that the third Condition is
not ornamental, and that the work it does can be counted.

## What is not here

The results are exact for two bearers and open in bearer count. The counting argument turns on there
being exactly two bearers and two occupied positions, so that one stands at each, and that step does
not generalize.

The model implements two of the three parts of §2.4.7's criterion for positional distinctness.
Extension and Traversability are represented; the requirement that both ends of a crossing be
*occupiable* is currently automatic rather than tested, and a model admitting unoccupiable positions
would be the sharper instrument.

A separate body of results concerns the *unstructured* ternary encoding — the interaction defect and
its behaviour under products and coarse-graining, and a proof that no measure of it can be stable
under both. Those are proved, and they are about the untyped object rather than about the
Conditions, so they belong with the research notes rather than in the book.

Whether the crossing obstruction is the same obstruction that the physics of identical particles
resolves by denying there is a fact of the matter is an open question and a live objection to the
Φ-limb. It is not settled here, and it is not settled by any result above.



# Author’s Notes

## On the Anonymity

Why no name behind the book?

The first reason is principled: an argument should stand or fall on its own merits, not the name or credentials behind it. Blind reviews are blind for a reason.

The second is personal: the work that went into this absorbed most of my waking hours for a sustained stretch. It took time away from earnings, loved ones, and enjoyment. What I’d love—more than anything—is to regain what was lost in the process. I need a break, and privacy protects that. Whether a name is eventually released isn’t a decision I’m ready to make, and it’s a decision that can only be made once. There’s no putting the toothpaste back in the tube, so to speak.

In any event, the work here is presented in the name of contribution, not recognition.

## On the Use of AI
Books are normally written slowly—drafted, read back, argued over with a field, and revised over the years that process takes. That slowness isn’t incidental; it’s what makes the output seamless, well researched, and comprehensible. The process is necessary, and so is review.

What AI supplied was the process without the pace. It was used as a backstop, a research aid, and a tool for review. It worked only within the constraints built into the process and on the ideas I provided.

## The Constraints
*Accuracy is non-optional.* A claim that outruns the step that earned it isn’t a stronger claim, it’s an unearned one. The quiet failure runs the other way: a hedge that withdraws what the argument already secured reads as modesty and costs a result. Both are the same defect. Confidence should never exceed the derivation.

*Agreeableness is failure, adversary is the resistance.* Without backstops in place, models can feed you what you want to hear. Models were granted no room for agreeableness. They were instructed to break the argument wherever they could and to keep anything out that wasn’t earned. The result isn’t a book written by AI. It’s the ideas that survived it.

*Contribution is owed.* Every position engaged with is a contribution to the question, not an obstacle in the way. Rival accounts need to be engaged charitably, and at full strength. A conclusion earned against a weaker presentation isn’t concluding anything.

*Maximum accessibility.* Philosophy belongs to everyone, not just philosophers. The goal was to make the work as accessible as possible, both in format and in content. Where a technical word had an ordinary substitute, I used it. Where substitution would blur a necessary distinction, the technical word remained. The mixed use of contractions is intentional. The difference between *does not* and *doesn’t* isn’t merely one of formality. When *not* is doing the heavy lifting, I leave it standing. Elsewhere, the contraction keeps the sentence moving.

*Words have to mean one thing.* Every discipline builds edges into its vocabulary that ordinary language blurs. The difficulty is in carrying an argument through interdisciplinary work without filing those edges off. A term-sense ledger keeps each word to one sense. Nothing here turns on a word doing double duty.

*My voice.* The content produced by AI can be sound, but the voicework isn’t built in. Every model and every update comes with its own change in prose. I needed a way to rein in the voice across the use of different models. To do that, I used copyediting sessions to double as voice-building opportunities. If anything was written in a way I wouldn’t say it, I recorded what I didn’t like about it, and how I would fix it. The findings accumulated into a voice that was more “me.” This isn’t a substitute for book-wide editing, but it’s a good baseline until I can afford to work through it more thoroughly.

*Model for the task.* Different models have different strengths and weaknesses, and many of those fluctuate model to model, version to version. In my experience, Anthropic models seemed more capable when it came to refining ideas, writing, and voice. Models like Opus rarely broke leash, and stood firm against allowing anything into the book that didn’t earn its way in.

*Review everything, often.* Auditing standards were built around soundness, voice, consistency, and the like. Those standards were then used by frontier models (GPT, Claude, Grok, Kimi) for independent blind audits. What audited a passage was never what wrote it—a model reading its own output has already agreed with it. GPT models tended to produce the most genuine findings, while also being the most likely to overshoot the correction. Where the auditors disagreed, I read the passage and decided. That is internal review. It is not external review and does not substitute for it.

## On Publication
Why online? And why free? If the argument here succeeds, it doesn’t belong behind a paywall or institutional gate. This isn’t a stance against being paid for work. It’s a commitment to accessibility. No funding, grant, institution, or advance was received in the book’s making; all costs were my own.

The other reason comes down to personal freedom. Without a house style to negotiate with, the book could be written the way I think, and at my own pace.

A print edition will arrive in time, pending public review, interest, revisions, and finances. What’s here for free stays up.

# Symbols


The notation used throughout the argument, collected for reference. The sections before **Scoped notation** are the **canonical legend**: symbols a reader may carry from one section to another. The scoped section records stable, readable forms confined to particular arguments.

Each symbol is defined in full where it’s introduced; the italic tag at the end of an entry points to the section where it first appears. Established logical, mathematical, and physical notation takes priority: the book introduces no private glyph where a standard sign already does the work. Book-defined single-letter constants are upright; schematic variables are italic; named operators, predicates, and multi-letter mnemonic propositions are upright. Bold is reserved for conventional system names and imported temporal operators.

## Logical and modal notation

**$\Box$** · *Necessity operator* · $\Box P$ is true just when $P$ holds across every configuration of Reality. *First use: §1.2.*

**$\Diamond$** · *Possibility operator* · $\Diamond P$ is true just when $P$ holds in at least one configuration of Reality. *First use: §1.2.*

**$\land\ \lor\ \neg\ \to\ \leftrightarrow$** · *Logical connectives* · Conjunction, disjunction, negation, material conditional, biconditional.

**$\forall\ \exists$** · *Quantifiers* · $\forall$ is the universal quantifier, read *for all*; $\exists$ is the existential quantifier, read *there exists*.

**$\top$** · *Logical truth* · Any logical truth, used to witness that the possible pole is non-empty. *First use: §2.1.3.*

**$\bot$** · *Contradiction* · Any contradiction, used to witness that the impossible pole is non-empty. *First use: §2.1.3.*

**$\therefore$** · *Therefore* · Reserved for the conclusion lines of formal syllogisms.

**$=_{\mathrm{df}}$** · *Defined as* · Introduces a stipulative definition.

**$\equiv$** · *Logically equivalent* · Marks interdefinable formulas in the modal-logic primer; unlike $=_{\mathrm{df}}$, it doesn’t introduce a stipulative definition. *First use: [Appendix A](https://inversionofgreatness.org/modal-logic-primer).*

**$\models$** · *Semantic consequence* · $M\models Q$ says that every admissible realization of the profile or model $M$ satisfies $Q$. This is the standard model-theoretic consequence sign, not a further modal operator. *First use: §3.5.6.*

## Variables

**$P, Q$** · *Propositional variables* · Schematic propositional variables, ranging over contentful claims. *First use: §1.2.*

**$M$** · *Model or profile variable* · A schematic mathematical or physical-mathematical profile. Italic $M$ follows the ordinary model-theoretic convention and is distinct from upright $\mathrm{M}$, the book’s fixed symbol for Movement. *First use: §3.5.6.*

**$L$** · *Law-profile variable* · A schematic independently specified physical law-profile in a conditional such as $\Box\forall x(\operatorname{Realizes}(x,L)\to Q(x))$. It is a local variable, not a proposition or a second necessity operator. *First use: §3.5.6.*

**$p$** · *Contingent-configuration variable* · A propositional variable ranging over claims about which contingent configuration is occupied. Lowercase $p$ is the scoped variable used in *Necessity Permits Contingency*, not a second book-wide propositional-variable convention. *First use: §2.9.4.*

**$x, y, z$** · *Individual variables* · Variables ranging over individuals or relata. In a locally defined predicate such as $\operatorname{Grounds}(x,y)$, the arguments are variables even when the predicate name has a separate fixed use elsewhere.

**$g$** · *Ground-candidate variable* · A proposed additional ground of Nature or concrete actuality, bound fresh in each argument that tests a candidate ground. *First use: §2.8.*

**$t$** · *Temporal index variable* · A time or temporal evaluation point within a locally indexed argument. *First use: §2.7.2.*

**$w, w’, w_0, w_1, w_2, w^*$** · *Possible-world representation variables* · These belong to the standard or rival semantic apparatus and represent complete configurations $\mathrm{R}$ could be claimed to admit; they don’t denote plural Realities. $w$ is generic; $w_0$ is the candidate representation posited to lack the structural Conditions at §2.7.4; $w_1, w_2, \ldots$ enumerate representations; $w^*$ is the dual representation introduced at §11.1 and Appendix B item 16. *First use: §2.1.5.*

## The Conditions

The book uses related structural vocabularies at different levels of resolution. The two symbolic columns come first; the prose columns then give the role disclosed by Change and the Condition’s name as borne in Reality. The rows mark corresponding role-families, not identities or automatic entailments. In particular, the generic Chapter 3 roles $\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{D}$, and $\mathrm{B}$ don’t by themselves establish the fully specified Conditions $\mathrm{T}$, $\mathrm{S}$, and $\Phi$.

| Modal-core Condition | Generic role-floor | Role disclosed by Change | Condition as borne in Reality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\mathrm{T}$ · Temporality | $\mathrm{O}$ · directed order | Succession | Time |
| $\mathrm{S}$ · Spatiality | $\mathrm{D}$ · determinate difference | Distinction | Space |
| $\Phi$ · Substantiality | $\mathrm{B}$ · bearing or realization | Exchange | Substance |

### Modal-core Conditions

**$\mathrm{T}$** · *Temporality* · The Condition of Reality such that succession is necessarily possible. *First use: §1.4.*

**$\mathrm{S}$** · *Spatiality* · The Condition of Reality such that distinction is necessarily possible. *First use: §1.4.*

**$\Phi$** · *Substantiality* · The Condition of Reality such that exchange is necessarily possible. Because the glyph is stipulated, the chapters avoid lowercase Greek for schematic formulas: propositions are $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{Q}$, $\mathrm{R}$, so that $\varphi$ is never set beside $\Phi$ where only case would tell them apart. Six such uses in §2.1 were converted to $\mathrm{P}$ on 2026-08-27. [Appendix A](https://inversionofgreatness.org/modal-logic-primer) is the deliberate exception and keeps $\varphi(x)$: it expounds standard modal logic in the notation its readers already know, and the schematic sense is the only one in play there. Unlike $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{S}$, the glyph is stipulated rather than mnemonic: it was fixed when the Condition was named *Physicality* and is retained across the rename so that every formula in print keeps its reference. *First use: §1.4.*

**$\mathrm{T}(x),\ \mathrm{S}(x),\ \Phi(x)$** · *Predicate form* · Applied to an individual $x$, each says that $x$ instantiates the corresponding Condition.

**$\operatorname{Concrete}(x)$** · *Concrete-existence predicate* · $\operatorname{Concrete}(x) =_{\mathrm{df}} \mathrm{T}(x) \land \mathrm{S}(x) \land \Phi(x)$. To exist concretely is to instantiate all three Conditions. This replaces the private notation $\operatorname{Exists}^{\mathrm{c}}(x)$: the superscript $\mathrm{c}$ was a local qualifier, not a standard operator. Abstract existential quantification isn’t represented by this predicate. *First use: §1.5.*

### Generic role-floor

The *Notation* paragraph at §2.2 introduces $\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{D}$, and $\mathrm{B}$ together; the derivation at §3.2 establishes them and uses them throughout.

**$\mathrm{O}$** · *Directed order* · The generic role of asymmetric ordering. It isn’t yet Temporality: $\mathrm{O}$ is directed order, not temporal succession.

**$\mathrm{D}$** · *Determinate difference* · The generic role of distinctness. It isn’t yet Spatiality: $\mathrm{D}$ is difference, not concrete relational exteriority.

**$\mathrm{X}$** · *Variable over the Conditions* · A bound variable ranging over the Conditions themselves, $\mathrm{X} \in \{\mathrm{T}, \mathrm{S}, \Phi\}$, used where a claim holds for each and is stated once. It isn’t one of the generic roles: those are $\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{D}$, and $\mathrm{B}$ above, which are thinner than the Conditions, whereas $\mathrm{X}$ takes the Conditions as its values. *Used at: §2.1.5 (Parasitic Negation, Negation Seal); §4.6 (Triconditional Closure).* The letter was chosen in 2026-08-30 to replace an earlier use of $\mathrm{D}$ in this role, which collided with the generic-difference $\mathrm{D}$ and inverted its sense—the role stands *against* Spatiality while the variable *includes* it.

**$\mathrm{B}$** · *Bearing or realization* · The generic role of carrying a fact, act, state, or arrangement. It isn’t yet Substantiality: $\mathrm{B}$ is bearing, not causal persistence.

## Structural notation

**$\mathrm{R}$** · *Reality* · The totality of what is real, identified with Nature in $\Box(\mathrm{R} = \mathrm{N})$. *First use: §1.1.*

**$\operatorname{Capacity}(\mathrm{R},P)$** · *Capacity relation* · Reality has the standing capacity for $P$ to obtain. Thus $\Diamond P$ means $\operatorname{Capacity}(\mathrm{R},P)$, while $\Box P$ means $\neg\operatorname{Capacity}(\mathrm{R},\neg P)$. *First use: §1.2.1.*

**$\operatorname{Range}(\mathrm{R})$** · *Complete admissible range* · The set of propositions Reality has the capacity to admit: $\operatorname{Range}(\mathrm{R}) =_{\mathrm{df}} \{P \mid \operatorname{Capacity}(\mathrm{R},P)\}$. Possible-world variables represent members or arrangements within this range; they don’t denote plural Realities or ground the range. *First use: §1.2.1.*

**$\mathrm{C}$** · *Change* · The concrete reflective transition witnessed in reading, doubting, and recognizing the doubt, reference-fixed at minimum resolution as *one state, then another*. Formal $\mathrm{C}$ retains that referent at book scope; it doesn’t denote maximally thin generic succession. *First use: §1.3.*

**$\mathrm{N}$** · *Nature* · $\mathrm{N} =_{\mathrm{df}} \mathrm{T} \land \mathrm{S} \land \Phi$. The definition is box-free; the necessity $\Box(\mathrm{T} \land \mathrm{S} \land \Phi)$ is the earned result Triconditional Necessity (§2.5). *First use: §1.4.4.*

**$\mathrm{M}$** · *Movement* · Change of position: one thing at a position and afterwards at another, having crossed what lay between. A species of $\mathrm{C}$, so $\Diamond\mathrm{M}$ entails $\Diamond\mathrm{C}$. Its containment of $\mathrm{T}$, $\mathrm{S}$, and $\Phi$ is constitutive rather than inferred, which is what lets the Movement Line spend none of the three constitutive premises. *First use: §2.4.7.*

**$\varnothing$** · *Null State* · Absolute nothingness. *First use: §2.7.1.*

**$\mathrm{Con}$** · *Convergence proposition* · Some separated physical trajectories reduce their separation and enter a common region or phase. Paired with $\mathrm{Div}$ in the Bidirectional Modal Capacity theorem: $\Box\Diamond\mathrm{Con} \land \Box\Diamond\mathrm{Div}$. The modal operators have global scope; the embedded proposition remains minimal convergence and doesn’t abbreviate total cosmic reconvergence. *First use: §4.6.*

**$\mathrm{Div}$** · *Divergence proposition* · Some separated physical trajectories increase their separation. Paired with $\mathrm{Con}$ in the Bidirectional Modal Capacity theorem: $\Box\Diamond\mathrm{Con} \land \Box\Diamond\mathrm{Div}$. *First use: §4.6.*

## Scoped notation

These forms have a stable, readable job within the indicated argument but aren’t book-wide metaphysical constants.

**$\operatorname{Acc}(x,y)$, $\operatorname{Reach}(x,P)$** · *Accessibility relation; reachability predicate* · In the locally introduced rival semantics, $\operatorname{Acc}(x,y)$ says that $y$ is accessible from $x$, and $\operatorname{Reach}(x,P) =_{\mathrm{df}} \exists y(\operatorname{Acc}(x,y) \land P(y))$. These are readable names for the rival apparatus; neither belongs to the book’s capacity-based ground of modality. *First use: §2.1.4.*

**$\mathrm{SC}$** · *Square-circle proposition* · One figure is square and circular in the same respect at the same boundary. Its invariant exclusion, $\neg\Diamond\mathrm{SC} \to \Box\neg\Diamond\mathrm{SC}$, supplies the spatial example of the negative modal arm. *First use: §2.1.10.*

**$\operatorname{Begin}(x)$, $\operatorname{Place}(x)$, $\operatorname{Produce}(x)$** · *Onset predicates* · Respectively: $x$ begins, $x$ is placed, and $x$ is produced. They occur only in the three Parasitic-Negation reductios and remain distinct because they carry distinct warrants. *First use: §2.4.6.*

**$\operatorname{Past}(\varnothing)$** · *Past-null proposition* · The Null State $\varnothing$ obtained at some past time $t$. The temporal reductio concludes $\neg\operatorname{Past}(\varnothing)$. *First use: §2.7.2.*

**$\operatorname{Grounds}(x,y)$** · *Grounding relation* · A locally introduced two-place predicate saying that $x$ grounds $y$. *First use: §3.1.5.*

**$\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)$** · *Realization predicate* · The concrete system or configuration $x$ instantiates the elements or positions of profile $M$ and preserves the relations relevant to the stated consequence. The named predicate is used because no single standard logical glyph expresses physical realization; its typography follows the standard convention for multi-letter predicates. *First use: §3.5.6.*

**$M_{\Delta}, I, X, \gamma$** · *Transformation-profile notation* · $M_{\Delta}$ is the locally defined non-trivial transformation profile; $I$ is its ordered index set, $X$ its state space, and $\gamma:I\to X$ the map assigning states to indices. The symbols retain their standard schematic mathematical roles. Italic $X$ is a state-space variable and is distinct from upright $\mathrm{X}$, the book’s variable over the Conditions. *First use: §3.5.6.*

**$\mathrm{MGB}$** · *Maximally-great-being proposition* · The proposition that a maximally great being is instantiated in Plantinga’s modal ontological argument. S5 validates $\Diamond\Box\mathrm{MGB} \to \Box\mathrm{MGB}$ without supplying the possibility premise. *First use: §2.1.9.*

**$\mathrm{CG}_0$** · *Contentless-God description* · The stipulated description that combines atemporality, aspatiality, and denial of any bearer-role with determinate active-ground predicates while refusing every thinner or analogical truth-condition for them. The Contentless God Has No Referent establishes $\Box\neg\mathrm{CG}_0$ for that description only. *First use: §11.10.*

**$\mathrm{Resolution}$** · *Resolution proposition* · The proposition that a history or mechanism preserves $\mathrm{T} \land \mathrm{S} \land \Phi$ through a would-be classical singular boundary. Necessary Resolution Possibility is $\Diamond\mathrm{Resolution} \to \Box\Diamond\mathrm{Resolution}$. *First use: §4.6.3.*

**$A$** · *Aggregation proposition* · Gravitational aggregation: matter converges into bound systems under mutual attraction. As a locally bound propositional letter it remains italic: $A \to \Diamond A \to \Box\Diamond A$. *First use: §4.6.3.*

**$K, E$** · *Compression-profile and expansion-phase variables* · In Conditional Phase Recurrence, $K$ ranges over a dynamically complete maximal-compression phase-class and $E$ over entry into an expanding phase. The standard schematic conditional is $\Box(K\to E)$. These italic variables are local to the argument: $E$ elsewhere retains its locally declared conventional meaning, including energy or an event. *First use: §4.6.3.*

**$\mathrm{Bang}$** · *Hot-phase type* · In No Final Exercise and The Cycle, $\mathrm{Bang}$ names the phase-type of the totality attested as the hot, dense state from which the present expansion proceeded, together with its passage into expansion: a type rather than a token, and an exercised phase rather than a merely possible one. Introduced at §4.6.5.

## Conventional notation in local examples

These symbols retain established meanings within the indicated technical example. They aren’t additional book-wide metaphysical constants.

**$\operatorname{Ch}$, $\Omega$, $E$** · *Chance notation* · $\operatorname{Ch}$ is an objective chance function, $\Omega$ its possibility-respecting sample space, and $E$ an event assigned positive chance. Here italic $E$ is an event variable, not upright $\mathrm{E}$ for outward continuation. *First use: §2.9.5.*

**$\mathbf{K}$, $\mathbf{T}$, $\mathbf{S4}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{S5}$** · *Modal-system names* · Conventional names for normal modal systems in Appendix A. Bold system-name $\mathbf{T}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are metalogical labels, not the book’s constants $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{B}$. *First use: [Appendix A](https://inversionofgreatness.org/modal-logic-primer).*

**$\mathbf{F}$, $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{G}$, $\mathbf{H}$** · *Temporal-logic operators* · Conventional operators for *will sometime*, *was sometime*, *will always*, and *has always been*. Section 4.6 uses $\mathbf{G}\mathbf{F}P$ diagnostically for a liveness claim—at every point, $P$ occurs again later—without adding that claim to the modal derivation. Bold distinguishes these operators from the conventional physical variables $F$ and $G$ below. *First use: §2.11.*

**$F, G, m_1, m_2, r$** · *Newtonian symbols* · Force, the gravitational constant, two masses, and their separation in $F = Gm_1m_2/r^2$. Italic $F$ and $G$ retain their conventional physical meanings locally; they aren’t upright $\mathrm{F}$ or $\mathrm{G}$. *First use: §4.6.3.*

**$M_{\mathrm{SR}}, E, E_0, p, m, c$** · *Special-relativistic example* · $M_{\mathrm{SR}}$ is the locally specified special-relativistic profile; $E$ is energy, $E_0$ rest energy, $p$ momentum, $m$ invariant mass, and $c$ invariant speed in $E^2=p^2c^2+m^2c^4$. The roman subscript is a descriptive abbreviation; the physical symbols retain their standard meanings. *First use: §3.5.6.*

**$\varphi$, $a$** · *Formula and individual metavariables* · Conventional schematic letters in Appendix A’s quantified-modal examples. They have no fixed book-wide referent. *First use: [Appendix A](https://inversionofgreatness.org/modal-logic-primer).*

**$\mathrm{MP}$, $\mathrm{UI}$** · *Inference-rule abbreviations* · Modus ponens and universal instantiation in Appendix A’s proof summary. *First use: [Appendix A](https://inversionofgreatness.org/modal-logic-primer).*



# Glossary

**Actuality** · *Definition.* A proposition is actual when it is true of the configuration that has actually been taken. Every actual fact is possible (actuality implies possibility), but not every possibility is actual. Conflating actuality with necessity—treating what happens to be true as if it could not have failed to be—is the *modal-collapse error*. Established in §1.2.

***actus essendi*** · “Act of being” (Latin); the metaphysical actuality of a being’s existence.

***actus purus*** · “Pure act” (Latin); Aquinas’s name for God as having no potency.

**Addressed Denial Instantiates Communication** · *Theorem.* A denial addressed through signs to another subject presents content for uptake across their separation. Whatever its success, truth, conventional form, or eventual interpretation, the act is an attempted coordination of signs and response, so an addressed denial that communication occurs instantiates communication at that minimal level. The theorem establishes attempted communication, not shared conventions, successful reference, accurate transfer, mutual understanding, or language's complete functional identity; a private mark, involuntary signal, or uninterpreted event falls outside it unless it is addressed for uptake. Depends on Representational Minimum (§5.4). Earned at §5.12.

***aeviternus*** · “Of the aeon” (Latin); the medieval intermediate category between time and eternity.

**Art as Encounter** · *Corollary of Art and One Channel.* Description alone does not reproduce acquaintance, though linguistic and nonlinguistic communication can both guide and partly constitute encounters. Artworks characteristically supply organized things or events for a receiver to undergo, not merely reports about them. Art is therefore not a clean second channel running beside language: the two overlap in poetry, narrative, performance, song, film, ritual, and ordinary expressive speech, and what distinguishes the artistic function in those mixed cases is the organized encounter and attention the work solicits, not the absence of propositions or a deliberately encoded feeling. Its liability follows: a manufactured encounter can install a reading that misrepresents what it is a reading of, with no paraphrase for the receiver to check it against—the against-mapping mode (§5.14) running through a channel with no propositional surface. Established in §5.15.

**Aseity** · *Definition.* The property of being uncaused, ungrounded, and self-sufficient. The present argument treats Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality as structurally prior to beings embedded in their roles. An embedded deity therefore forfeits classical exterior aseity and cannot be the independent ground of those Conditions. This is not by itself a contradiction: the deity may be described as uncaused within Nature or assigned a revisionary form of aseity, while an essence-prior proposal requires a separate account of its grounding relation.

**Aseity Forfeiture** · *Conditional Theorem from Necessary Occupancy and the Triconditional Identity.* Structure is ontologically prior to any being embedded in it: Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality (T, S, Φ) are prior to any being embedded in them—not temporally prior, but structurally prior in the sense that structure is the precondition of the embedded being’s existence rather than the reverse. Therefore no embedded deity (process, open, panentheist) possesses *classical exterior aseity*, independence from every more basic condition, or the standing to ground the Conditions it already requires. It may still be uncaused within Nature or retain a revisionary use of *aseity*, but that is not the classical grounding claim. The relabeling move (‘the triconditional structure is God’) changes the word while conceding the substance: necessity, all-encompassingness, and explanatory basicness do not entail personhood, agency, or intentionality. Established in §11.1, §11.10.

**Aversion as Modal Weight** · *Corollary of Drive.* Drive at either pole is directed at a branch rather than at a state of affairs: a being is averse not to the injury already sustained but to its continuing, worsening, or recurring, and the aversion persists through stretches in which nothing occurs. A drive-state is therefore a standing weight on a line the being holds as available, not an occurrent response to what is present. Three consequences: the modal field is required at the chapter’s floor rather than introduced at §5.4; aversion to a really impossible outcome is empty rather than small, since impossibility does not vary (§2.1.5), making it a mapping failure wearing the phenomenology of a stake; and a weight can be borne without being felt, which is what lets a wrong go unnoticed (§5.14). The result fixes the *form* of a drive-state only—not the accuracy of a being’s weights, nor whether what it is averse to is actually available to it. Established in §5.2.

**Benevolence, Divine** · *See* Moral Predicates, Divine; §11.9.1.

**Bidirectional Modal Capacity** · *Theorem.* Let $\mathrm{Con}$ state that some separated physical trajectories reduce their separation and enter a common region or phase, and $\mathrm{Div}$ state that some separated physical trajectories increase their separation. Both are actual; actuality implies possibility, and Necessary Possibility lifts each to a necessary global capacity: $\Box\Diamond\mathrm{Con} \land \Box\Diamond\mathrm{Div}$. Reality can neither acquire nor lose either directional capacity. The theorem supplies a boundary-closed, two-directional modal architecture when combined with No Stable Zero-Extension, but it does not entail that both directions are locally reachable from every configuration or that minimal convergence scales into total cosmic reconvergence. Established in §4.6.

**Big Bang Within the Cycle** · *Proposition.* The Big Bang is not a coming-to-be of Temporality from non-Time; that much follows strictly from the structural closure of Temporality together with No Stable Zero-Extension. A physically earlier phase follows only conditionally, if the endorsed modal PSR is strengthened by a productive bridge on which every contingent token configuration is explained by a physically prior one. Earned at §4.6.

**The Contentless God Has No Referent** · *Theorem.* CG₀ combines atemporality (¬T), aspatiality (¬S), and denial of any bearer-role (¬Φ) with determinate active-ground predicates, then refuses every thinner or analogical truth-condition those predicates might have. The description reaches ∅, which the Exclusivity of Nature precludes; so ¬◇CG₀, and □¬CG₀ by modal duality. Established at §11.10 by specification failure. It is not reached by mirroring Plantinga’s inference—no ◇□¬CG₀ premise is asserted anywhere in the argument; S5 is neutral between Plantinga’s ◇□MGB and its schematic mirror ◇□¬MGB (§2.1). Classical, essence-prior, apophatic, analogical, and revisionary proposals that retain determinate content are not made impossible by this theorem. No Divine Addition supplies the broader location result for any possible referent. *See* No Supernature; Appendix B item 20.

**Conditional Phase Recurrence** · *Theorem.* Let *K* be a dynamically complete maximal-compression phase-class and *E* entry into an expanding phase. If *K* is metaphysically sufficient for *E*, then □(K → E), so every actual realization of *K* yields an expanding phase, and a later dynamically equivalent realization yields another. **The recurrence of *K* is a further physical premise**; the theorem supplies the conditional, not the cycle. Earned at §4.6.

**Conditioned-Nature** · *Theorem.* For any X that spells out a structural feature of N, the nature of X = the X-describable feature of N. Earned at §2.6.12.

**Configurational Necessitation** · *Theorem.* Where *P* is metaphysically sufficient for *Q*—where no possible realization of *P* lacks *Q*—the relation is a structural constraint rather than a local regularity: □(P → Q). Earned at §2.9.4. *See* Strict Actualization for the move from the conditional to an actual consequent.

**Constitutive Grounding Non-Propagation** · *Lemma.* □(T∧S∧Φ) and □◇C are not ground and grounded but one fact under two readings: by Modal Identity the necessity of the structural Conditions just *is* the necessary possibility of change read modally, so □◇C carries its necessity by identity rather than by transmission across a grounding relation. Earned at §8.2.5.

**The Cycle** · *Theorem.* Given actual continuation and No Final Exercise, the hot, dense phase and its passage into expansion ($\mathrm{Bang}$) return without end: $\mathbf{G}\mathbf{F}\,\mathrm{Bang}$. Where a return completes a maximal-compression phase-class sufficient for expansion, Conditional Phase Recurrence carries each passage. Ordered return is the returning branch The Far-Future Partition leaves unpriced; fluctuation-only return carries an epistemic cost. **Future-directed; the mechanism remains physical.** Earned at §4.6.5.

**Demand Instantiation** · *Corollary.* Any demand for a ground of Temporality, Spatiality and Substantiality must itself be structured: grounding, explanation and condition each already name asymmetric ordering, distinct terms, and a stable standing of dependence. A grounding relation stripped of all three is not a grounding relation, so the demand cannot terminate in an absolutely structureless ground. These are the generic roles of ordering, distinction and bearing, not yet the loaded Conditions—the corollary does not upgrade ontological priority to Temporality, distinct relata to Spatiality, or stable dependence to Substantiality, and a thinly or analogically structured ground remains a live candidate carrying a contact burden (§7.2.1). Earned at §2.4.3.

**The Discursive Minimum** · *Theorem.* Any addressed, reason-giving argument instantiates at least a held distinction, an inferentially answerable transition, and attempted communication; if it is sustained as inquiry, it also instantiates episode-relative weighting. No argument of that form can establish the global absence of representation, reasoning, communication, or—where inquiry is sustained—all local concern, because the argumentative token is a counterinstance. The theorem establishes only those minimal operations: not truth, warrant, knowledge, successful reference, shared understanding, existential meaning, or normative binding. Gathers Representational Minimum (§5.4), Reason-Giving Instantiates Reasoning (§5.6) Addressed Denial Instantiates Communication (§5.12) and, for the local-weight clause, Inquiry Carries Local Weight (§5.10). Earned at §5.17.

**Downstream Does Not Discharge** · *Theorem.* Suppressing, managing, or concealing the visible expression of an unmet condition does not thereby discharge the obligation the condition created. Where upstream prevention, immediate protection, repair, sanction, and recovery compete, they are compared across the whole causal sequence rather than only where breakdown becomes visible; no layer wins by its label, and prevention has priority only where evidence shows it addresses the condition without imposing a worse cost or leaving an acute danger unanswered. Earned at §6.14.

**Extension’s Realizers** · *Lemma.* Real relational extension is biconditional with directed succession and persistent bearing: S ↔ (T ∧ Φ). The S entering the pivot is the S-role the theorem spends—concrete, occupiable, exclusive extension, the extension of media—rather than any static or merely representational surrogate. Earned at §2.6.

**The Far-Future Partition** · *Disjunction.* After any present state, cosmic history ends in a last state, runs a changeless stretch without end, has a last realization of the hot, dense phase, returns that phase only as fluctuation, or returns it in order. The first three are priced by actual continuation with No Stable Zero-Extension, by No Changeless Duration, and by No Final Exercise; fluctuation-only return carries the Boltzmann-brain cost; ordered return is unpriced. Earned at §4.6.5.

**No Final Exercise** · *Premise.* In a history with no last state, a phase-type of the totality that has been actual has no last realization. It ranges over exercised phase-types only, so it neither actualizes an unexercised possibility nor repeats a token history. **Adopted and defended, not derived from the modal floor.** Stated at §4.6.5.

**Greatness inverted** · *Concept.* At the level of metaphysical ultimacy, the properties traditionally sought in an ultimate ground belong to Nature: the temporal, spatial, and substantial structure constituting Reality. Nature is Reality’s necessary constitution, □(T∧S∧Φ), rather than a being that exists necessarily or one contingent arrangement; it depends on no ground outside itself and includes every real being and every real possibility. Developed at §4; the modal results it rests on are earned in Chapter 2.

**Ground-Candidate Partition** · *Lemma.* With respect to the grounding role, any candidate *g* either formally instantiates T ∧ S ∧ Φ; or claims to realize the same grounding functions without formal instantiation; or claims to ground temporal, spatial and substantial facts while realizing none of the corresponding structure. One criterion runs throughout—how *g* is alleged to realize the role—and the partition is diagnostic rather than probative. Earned at §3.5.

**The Grounding Conditional** · *Theorem.* Any grounding relation, at any level of any possible ontological stack, requires asymmetric priority, real differentiation of its terms, and a real fact or realizer in which it obtains. Any coherent ground of actual change therefore instantiates the generic role-floor. **The theorem fixes the roles only**; it does not identify their concrete types. Earned at §3.1.5.

**Guilt Does Not Travel** · *Theorem.* Culpability is blameworthiness indexed to the bearer whose act it evaluates. Consequence, inherited condition, remedial responsibility, corporate answerability and harm may all cross relations between persons; culpability does not cross merely because one of those does. Earned at §12.1.6.

**Incoherence of ∅** · *Theorem.* The Null State is not a coherent alternative to structure: it can’t be the case at any possible world, and it never obtained at any past time. ¬◇∅ ∧ ¬Past(∅). Earned at §2.7.2.

**Individuate** · To mark one thing off from another as a distinct item—to say what makes this one this one rather than that one. An *individuation* condition is whatever does that marking off.

**Inquiry Carries Local Weight** · *Corollary.* Where a subject sustains an inquiry as an inquiry, some answer, method, clarification, or warranted refusal is treated as worth the attention the episode gives it. The inquiry therefore instantiates local weighting even when its conclusion is that life has no cosmic purpose or that no answer is presently available. This establishes episode-relative concern only: not that every compelled response is meaningful to the respondent, that an entire life has meaning, that the inquiry's object exists, or that what the subject weights ought to be weighted by anyone else. Depends on Drive (§5.2) and Representational Minimum (§5.4). Earned at §5.10.

**Living Directionality** · *Theorem.* Any active living closure in the sense of Life (§4.8) regulates its exchanges relative to its own continued organization: closure produces and repairs the conditions of continuation, and throughput maintains the gradient across which that work occurs. During genuine dormancy the organization retains an internally grounded disposition to resume that regulation, though no regulation or measurable metabolism need then be occurrent. Biological directedness therefore follows from Life without an additional premise. The theorem establishes regulation toward continuation; it does not establish phenomenal feeling, felt drive, one experience common to every living system, or the identity between regulation viewed from outside and orientation lived from inside. Earned at §5.2.

**Modal Self-Sustenance** · *Theorem, standing beside Necessary Possibility.* Logical truth supplies a necessary possibility-witness, and contradiction supplies a necessary impossibility-witness, so both poles of the fixed modal frame are necessarily occupied: □∃P: ◇P ∧ □∃P: ¬◇P. The theorem secures non-vacuity alongside the derivation of Necessary Possibility rather than as a step within it; it does not itself establish proposition-wise modal invariance. The global-capacity argument at §2.1.4–2.1.5 earns that invariance, while Transition Closure (§3.1.2) remains the narrower diachronic result. Established in §2.1.3 and standing beside the theorem at §2.1.10.

**No Changeless Duration** · *Lemma.* No interval of positive duration is changeless. A stretch of time has positive duration only if it contains two distinct moments, and where moments are individuated by some discerning difference in the T∧S∧Φ state they index, distinct moments require that difference to obtain—so positive duration entails differentiation across the stretch. Earned at §4.6.

**Cartesian Certainty** · *Concept.* The indubitable certainty that change is possible (◇C): to doubt it is already to change one’s epistemic state, so the denial is self-refuting. The Cartesian fixed point of the argument, its premise Cartesian Certainty (§2.2), reformulated as *cogito ergo muto*. Lifted to its necessitated form—the Necessary Possibility of Change (□◇C)—by the Necessary Possibility theorem. *See* Performative Self-Refutation; Necessary Possibility of Change. Established in §2.2.

**Causal Offices** · *Concept.* The distinct explanatory jobs gathered under causal language: efficient or productive causation identifies what brings an effect about; material causation identifies what it is made from; formal causation identifies its organizing form; and final causation identifies its end. Metaphysical grounding is treated separately as non-causal dependence. Chapter 2’s Concrete-Entity Test governs productive work, not the other offices merely because they answer a *because* question. Scoped in §2.4; applied to divine causality in §11.7.2.

**Causation** · *Concept.* In the productive or efficient sense, a source causes a concrete effect when the effect obtains because the source makes a difference to it. Causation isn’t identified with Φ here: at the resolution of the Chapter 2 theorem, Φ supplies cross-interval bearing, while productive causal transmission belongs to the richer realization tier. Whether efficient causation is mere regularity or real production remains the Humean/anti-Humean dispute fixed at §1.5.6. Material, formal, and final causes answer different explanatory questions, and metaphysical grounding is non-causal dependence. The Concrete-Entity Test applies to concrete productive work, not to every use of *because* or *cause* (§2.4); the offices where divine causality is tested are distinguished at §11.7.2.

**Change** · **C** · *Reference-fixing definition.* The concrete reflective transition witnessed in reading, doubting, and recognizing the doubt, introduced at minimum resolution as *one state, then another*. The phrase fixes the phenomenon rather than exhaustively analyzing a maximally thin generic succession. Its ordered phases, concrete co-present differentiation, and retained content are progressively resolved as Succession, Distinction, and Exchange without changing C’s reference. Lowercase *change* may retain its ordinary generic use; formal C always names the witnessed kind fixed at §1.3 and displayed at full resolution in §2.2.

**Classical God** · *Definition.* The God of scholastic theology, including the Boethian conception of eternal presentness and the doctrines of immateriality and divine simplicity. Classical atemporality, aspatiality, and immateriality deny creaturely or loaded types; they do not automatically deny every thin ordering, differentiation, or grounding relation. A Maximally Great Being overlaps with this set only when the candidate is enriched with the additional classical attributes. *See also* Maximally Great Being; Perfect-Being Theology; Revised God; Scriptural God.

***Cogito Ergo Muto*** · *Concept.* “I think, therefore I change.” Its reformulation of Descartes’s *cogito*: the structural condition of thinking is the structural condition of change. The performative form of Cartesian Certainty (◇C): to doubt that change is possible is already to change one’s epistemic state, so the denial is self-refuting. *See* Cartesian Certainty; Performative Self-Refutation. Established in §2.2.

**Concept-Essence Identity** · *Named Corollary.* A concept and its essence are not two things related, but one thing under two descriptions. The classical move that distinguishes them—placing the essence behind the concept as its ground—introduces a structural separation that the analysis at the Modal Identity (§2.6.6) forecloses.

**Consciousness** · *Identification.* Consciousness is actual in at least the present first-person episode, and is what sufficiently integrated self-producing life is like from within: at minimum, a bounded organism’s integrated registration of its own condition in relation to its environment, where differences bear positively or negatively on it and can alter its conduct. Depth varies along discrimination, temporal reach, flexible integration, and reflective self-awareness, as a branching profile rather than a ladder. The first-person witness and T/S/Φ constraint are strict. Biological continuity, multiple realization, and explanatory economy warrant the identity between phenomenal awareness and the proposed living organization abductively as the best-supported explanation developed at §5.1; they do not deductively demonstrate it. Configurational Necessitation and Strict Actualization apply strictly only if that sufficiency premise is true. Life at §4.8.

**Constitution** · *Concept.* The relation between a thing and what it is made up of, read from either side: the clay *constitutes* the statue, and the statue *consists in* the clay. Runs at both the material-token level (statue and clay) and the role-analytic level (*change consists in succession, distinction, and exchange*). Established in §1.5.2.

**Constitutive Instantiation** · *Corollary of Triconditional Cross-Entailment.* Where one of T, S, Φ is *operatively present* in an experiencing—doing temporal, spatial, or bearing work rather than merely represented—the Operative-Role Bridge and same-realizer pivots co-instantiate all three there; if that experiencing is a state its ground is in, the ground instantiates them in that state. Mere actuality of a thin predicate does not trigger the result. Distinct from Mutual Containment, which states the domain-indexed co-requirement: Constitutive Instantiation carries the concrete occurrence to its ground. For the case where the ground merely *encodes* the Condition rather than instantiating it, *see* Encoding Dilemma. Established in §2.6.7; deployed at §3.1.5.

**Contingency** · *Definition.* A proposition is contingent (◇P ∧ ◇¬P) when it really could be the case and really could fail to be. The modal status that tracks arrangement-dependence: truth varies with which configuration obtains. Established in §1.2.

**Cycle** · *Concept.* A macro-structural recurrence of cosmic history in which the hot, dense phase and its passage into expansion return without end. The strict modal floor forbids a stable zero-extension terminus; the return itself is argued on a named premise, No Final Exercise, and stated as The Cycle; its physical mechanism remains for cosmology. Established in §4.6.

***Dasein*** · Heidegger’s “being-there,” the human mode of existence.

**Distinction** · *Concept.* One of the three structural requirements of Change (alongside Succession and Exchange). Identified with S in the role-definitions.

**Distributed Correction** · **R27** · *Theorem.* Democracy’s first function is not periodic preference aggregation but continuing public correction: representation supplies direction, public information makes conditions visible, plural institutions test competing descriptions, and review enables revision when an arrangement’s first account fails. Exclusion, censorship, opacity, and capture therefore damage a polity’s capacity to learn what it is doing to those it governs. The epistemic half inherits the conditions of Modal Convergence—distributed content, coordinated dependence, and correction that answers to a common object—and doesn’t guarantee that a polity meeting them tracks the truth. Established in §6.14.

**Duty Does Not Confer Authority** · *Conditional political proposition.* Distinctive institutional capacity can allocate a primary duty without authorizing every means of discharging it. Coercive authority requires a separate route through public authorization, affected-party inclusion, stated reasons, rights-bounded procedure, review, and remedy. The proposition does not derive legitimacy from T∧S∧Φ or supply a complete theory of political obligation. Established in §6.1.

**Efficient Causation** · *Concept.* Productive causation: one event or agent brings about a concrete effect. The book leaves open whether this is ultimately regular succession or real production, but any proposed efficient operation must satisfy the Concrete-Entity Test at its operation or contact. Distinguished from material, formal, and final causation, and from metaphysical grounding. Established in §1.5.6; scoped in §2.4.

**Encoding Dilemma** · *Corollary.* Any candidate ground of an actually structured experience either instantiates the experienced Conditions outright or merely *encodes* them; but an encoding that grounds a live experience is a tokened activity, borne in a medium (Φ), across distinct vehicle-elements (S), processed across steps (T). Either horn therefore delivers a ground instantiating all three. Independent of both the Triconditional Cross-Entailment and the level-invariance grounding-priority premise, which is why it reaches a critic who rejects both. Scoped to grounds of actual, ongoing experience—a frozen, never-read encoding need not succeed in time. *See also* Constitutive Instantiation. Established in §2.6.7; applied at §3.1.5 to the simulation, Cartesian-demon, and Boltzmann-brain hypotheses.

**Entailment** · *Concept.* One claim guarantees another: *P entails Q* means there is no way for P to be true while Q is false. Throughout the book *entails* carries the modal-metaphysical reading—no possible world in which P obtains and Q fails—unless the context is explicitly formal-logical. *See also* Necessity. Established in §1.5.3.

**Euclidean Axiom** · *Principle.* The S5 axiom that what is possible is necessarily possible: ◇P → □◇P. The present argument derives this as the Necessary Possibility theorem—from the Modal Constitution premise and the real/Reality identity—rather than importing it as an axiom (§2.1.3, §2.1.10). The *Principle* label here is the literature’s classification, not this book’s: in this book the content is a theorem, and a strictly stronger one, since Necessary Possibility also carries the bilateral limb ¬◇P → □¬◇P, which is not the Euclidean axiom. *See* Necessary Possibility theorem.

**Exchange** · *Concept.* One of the three structural requirements of Change. Identified with Φ.

**Exclusivity of Nature** · *Theorem.* The necessary structural ground of any concrete change-realizer is uniquely T, S, and Φ together: any proposed alternative for that role is either functionally equivalent to them, and so structure under another description, or unable to supply the full Conditions, and so unable to ground concrete change-realization. A zero-content candidate is ∅; a thinly or analogically structured candidate isn’t thereby ∅, but owes how its grounding role reaches concrete change without reinstantiating the Conditions. Declining the role secures no outside: any real coexistent belongs to Reality and so, by the Reality–Nature Identity, to Nature. This theorem alone does not decide Finean explanatory priority; the downstream No Unconditioned Essence result combines it with Reality–Nature Identity, Essence-Description, and Way–Possibility Convertibility to close essence as a structurally prior or additional source. Established in §2.9.7; completed for essence-priority at §7.2.1.

**Existence** · *Definition.* Concrete existence is the three Conditions in determinate operation; it need not mean point-location in metric space. Abstract existence is an abstraction of structural articulation and therefore realizes the Conditions at abstract resolution without thereby becoming a concrete location or activity. A candidate said to change, act, experience, create, sustain, or cause incurs the concrete definition at the operation. Established in §1.5; formalized by the Concrete-Entity Test at §2.4 and the constitutive non-addition of §2.8.

**Feeling as Lossy Readout** · *Corollary of Feeling and Aversion as Modal Weight.* The correspondence between a body’s standing weights (§5.2) and what it feels at a time fails in both directions: a weight can be borne without being registered, so a subject may hold a real stake it is not feeling; and valence can fire where no weight is warranted, which is dread arriving with nothing threatening. Two consequences: felt intensity is not a measure of standing, the two being distinct quantities neither of which can be read off the other; and the readout cannot discriminate its own object’s modal status, since aversion directed at a line R cannot admit is empty rather than small (§2.1.5) yet dread of the really impossible presents exactly as dread of the avoidable—a distinction available to reasoning (§5.6) and not to feeling. Downstream, the readout is a source of loss standing upstream of any distortion in the reporting channel (§6): a subject can report faithfully what it feels while what it feels misrepresents what it holds. Established in §5.3.

**Final Cause** · *Concept.* The end, purpose, or good for the sake of which something occurs. A final-causal explanation does not by itself describe a concrete productive transmission, though any agent or mechanism said to realize the end may incur the Concrete-Entity Test. Distinguished from efficient, material, and formal causation. Scoped in §2.4 and applied to divine causality in §11.7.2.

**Fine-Tuning Leaves an Actuality Question** · *Theorem.* Once modal availability and profile-relative invariance are separated, fine-tuning leaves at most the question why this necessarily available physical profile is actual here rather than another. Its actuality secures its possibility, and Necessary Possibility secures that possibility throughout the modal field; neither makes the profile actual at every world. Fine-tuning does not by itself supply the space or measure of alternatives, explain the profile’s constitutive invariants, or establish a personal selector and intention. Multiple consequences entailed by one profile are not independent tuning data. Earned in §10.1.9 from Possibility Precedes Probability, Modal Availability Cannot Be Tuned, Physical Invariance, and Metaphysics–Physics Continuity.

**Field** · *Concept.* The physical realization of S↔Φ—substance does not occur without spatial extent. Established in §4.5.

**Floor Condition** · *Terminology.* A binary gate in Chapter 6’s domain analyses: a requirement inherited from something the argument has already established as necessary, rather than a feature whose contribution is graded. Its test is failure-conditional: without it, the arrangement fails to satisfy the underlying requirement at all. Floor conditions are jointly non-negotiable, although the institutional forms that realize them may remain underdetermined. *See also* Maximization Condition. Applied across §6.6–6.13.

**Formal Cause** · *Concept.* The form, organization, or structure in virtue of which a thing is the kind of thing it is. A formal-causal explanation does not by itself assert efficient production or temporal transmission. Distinguished from efficient, material, and final causation. Scoped in §2.4 and applied to divine causality in §11.7.2.

**Grounding** · *Concept.* Non-causal dependence: X *grounds* Y when Y holds *because of* X, where the *because* is metaphysical, not causal or temporal. The dependence runs one way only; the canonical case is Fine’s singleton, grounded in its member and not the reverse. Adjacent operators (*fixes*, *makes the case*) name determination. Established in §1.5.5.

**The Identity of the Totality** · *Theorem, from Necessity of Nature and the Reality–Nature Identity.* Reality, Nature, and the universe in its totality sense are one and the same—one totality under three names, not three things that coincide. Necessity of Nature establishes □(T∧S∧Φ); the no-surplus Reality–Nature Identity Derivation establishes N = R at the field level. Together they support the identity, which is stated as plain identity: the modal theorem governs Nature’s structure rather than separately establishing necessary identity. Necessary co-instantiation alone would not establish identity. *Nature Alone* (Chapter 4) supplies the totality-sense extension: with nothing standing outside Nature to ground or supplement it, the totality of what there is just is Nature. Discharges the totality-sense identity flagged at §1.4.4; the contingent-arrangement sense of “universe” is excluded. Established in §4.9.

**Immutability, Divine** · *Concept.* The classical attribute that God can’t undergo change of any kind—in essence, will, knowledge, or relation. *Immutabilis* names what can’t be moved or altered; the doctrine extends the negative predicate past contingent change to *any* change whatever, including the change of standing in a new relation to a contingent creature. The argument shows the doctrine is unintelligible at its load-bearing point: change is what the Modal Identity (§2.6.6) shows is what it is for a being to be in Nature; a being for which change is foreclosed in every direction is a being whose conditions of existence—succession, distinction, exchange—have been stripped, and what remains is no being at all. Distinguished from the contingent-feature-stability classical theism also valorizes (constancy of character, of purpose, of love), which the framework can preserve as a structural feature of any integrated being-in-Nature but which the classical doctrine collapses into the metaphysical claim that no change of any kind is metaphysically possible for God. Established in §11.3.3.

**Impassibility, Divine** · *Concept.* The classical attribute that God can’t be acted upon or affected—not by suffering, not by creaturely petition, not by the contingent fact of any creature’s existence. *Impassibilis* names what can’t undergo *passio*. The doctrine is the relational extension of immutability: where immutability forecloses change *of* God, impassibility forecloses being-affected *by* anything that would constitute a real relation between God and the contingent. The argument’s response runs parallel to immutability: being-affected is the receiving side of exchange (Φ); a being for which the receiving side is foreclosed in every direction is a being for which Φ is stripped, and Φ stripped means ∅ by the Exclusivity of Nature theorem. The compassion-language of scripture and liturgy presupposes precisely the relational receptivity the doctrine denies. *See also* Immutability; Benevolence, Divine. Established in §11.3.4.

**Impossibility** · *Definition.* A proposition is impossible (¬◇P) when it really could not be the case. Structurally so: there is no configuration that includes it. Distinguished from “very improbable” and “situationally unobtainable.” Established in §1.2.

**Intentional Traversability** · *Constitutive Premise · reflective S-route.* The reflective witness’s retained content and present act are separately selectable, co-present poles; attention can pass between them while retaining their non-identity. That relation satisfies Spatiality’s modal-core criterion only if this possible passage constitutes nonmetric positional structure. The premise is the disputed bridge from intentional articulation to relational exteriority: it grants neither metric nor bodily geometry, and a critic may reject it while retaining the Movement Line to S. Established in §2.4.7.

**Institutional Bearer** · *Political-structural definition.* A persisting arrangement of offices, rules, records, procedures, and material capacities through which changing persons can make and carry publicly attributable commitments. The arrangement is not a collective consciousness: persons remain the subjects, while offices and procedures specify how an act becomes attributable to the institution and records carry its obligations across turnover. Established at the Chapter 6 political bridge.

**Infrastructure** · *Concept.* The standing material, institutional, and cooperative supports that political and productive activity already presuppose. Chapter 6 distinguishes hard infrastructure (roads, utilities, hospitals, ports, broadband), soft infrastructure (law, regulation, public health, scientific commons, market-making institutions), and cooperative infrastructure (trust, norms, accumulated knowledge, trained capacities, and predictable rule of law). The word names those supports, not every feature of a polity or shared life. Established in §6.

**Inversion** · *Definition.* Showing that what a position places prior to structure in fact runs downstream of it. The book makes the move twice. Against classical theism, the tradition’s negations of T, S, Φ do not describe a higher reality but an evacuated one, and the application runs systematically across the divine attributes (§11.2–§11.9). Against Platonism, the *polarity inversion*: what looks like a prior pattern prescribing actuality is a description of what actuality, under the structural conditions, produces (§8.1.5). The term names that move and its applications; it is not a label for any argument that reverses a claim.

***Ipsum Esse Subsistens*** · “Subsisting being itself,” Aquinas’s name for God as pure act of being.

**Legacy** · *Corollary of Mortality, Identity, and Meaning.* The continuation of a person’s effects after the person’s own self-producing recursion has closed: representations held by other subjects, possibilities opened through relationships, practices and artifacts set in motion, and institutions or living subjects the person helped shape. Real causal and relational continuation, admitting of degrees, but not numerical or experiential survival of the person. At political scale, generative legacy widens the possibilities of living subjects without preserving unanswerable posthumous control. Established in §5.9, where the *Legacy as Transferred Field-Content* corollary gives it a mechanism: what continues is field-content already transferred into fields that remain open, so legacy admits of degrees by how much transferred and into how many fields rather than by how well the person is remembered, and the content is fully alienated from its source—revisable, corruptible, and improvable by others, never again by the one whose it was. Political application in §6.7.

**Life** · *Definition.* A temporally extended process whose active phases couple a closed self-producing recursion to sustained energy throughput. During dormancy or cryptobiosis, the organization produced by that activity persists with an internally grounded disposition to resume the same process when enabling conditions return; external reconstructability alone does not suffice. Multiply realizable across substrates, with Darwinian evolution downstream of closure. Established in §4.8.

***maranasati*** · The Theravada Buddhist meditation on death (Pali).

**Material Cause** · *Concept.* That out of which something is made or constituted. A material-causal explanation identifies a constituent basis; it does not by itself assert productive transmission. Distinguished from efficient, formal, and final causation. Scoped in §2.4 and applied to divine causality in §11.7.2.

**Maximally Great Being** · **MGB** · *Concept.* Plantinga’s perfect-being candidate: a being with maximal excellence—omniscience, omnipotence, and moral perfection—in every possible world, and therefore with necessary existence. This thinner candidate is not by definition a species of the Classical God and does not by itself include atemporality, aspatiality, immateriality, or divine simplicity. Those are additional classical enrichments whose joint realization carries further coherence burdens. Perfect-being theology generates the candidate; the modal ontological argument still requires independent warrant that such a candidate is possible. *See also* Classical God; Perfect-Being Theology; Perfection, Divine; Possibility-Premise Burden; The Contentless God Has No Referent. Established in §10.1.1; the enriched set is tested through §11.2.4 and §11.10.

**Maximization Condition** · *Terminology.* A graded contribution to Chapter 6’s standard of maximum shared possibility. Its test is substitutability: if the feature were absent, would the arrangement fail an already established requirement, or would it remain an instance of the required kind while realizing it less fully? In the latter case the feature is a maximization condition. Such conditions may be satisfied by degree and may trade off without the arrangement thereby failing its floor. *See also* Floor Condition. Applied across §6.6–6.13.

***meditatio mortis*** · The meditative practice of contemplating death (Latin).

**Depth Without Fidelity** · *Corollary of Imagination.* A modal field is measured on two axes: modal depth, how much of the modal structure it maps, and modal fidelity, how truly it maps it (§5.4). Imagination raises the first and does not, by itself, touch the second—a branch can be loaded into the field, held as live, weighted, and reasoned over, with nothing in the loading that certifies that R can admit the branch. Four consequences: conceivability is not, by itself, modal evidence, now for a stated reason, since entertaining a branch is a fact about the recursion’s capacity to assemble prior material rather than about what R can admit (§7.3.2); imagination is nonetheless not idle, since depth can answer the third of the Three Frustrations of Will, unmapped availability (§5.11); fidelity has to come from elsewhere—reasoning, convergence, or action; and conceivability is time-indexed while R’s standing capacity is not, so what a population can entertain grows with its representational stock while what R can admit does not, and no fact about conceivability at a time carries modal weight on its own. The loading is recombinatorial and over-generates at two distinct levels, alongside a third case that is not a defect: excluded by R altogether (compossibility failure, elements severally possible that cannot jointly obtain); admitted by R but not locally reachable (the second of the Three Frustrations of Will, arriving at the level of loading rather than willing); and admitted by R, reachable, and merely not actual, which is the productive case a hypothesis, a plan, and fiction all occupy. Kept sharply apart from combinatorialism about modality (§7.2.5), which makes possibility itself the recombination of actual elements: this claim concerns the operation a recursion performs on its own field, not what fixes what R can admit. Established in §5.5.

**Derivative Corrigibility of Meaning** · *Corollary of Meaning.* A weighting is not true or false in the way a mapping is: that some branch matters to a subject misrepresents nothing, and no standard is supplied here by which one end is the right end. But weightings are rarely bare—most run through a dependency, *this is worth doing because it is required for that*—and a dependency is a modal claim, ¬◇(that ∧ ¬this), whose truth is fixed by the structure rather than by the subject holding it (§2.1.5). A weighting therefore inherits the defect of any false dependency it runs through. A second defect is independent of the first: a weight is a standing weight on a line the subject holds as available (§5.2), at the attraction pole as at the aversion pole, so where the line is not available the weight is empty rather than small. Availability fails two ways: R may be unable to admit the line at all, which no inquiry could have revealed otherwise; or R may admit it while it simply is not the case, the ordinary situation of a life organized around a falsehood, which inquiry can in principle correct. The clearest cases are not religious—a life spent demonstrating that the earth is flat, a vindication that will not arrive—and a political orientation adds a first-limb variant in which the arrangement is real and reachable while the consequence attributed to it is false, corrigible in principle but slowly, through confounded evidence. That limb is restricted—preclusion is established for specific candidates under specific sets rather than for whatever a subject might mean by its object, and emptiness attaches to the line under the description the subject holds it by, so a weighting can track a real branch under a failed description (Spirituality (§5.16) recovers those on structural terms). The limb is not sectarian: where two traditions make incompatible claims, each already holds of the other that a large population orients a life toward what is not there while experiencing the orientation as fully meaningful, so every party has conceded the phenomenon and merely locates it elsewhere. Two consequences—felt meaning is not evidence of its object, which is §5.3 at population scale; and the framework is one more entry in the structure rather than an exception, its own weightings corrigible on both limbs. The framework can accordingly show that a life is organized around a requirement that does not hold, and cannot show that what the life was reaching for was not worth reaching for. Such errors persist because necessity-axis corruptions are self-sealing (§5.14): complying with a requirement never tests whether it held. Where the false dependency was installed by another agent, this is the against-mapping mode of wronging operating on the weighting layer, which can direct a life without telling it a false thing about the world. Established in §5.10.

**Medium** · *Concept.* What carries or sustains something across: a beam *bears* a load, a wire *carries* a current. Adjacent to causation but distinguishable—a medium can bear without producing. Names the general transmission operator, not a role-term for Nature or a synonym for Substance (§1.4.3). Established in §1.5.7.

***memento mori*** · “Remember that you must die” (Latin).

**Invariant Realization** · *Theorem.* Where *Q* is a formally valid consequence of a mathematical profile *M*, every configuration realizing *M* carries *Q* under every modal evaluation: $M\models Q \Longrightarrow \Box\forall x(\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)\rightarrow Q(x))$. The theorem transfers a proved consequence to realizations and does no more: it does not establish that *M* has a real realization, nor that *Q* follows from *M*, which remain the burdens of mathematical construction and proof. Earned at §3.5.6. *See* Physical Invariance, which applies the transfer where physics establishes the profile.

**Metaphysics–Physics Continuity** · *Theorem.* Modal metaphysics and physics describe one Nature at different resolutions, not two ontological layers. Metaphysics fixes the invariant role-conditions of any concrete change-realizer; physics identifies the actual profiles that realize those conditions and proves the invariants those profiles carry. The role-conditions do not select one physical profile, and an alleged explanation placed above physics gains no exterior domain merely by changing registers. Earned in §4.5.

**Methodological Convergence** · *Principle.* Logic, metaphysics, mathematics, and physics can be read as partially converging on structural roles relevant to the three Conditions. The convergence is abductive and interpretive: physics and mathematics do not independently demonstrate the modal proof, while the proof does not derive their particular empirical results. Established in §4.1.

**Modal Access** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The reaching-into relation by which a being queries the modal structure and updates its modal field: perception is modal access running in real time, knowledge is modal access retained in modal memory, and language enables access to representations expressed by other beings. The reliance-on-modal-memory gradient developed across Chapter 5 tracks how heavily current access leans on prior memory. Defined at §5.

**Modal Availability Cannot Be Tuned** · *Theorem.* For any physical profile *M*, a genuinely possible real realization is necessarily possible: $\Diamond\exists x\,\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)\rightarrow\Box\Diamond\exists x\,\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)$. Since actuality entails possibility, the present actual profile is therefore necessarily available: $\exists x\,\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)\rightarrow\Box\Diamond\exists x\,\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)$. The profile’s availability can’t be conferred or withdrawn by selecting among profiles. A selector may be proposed only for which available profile is actual, not as the source of the alternatives among which it selects. Necessary availability is not actuality at every world. Earned in §3.5.6.

**Modal Field** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* A body’s fallible interior mapping of the modal structure at the depth its recursion has reached. Where the modal structure is the fixed structure of what is and is not possible—the modal structure □(T∧S∧Φ) defines, presupposed by any possible description, law, or transition—the modal field is a particular being’s interior mapping of that structure. It is not the modal structure itself but a fallible map of it: the structured space of possibility the being is configured to operate in, which can misrepresent the modal structure (a field can be wrong; the modal structure cannot). Constituted by the being’s modal access relations to the modal structure; populated by modal memory; organized by its modal representations, each placed by a modal weight. Measured on two axes: modal depth (how much of the modal structure it maps) and modal fidelity (how truly it maps it). The individual pole of the Chapter 5 apparatus; its collective counterpart—many fields pooled and interlinked—is the modal network. Distinct from the modal structure (shared as the structural ground) and from logical space / possibility space (literature-engagement names for the modal structure). Defined at §5 and developed at §5.4.

**Modal Structure** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The objective pole of the apparatus: the uncreated structure of what is and is not possible, fixed by □(T∧S∧Φ) and the same for every body. A modal field is a body’s fallible mapping of this structure, not the structure itself. Defined at §5 from the modal constitution established in Chapters 1–2.

**Modal Identity** · *Theorem.* Nature read from the side of possibility: the three Conditions whose joint instantiation is co-extensive with the possibility of change across all worlds—◇C ↔ (T ∧ S ∧ Φ). In the equivalent capacity idiom, Reality’s capacity for Change is internally the capacity for before and after (T), here and there or this genuinely apart from that (S), and bearing from one state into another (Φ). The Conditions are therefore what the capacity is, not three further possibilities it might later acquire. Read as an identity, not a mere necessary biconditional—the two sides have no independent ground, so they are one structural fact under two descriptions rather than two facts that necessarily co-vary. The identity reading is load-bearing rather than optional: once □◇C and □(T∧S∧Φ) are both established, both sides are necessary and their necessary co-extension follows for free, as it would between any two necessary truths, so the biconditional alone carries no structural information. What distinguishes this pairing is hyperintensional—the absence of individuating content on either side—and a reader who resists it falls back to the forward conditional, not to the biconditional (§2.6.6). The first of three readings composing the Triconditional Identity (§2.6.10), alongside the Triconditional Cross-Entailment theorem and the Ontological Identity theorem; in necessitated form, □◇C ↔ □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ). Both legs carry Change under the same structural description. The reflective transition and movement are witnesses for that kind, not different meanings of it; the forward conditional identifies what actual Change requires, while the sufficiency argument yields Change’s possibility from the joint instantiation of those requirements (§2.4.10).
