The chapter theorem □(T∧S∧Φ) spends the forward conditional and □◇C, not the converse. Established in §2.6.6.

**Modal Representation** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* A registered aspect of a modal field, rendered in any modality and available for the body’s operations. A representation may register what is necessary, conditionally necessary, structurally co-varying, or freely contingent across some domain. Self-modeling systems instantiate interior modal representations; technology at depth externalizes representations into shared substrate, building the modal network (§5.13). Probability is conditional on the modal structure the representation identifies; probability precision is bounded above by modal-representation resolution (§10.1.9). Defined at §5.

**Modal Memory** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The registration of modal access that has occurred and remains available for re-access. The substrate of knowledge: to *know* is to have modal memory of an access, retrievable on demand. The folk-language entry point is the phrase *I used to know that*—which marks not the loss of a fact but the failure of current modal access to retrieve from modal memory the path to the fact. Perception is modal-memory-in-real-time: the ongoing write-update of modal memory as access is currently occurring. The reliance-on-modal-memory gradient developed across Chapter 5 (including the hallucinogenics passage at §5.16) tracks how heavily current modal access leans on prior modal memory versus operates with that reliance loosened. Defined at §5.

**Modal Pressure** · *Theorem.* Cartesian Certainty (§2.2) supplies a strict existential witness that at least one structured subject registers actuality and possibility from within. *Modal Pressure* names the chapter’s proposed generalization from that witness: where a conscious body represents alternatives as open and weighted by its stakes, those representations exert directional pressure within its modal field (§5.4). The objective possibility of Change, the body’s local representation of alternatives, and the felt pressure of those representations remain three related claims, not one fact under three descriptions—only the existential witness is strict; the general, naming-level account stays conditional on the chapter’s account of consciousness and its empirical fit. The N ↔ □◇C reading (§2.6.10) fixes the objective modal structure; it does not by itself describe what any organism represents or feels. *See* Triconditional Identity. Canonical callout at §5; structural lift at §2.6.10; load-bearing applications in §4.8 and §5.2.

**Modal Status** · *Concept.* A proposition’s modal status is whether it is possible, impossible, or necessary—the three values that pick out how it stands relative to what could really be. Two further values fall out alongside the three: contingency (a proposition that could be the case and could fail) and actuality (the value that picks out the configuration that has been taken). Modal status is the organizing concept of §1.2, not itself a numbered definition; its values are fixed by the definitions it ranges over. *See* Possibility, Impossibility, Necessity, Contingency, Actuality. Established in §1.2.

**Modal Convergence** · *Theorem.* Where an epistemic network distributes representations across subjects and artifacts so that no one member holds the whole, coordinated retrieval and correction are required for the network’s output, and those practices answer reliably to a common object, the network realizes an epistemic capacity no solitary member realizes. Its knowledge remains constituted by the holdings, media, and relations within the network; no further group subject is implied. Agreement alone is insufficient, and convergence is evidence of tracking only so far as the inquiries are sufficiently independent, the checks discriminating, and the common object able to correct them. Reasoning (§5.6) and language (§5.12) analyze important realizations of its conditions; morality (§5.14) and spirituality (§5.16) state their own grounds rather than inheriting this one. Established in §5.4.

**Modal Closure** · *Corollary.* The necessary structural Conditions admit no unnecessary alternative standing apart from them. Stated to hold together the two claims the chapter runs in parallel—□F at the structural level, where F = T∧S∧Φ, together with genuine contingency ◇p ∧ ◇¬p among the configurations F admits—so that the necessity of the Conditions is not read as the necessity of what occurs within them. Distinguished from modal collapse, which is the error the principle forecloses. The converse direction, that necessity-talk itself presupposes a non-trivial modal space, runs through Way–Possibility Convertibility (§3.2). Established in §2.9.7.

**Modal Depth** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The extent axis of a modal field: how much of the modal structure a body has mapped—the breadth and resolution of possibility held as live. Distinct from modal fidelity (how truly the field tracks the structure); a field can be deep but distorted or shallow but accurate. A factor of modal freedom, not the whole of it. Defined at §5 and developed at §5.4.

**Modal Expression** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The externalized subset of a body’s modal field: a representation pressed outward into a medium—language, image, sound—so it can be transmitted to another body. A field always holds far more than it expresses. Expression is the vehicle by which representations reach other fields, become available for comparison and correction, and, when persisted into shared substrate, build the modal network. Defined at §5 and developed at §5.12.

**Modal Fidelity** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The accuracy axis of a modal field: how truly the field’s mapping tracks the modal structure, as distinct from modal depth (how much of the modal structure is mapped). A field can be deep but low-fidelity or shallow but high-fidelity. Correction and convergence increase fidelity; error and distortion reduce it. Defined at §5 and developed at §5.4.

**Modal Network** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The collective converging field: many individual modal fields pooled and interlinked—through modal expression and externalization into shared substrate—into one shared body of modal representations, queried, corrected, and inherited across bodies (its paradigm case is the internet). The collective counterpart to the individual modal field; what modal convergence moves toward the modal structure, and what pre-weights the fields of new bodies. Defined at §5 and developed at §5.13.

**Modal Weight** · *Definition within The Modal Apparatus.* The placement and force carried by a modal representation: how the represented branch is held—possible, impossible, necessary, contingent, or actual—and how strongly it bears on the body. Weights are often inherited through the modal network rather than computed firsthand and can therefore be mistaken. Correction and convergence raise fidelity by bringing a representation’s weight into line with the modal structure. Defined at §5 and developed at §5.2 and §5.4.

**Moral Predicates, Divine** · *Concept.* The classical moral predicates the tradition applies to God—*benevolent*, *just*, *merciful*, *loving*, *patient*, *faithful*, *gracious*—are manner-of-acting predicates: adverbial in grammar, requiring an act for the manner to modify. Acting requires the structural conditions of action—succession from not-acting to acting (T), a target distinct from the actor (S), a substantive agent who acts (Φ). The doctrine that strips T, S, Φ from divine being strips the conditions on which the moral predicates run; the reframings that preserve the predicate-names (analogical predication, indexing possibility to divine nature, identifying the being with the standard against which alternatives are measured) preserve the verbal predicates at the cost of the conditions their content depends on. *Benevolence* is the lead case: the Latin compound *bene volens* (*well-willing*), traced honestly, names what Nature is when subjects act on subjects to keep each other in being under symmetry-of-extraction. The doctrine’s God is not malevolent, not benevolent, not indifferent in any positive sense—the being is outside the field in which moral predicates have purchase, and what those predicates actually pick out is what Nature is when subjects mutually maintain one another. Established in §11.9.1.

**Moment-Individuation** · *Lemma toward Sufficiency of Structure.* Positions in an order are distinguished by their occupants, not by a bare thisness attaching to instants as such: where no state, arrangement, or bearing differs between two alleged moments, there is one moment under two names. Derived rather than posited, from the closure of the haecceitist exit at §2.4.7—what is offered as the distinctness is a label, and a label is not a difference—so its security is exactly that of the chapter’s anti-haecceitism and no more. The permutation test at §3.2.2 independently supports the no-bare-difference verdict without deriving the loaded types. Spent by the converse and the Modal Identity, and by the frozen-world and masking closures. It is not a sufficient premise for an ∅ reductio: the ∅ Reductio Boundary (§2.7.4) records the missing field-level co-failure bridge. Triconditional Cross-Entailment and the partial-overlap argument instead run through the same-realizer succession, extension, and persistence routes. Chapter 3 adds no role-to-type upgrade; that dependency boundary is recorded at §3.5.3. Established at §2.4.10.

**Mortality** · *Corollary of Drive and Identity.* The living process registering its own ending as a structural fact about itself: the closure every living current is organized against, folded back into a self-model deep enough to project itself toward its terminus. That this registration just is mortality is a functional proposal defended by fit. The present account does not soften the registration: a self-modeling configuration deep enough to register itself as the I that knows it will end is the configuration in which finitude becomes phenomenologically load-bearing. *See also* *Sein-zum-Tode*; *memento mori*; *maranasati*; *meditatio mortis*. Established in §5.9.

**Movement** · **M** · *Premise.* Change of position: one thing at a position and afterwards at another, having crossed what lay between. Movement is really possible (◇M), and M is one species of C, so ◇M entails ◇C. The premise is empirical rather than performative on purpose: soundness needs a true premise, not an indubitable one, and actual displacement supplies it. Aquinas’s broader premise of motion includes alteration as well as locomotion and does not alone entail ◇M. Supplies the second witness for □◇C and the second derivation of the Structural Requirement (§2.4.9). Established in §2.4.7.

**Mutual Containment** · *Corollary of §2.6.2–2.6.4.* Under the Operative-Role Bridge, any one of T, S, Φ doing its characteristic work in a concrete change-realizer requires the other two in that same realizer. The entailment is derived through the succession, extension, and persistence pivots and gathered by Triconditional Cross-Entailment, rather than obtained by renaming every thin order, distinction, or bearer as a loaded Condition or by distributing a field-level conclusion locally.

**Mutual Sustenance** · *Conditional political proposition.* Subjects exposed to shared conditions may have reason to support their maintenance. Durable convergence also depends on recognition of others’ standing, accountable institutions, and empirical conditions for cooperation; it is not a deduction from self-interest alone. *Convergent Individualism* names the proposal that individual pursuit can support shared maintenance under those conditions. Paired with Subsistence at the chapter-paradigm level. Established at the §6 chapter root.

**Obtain** · Said of a state of affairs: to be the case. “If that condition obtains” means *if that is how things are*. It does not mean *acquire*.

**Persistence’s Realizers** · *Lemma.* Persistent bearing is biconditional with directed succession and relational extension: Φ ↔ (T ∧ S). The two halves carry different prices and are paid separately: the T↔Φ half is the pivot’s own work, four lines running two in each direction, each refuting a distinct deflationary mimic, while the S half is carried on its own terms rather than derived from persistence. Earned at §2.6.

**Pick out** · Said of a term: to refer to, to have as what it names. That *Reality* picks out the whole within which anything is real is a claim about what the word names, not about a selection made among alternatives.

**Prima facie** · “At first appearance” (Latin); how something looks before the case for or against it has been heard. A prima facie reason can be outweighed by another.

**Primitive** · Taken as basic and not defined in terms of anything more fundamental. A claim about where an account starts, not about how crude it is.

**Profile** · A specified pattern—mathematical, physical, or structural—given by its elements and the conditions that define it. A profile is what a realization realizes; that a profile has a realization, and that a consequence follows from it, are separate questions (§3.5.6).

**Realizer** · Whatever occupies a role: what actually stands in it. To *realize* a role is to occupy it, and a *realization* is an instance of that occupying. The term fixes no kind of occupant—which things can fill which roles is argued rather than settled by the word (§1.4).

**Reason-Giving Instantiates Reasoning** · *Theorem.* Whenever a denial of reasoning is offered *for a reason*, the speaker treats at least one consideration as bearing on a conclusion, and that token instantiates the inferentially answerable transition it denies. No reason-giving denial can establish that reasoning never occurs. The theorem proves an instance, not a complete theory: a bare refusal, threat, associative transition, or unsupported assertion need not count as reasoning, and the result does not determine which non-discursive performances are genuinely reasons-responsive. Depends on Representational Minimum (§5.4) and the performative-witness method of Cartesian Certainty (§2.2). Earned at §5.6.

**Representational Minimum** · *Theorem.* Any tokened inquiry into whether representation occurs holds at least the content under consideration and its proposed denial apart long enough for one to be assessed against the other. An argumentative denial that any representation occurs therefore instantiates a held distinction and cannot eliminate representation from the episode in which the denial is considered. The theorem establishes one actual representational minimum—differentiated content held through an act of inquiry—and does not establish that the content is true, warranted, non-accidentally held, remembered accurately, or known, nor does it identify every discriminative response as representation. Depends on the performative-witness method of Cartesian Certainty (§2.2). Earned at §5.4.

**Resolution** · The level of detail at which a claim is made and defended. One thing can be picked out at more than one, so a rough characterization and a formal derivation may fix the same ground; a conclusion carries only at the resolution of the argument that earned it (§1.2).

**The Self-Application Fork** · *Theorem.* A global deflation of modality owes a coherent account of its own modal status. If contingent, it owes why a configuration at which it fails does not unmake it as an account of what modality actually is. If necessary, the object-language/meta-theory distinction must be drawn before that necessity is treated as an exception. Earned at §7.1.

**No Stable Zero-Extension** · *Theorem.* No stable zero-extension state is a state Nature can occupy: ¬◇(permanent ¬S) at cosmological scale. **The claim is strictly modal** and holds independently of which specific physics describes the approach to compression, so it neither selects among bounce, cyclic or other models nor depends on one succeeding. Earned at §4.6.

**Strict Actualization** · *Theorem.* From □(P → Q) and actual *P*, actual *Q* follows by the T axiom and modus ponens: *Q* is strictly guaranteed by the fully realized sufficient configuration rather than merely favored by it, and **neither *P* nor *Q* is thereby necessary simpliciter**. Only where □P is independently established does K yield □Q. Earned at §2.9.4.

**Structural Naturalism** · *Definition.* The name of the position this book defends. Naturalism holds that the natural world is all there is; it has traditionally had to take that world as a brute fact, with no account of why there is a structured world rather than none. Structural naturalism supplies that account from the inside: Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality are derived as the conditions any reality must instantiate, so the natural world is not merely all there is but could not have failed to be structured as it is. It is the completion of naturalism rather than a rival to it, and it revises nothing the sciences observe—metaphysics and physics are two directions on one inquiry (§4.1). Distinct from *physicalism*, which treats matter as basic where this treats the three Conditions as co-equal roles (§2.9.3); from *pantheism*, since Nature is credited with no personhood, mind, or divinity; from Spinozan *necessitarianism*, since the structure is necessary while its occupants remain contingent (§2.9.4); and from *structural realism*, the nearest neighbor in name, which claims that structure is what survives theory change rather than that three specific Conditions are necessary—the two converge substantially, since neither posits the Conditions as objects with intrinsic natures, and what stays open is whether Temporality, Spatiality and Substantiality are required of any relational fabric or a parochial slice of a richer one (§9.10). *See also* Nature; Identity of Reality and Nature.

**Nature** · *Definition.* The joint structure of Time, Space, and Substance: what any genuine change requires. Box-free at the definition; that the three hold of necessity, □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ), is a separately earned result. Not a totality of natural objects, nor an abstract framework Reality happens to possess, but the necessary structural constitution in virtue of which any Reality is possible. The completed line states this constitution as necessary at §2.9.6; the *Reality–Nature Identity* theorem establishes the identity of Reality and Nature at §2.8. *See also* Identity of Reality and Nature.

**The Self-Model as Mapped Region** · *Corollary of Identity.* If the I is an object in the recursion’s own field, it is a mapped region of that field, and a field is a fallible mapping of the modal structure (§5.4); the self-model therefore stands on the same two axes as any other region, modal depth and modal fidelity. Holding the modeled I apart from the modeling recursion is the co-present content of a single episode (§2.4.7), the structure the reflective witness of Change Is Actual (§2.2.1) already displays. Three consequences: introspection carries no privilege, being a readout of a mapped region (§5.3) that can be shallow or false, with sincerity securing neither; the self-model is corruptible from outside, since the region modeling the subject is not exempt from the against-mapping mode of wronging (§5.14), which is the structural form of manipulation aimed at what a person takes themselves to be; and what dissolves in ego dissolution is a mapped region rather than the mapper, the vantage persisting because it is the mapping and not a thing mapped. Established in §5.7.

**Necessary Occupancy** · *Corollary of Triconditional Identity and Exclusivity of Nature.* For any concrete individual thing to exist is for it to occupy the necessary structure: to be temporally ordered, spatially or relationally situated, and substantially borne as a determinate relatum. This is constitutive of what real concrete occupancy consists in, not a constraint imposed from outside; a putative concrete entity satisfying none of the Conditions fails to be an occupant rather than existing in an unusual way. Abstract descriptions remain abstractions of structural features rather than a second concrete domain. Follows from the Exclusivity of Nature theorem and the Triconditional Identity theorem. Established in §2.9.7.

**Necessary Possibility** · *Theorem.* Whatever is possible, its possibility is necessary; whatever is impossible, its impossibility is necessary—◇P → □◇P, with bilateral companion ¬◇P → □¬◇P. A proposition’s modal status, once fixed, does not vary across modal space. Earned at §2.1 as a theorem—rather than imported as an axiom—and set out line by line at §2.1.10; the literature’s S5 *Euclidean Axiom* (◇P → □◇P) is the same content the argument derives rather than assumes. Applied to the Cartesian certainty of change (◇C, §2.2), it lifts that certainty to the Necessary Possibility of Change (□◇C, §2.3). Established in §2.1.10.

**Necessary Possibility of Change** · *Lemma toward Triconditional Necessity.* The possibility of change is necessary: □◇C. The lift of the bare ◇C of §2.2 (Cartesian certainty of change) to its necessitated form by a single application of the Necessary Possibility theorem (§2.1.10, ◇P → □◇P) under modus ponens. It is stronger than ◇C—the possibility now holds across all of modal structure—yet weaker than the unconditional necessity of the Conditions (□(T∧S∧Φ), §2.5): it is the necessitated antecedent that the structural requirement □(◇C → T∧S∧Φ) (§2.4) discharges into that conclusion. *See* Cartesian Certainty (§2.2); Necessary Possibility (§2.1.10); Structural Requirement (§2.4). Established in §2.3.

**Necessity** · *Definition.* A proposition is necessary (□P) when it really could not fail to be the case. What is necessary does not lapse: there is no configuration with a square circle, no configuration with 2 + 2 = 5. Necessity can attach to possibility itself—□◇P is true just when the permission does not lapse in any configuration. Established in §1.2.

**Necessity entails Possibility** · **R1** · *Corollary of the T-Axiom and the Actuality–Possibility Principle.* Whatever is necessary is possible: □P → ◇P; by contraposition, whatever is not possible is not necessary (¬◇P → ¬□P). Falls out of the T-axiom (□P → P) composed with the *actuality implies possibility* principle of §1.2 (P → ◇P). The result carries the load wherever a necessity ascription has to answer to a verdict on possibility—invoked at §11.1 against the classical-theist reply that God’s necessity insulates God from the no-way-possible verdict. Established in §2.1.4.

**Necessity of Each Condition** · *Corollary of Triconditional Necessity.* Each of the three Conditions is instantiated in every possible world: Temporality is necessary (□T), Spatiality is necessary (□S), Substantiality is necessary (□Φ). Since necessity distributes over conjunction, □(T∧S∧Φ) is equivalent to □T ∧ □S ∧ □Φ. The Parasitic Negation reductios at §2.4.6–2.4.8 independently close alleged onsets from each Condition’s absence; they do not supply a second world-wise derivation. Established in §2.5.

**Necessity of Nature** · *Theorem.* Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality are necessarily co-instantiated: □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ). The headline theorem of the argument and the thesis of the book. Derived by modus ponens—the Necessary Possibility of Change (□◇C, §2.3) discharged against the Structural Requirement (□(◇C → T∧S∧Φ), §2.4) yields □(T∧S∧Φ); declared formally at §2.9.6 once the chapter’s defense of the premises and *Reality–Nature Identity* bridge (§2.8) have completed the line. Chapter 3 independently rebuilds the generic role-floor and substantial parts of the identity result while expressly leaving the global modal lift upstream.

***noesis noeseos noesis*** · “Thought thinking itself” (Greek); Aristotle’s description of the *Prime Mover* in *Metaphysics* XII.

**No-Surplus Criterion** · *Principle.* Where both relata of a claimed identity have already been established as necessary, their modal co-extension is uninformative: it follows from the necessity of each, holds between any two necessary truths whatever, and therefore distinguishes nothing. The content of an identity claim between such relata is exhausted by the absence of individuating content on either side—that specifying either already specifies the other, with nothing left over to mark them as two. Two consequences: the biconditional notation *understates* such a result rather than overstating it, so a reader who reads only the operators has read past the claim; and a refutation must target the no-surplus claim directly, since exhibiting a world in which the sides come apart is unavailable in principle rather than merely difficult. Governs the identity family of §2.6.6–2.6.10, with the Modal Identity as its principal worked instance. A criterion for reading results of this shape rather than a further result about Reality; it spends nothing beyond the necessity of the relata established at §2.3 and §2.5. Established in §2.6.9.

**Null State (∅)** · *Definition.* Absolute nothingness. Not a state of Reality; the absence of any state. Distinguished from vacuum (which is structured emptiness within Reality) and from absence-of-X (which is a determinate fact within Reality). Can’t be a contrast class for Reality because it can’t be specified (§2.7.1).

**One Channel** · *Corollary of Language.* Externalizing a region of one modal field into another is a single operation, not a family of them: the same transfer builds shared knowledge (§5.4), carries a life’s mappings past its close (§5.9), and corrupts a field (§5.14). There is no second channel reserved for the last, so deception is not a misuse of some faculty adjacent to language but the constitutive operation of language run against the receiver. Two consequences follow. Truthfulness is internal to the practice rather than a virtue added to it, since the practice is what builds a receiver’s field and a corrupted transfer is that same building done wrongly. And lossiness can’t be what makes a transfer deceptive: transfer is lossy by constitution and lossiness has no direction, so fidelity is a separate axis—a perfectly faithful transfer of a false necessity is the most damaging case rather than the least. Established in §5.12.

**Ontological Identity** · *Theorem.* Being in Nature ↔ T ∧ S ∧ Φ at the realizer-level structure of genuine Change. Nature read from the side of concrete being: a participant in the change-hosting field persists distinguished in S and succeeding in T; there is no further concrete residue. The theorem does not exclude abstracta, atemporal entities, or candidate external grounds by definition; those proposals are tested downstream. The third of three readings composing the Triconditional Identity (§2.6.10); together they are three logical-categorical readings of one Nature: modal (necessity), nomological (law), ontological (being). Established in §2.6.8.

**Operative-Role Bridge** · *Constitutive Premise.* When a modal-core Condition is claimed to be concretely operative rather than merely represented, modeled, or abstractly specified, its characteristic work must be realized: T orders actual succession, S separates occupiable positions across a crossable interval, and Φ makes a stage a continuation. The premise does not derive all three from any one thin predicate. It is not needed for the field-level theorem □(T∧S∧Φ); it is spent by the stronger same-realizer cross-entailments and identity readings. Established in §2.6.1.

**Parasitic Negation** · *Lemma toward Negation Seal.* Let X be one of any of the three Conditions. The natural-language negation associated with each domain—‘never’ / ‘no first moment’ for T, ‘nowhere’ / ‘no place’ for S, ‘no causal medium’ / ‘no persistence-being’ for Φ—operates as a quantifier internal to X, not as an external denial of X. No world coherently describable as containing the emergence of X from its own absence is available, since any putative emergence would itself instantiate X-structure. Paired with the *Negation Seal* result: a candidate world described as lacking X is either incoherent or has truth-conditions that already require X-structure—no third option. Established in §2.1.5.

**Perfection, Divine** · *Concept.* The maxima-composition attribute: God possesses every great-making property to the maximum compatible degree and lacks every limitation. *Perfectio* (from *perficere*) names the state of having no deficiency and no remainder. The doctrine is the synthesizing capstone of the classical attribute system—what holds the individual attributes together as the description of one being rather than a list. The argument runs the perfection-composition test as a three-horn argument: the perfections compose either by an *exclusive standard* (each defined by negation of a contingent feature, jointly producing the ∅-equivalent foreclosed by No Supernature), by a *propagating standard* (each defined by maximization along its own scale, producing incoherence where the scales conflict—maximum power vs. maximum simplicity, maximum knowledge of contingents vs. maximum immutability), or by an *analogy escape* (each predicate analogically related to its creaturely cousin, with the analogy unable to bear the structural load of composing a single being). All three horns close. *See also* Maximally Great Being; Aseity Forfeiture; Three-Horn Dilemma. Established in §11.2.4.

**Perfect-Being Theology** · *Concept.* The method that identifies great-making properties and attributes them to God at the maximum degree compatible with one another. It generates the perfect-being or Maximally Great Being candidate that the modal ontological argument asks the reader to treat as possible; it does not itself establish that the resulting set of attributes is compossible. The distinction matters throughout the Chapter 11 perfection analysis: the method can select the attributes while the structural argument still tests whether one being can bear them together. *See also* Maximally Great Being; Perfection, Divine; Greatness. Established in §11.1 and §11.2.4.

**Performative Self-Refutation** · *Named Corollary.* A denial that instantiates what it denies. The denial of Cartesian Certainty (◇C, §2.2) is performative self-refutation: to deny that change is possible is itself to change one’s epistemic state, which presupposes the possibility of change. The denial of Necessary Possibility (◇P → □◇P, §2.1.3) is similarly self-refuting once the real/Reality identity is granted.

**Permutation-Invariant Bearing** · *Lemma.* Cross-Interval Persistence requires a real continuity structure spanning a transition, not numerical identity of a privileged object or particle trajectory. Endurantist objects, perduring wholes, counterpart relations, fields, permutation-invariant states, conserved quantities, and process structures may occupy the bearer role if they make the later state a continuation of the same change. The modal proof is neutral among those realizers. Established in §2.4.8.

**Persistence** · *Concept.* Staying the same through change: a thing *persists*, *endures*, or *remains* across a transition, as a river persists while its water turns over. *Endures* and *persists* carry technical readings in the philosophy of time (perdurantism and endurantism). Established in §1.5.8.

**Physical Invariance** · *Theorem.* A complete physical profile can’t vary independently of its proved invariants: if $M\models Q$, every really possible physical realization of *M* carries *Q*. Nomological necessity is therefore statable within the one modal field as $\Box\forall x(\operatorname{Realizes}(x,L)\rightarrow Q(x))$, the antecedent marking the profile held fixed, rather than as quantification over law-varying worlds. The result relocates physical contingency instead of removing it—a profile shown sufficient for an invariant can’t have that invariant reassigned while the profile is held fixed—and sorts laws by status: profile-constitutive invariants, effective laws carrying their boundary conditions in the antecedent, and empirical regularities with no proof of sufficiency. Earned at §3.5.6. Depends on Invariant Realization for the consequence and Necessary Possibility for availability.

**Physical** · *Definition.* Occupying T ∧ S ∧ Φ. Anything that is in time, somewhere in space, and persists as a causal relatum is physical. The Ontological Identity (§2.6.8) establishes that there is no residue beyond the triad—anything that is a being in Nature instantiates T∧S∧Φ.

**Substantiality** · **Φ** · *Condition.* The formal Condition of Reality such that exchange is necessarily possible. It is not stuff that occupies T and S, but the structural feature that lets there be the-same-thing-across-moments at all. Its three properties are *Distinctness* (relata of interaction are non-identical), *Holding* (the carrier-role is genuinely occupied rather than empty), and *Persistence* (remains through the transition it carries). Whether the occupant also *transmits* by productive causation is *Transmission*, a realization-tier question the modal derivations do not spend (§4.4). Chapter 1 introduces the corresponding ordinary term, Substance; Chapter 2 introduces and defends this formal register. Formal variable Φ. Established in §2.4.

**Possibility** · *Definition.* A proposition is possible (◇P) when it really could be the case. Distinguished in §1.2.1 from *logically possible* (broader: every real possibility is logically possible, not the reverse), *conceivable* (a reach of imagination), *epistemically possible* (a fact about a knower’s evidence), *nomologically possible* (narrower on the standard reading, though our characterisations of the laws may misfire in either direction), and *probable* (sorts what is in the running). Necessary truths count as possible. Established in §1.2.

**Possible World** · *Concept.* A complete and consistent way the world could be. Possibility is a feature of Reality here, not an external accessibility relation; possible worlds are alternative configurations of the structural medium, not separate substances.

**Polity** · *Concept.* A political community considered as an organized bearer of shared institutions, public direction, and governance. Chapter 6 uses the word where the political community itself is the relevant subject; it is not a prescribed substitute for every ordinary use of *state*, *government*, *political system*, or *shared arrangement*. Established in §6 and developed at §6.3.

**Principle of Modal Invariance** · *Principle.* What is structurally necessary holds across all of Reality, including across cosmological cycles. Established in §2.1.7 and used to license the macro-structural transmission across the bounce in §4.6.

**Probability** · *Concept.* A measure assigning real values in [0, 1] to members of a sigma-algebra of events over a sample space. Distinguished from real possibility at §1.2.1: probability sorts what is already in the running; it does not decide what could be. Objective chance presupposes real possibility and does not manufacture it (§2.9.5). Every probability is conditional on the modal structure that fixes the sample space; probability questions are asked within the frame, not of it. Probability precision is bounded above by modal-representation resolution (§10.1.9).

**Productive Causation** · *Concept.* *See* Efficient Causation. The book uses the two expressions for the causal role in which a source brings about a concrete effect, as distinct from constitution, form, purpose, and non-causal grounding (§2.4).

**PSR (Principle of Sufficient Reason)** · *Principle.* Every fact has an explanation. The structural argument honors PSR for Nature—Nature exists because non-existence (∅) is not a coherent alternative—but rejects the demand for an explanation outside Nature, because any such explanation would be a state, and ∅ is not a state.

**Real** · *Concept.* What is the case. The real and Reality are co-extensive: there is nothing real outside Reality, and Reality is exhausted by what is real.

**Reality** · *Definition.* The totality of what is real. Fixed by the role rather than by any claim about what fills it: whether Reality is matter or mind or number, one or many, created or not, is left open here. Has no contrast class—nothing is outside Reality, because anything that could be specified would be part of it (§1.1). *See also* Reality–Nature Identity.

**Reality–Nature Identity** · *Theorem.* Reality is Nature. Not two things that necessarily accompany one another, and not partners in an arrangement: one thing, named twice. N = R. The identity is stated at the modal-field and maximal-totality resolution the derivation reaches; that Reality *is* Nature, rather than being necessarily constituted by it, rests additionally on the constitutive reading of concrete occupancy and Structural Individuation. It does not show that no candidate within the field can claim explanatory priority over it; that role is tested at §2.9.7. Depends on Triconditional Necessity, the Triconditional Identity, and Structural Individuation. Established in §2.8.

**Registration Precedes Transfer** · *Corollary of Sexuality.* For one field to take another subject as an object, it must register that subject as an occupant genuinely apart from itself rather than as a modification of its own state—co-present mutual exteriority in the sense fixed at §2.4.7, obtaining between subjects rather than within a single episode. Attraction is the earliest register in the cascade where this holds, and it runs prior to sign, norm, and propositional content. Two consequences: the two-subject structure morality operates on (§5.14) is inherited rather than constituted there, since what morality adds is the weighting and not the second subject; and the Two Modes of Wronging are already available in pre-linguistic form, a body’s broadcasts being able to misrepresent what a coupling requires or leads to as readily as a sentence can. Transfer (§5.12) and convergence (§5.4) presuppose the containment rather than establishing it. The result neither derives Spatiality nor makes sexuality the origin of intersubjectivity as such. Established in §5.8.

**Revised God** · *Concept.* An umbrella category for theological candidates that revise the classical conception by placing divine life within temporal, relational, or otherwise structurally embedded roles. Process, open, and panentheist theologies supply different versions; the label does not treat them as one doctrine. Such a candidate may remain theologically significant while incurring dependence on the structure it inhabits. *See also* Classical God; Scriptural God; Three Conceptions of God. Developed at §10.3.3 and §11.10.

**S5 Axiom** · *Principle.* The modal logic in which ◇□P ↔ □P and ◇P ↔ □◇P both hold. The standard logic for metaphysical necessity. The present argument is compatible with S5, but the current proof runs the needed invariance through the Necessary Possibility theorem (§2.1.3, §2.1.10) and applies it to Cartesian Certainty (§2.2), yielding the Necessary Possibility of Change lemma (□◇C, §2.3). As with the Euclidean Axiom, the *Principle* label is the literature’s classification rather than this book’s: S5 is not assumed here, since the invariance of Range(R) is the frame condition S5 encodes, and that standing capacity is grounded in Reality’s maximality (§1.1). An opponent who rejects S5 therefore does not thereby reach the conclusion (§2.1.10).

**Scriptural God** · *Concept.* The personal, historical deity represented as acting at times, in places, and through media: speaking, appearing, responding, commanding, creating, or entering covenant. The category tracks the structural commitments of those action-predicates without claiming that every scriptural tradition gives them the same theological interpretation. *See also* Classical God; Revised God; Three Conceptions of God. Engaged at §11.9.2 and §11.10.

***Sein-zum-Tode*** · Heidegger’s “being-toward-death.”

***Soziale Marktwirtschaft*** · The German social market economy, invoked in the political application of the framework.

**Space** · **S** · *Condition.* The occupiable separateness that actually obtains: the extended interval across which positions stand genuinely apart. Chapter 1 introduces Space as a member of the Time/Space/Substance triad; Chapter 2 formalizes its structural role as Spatiality (S). Established in §1.4.

**Spacetime** · *Concept.* The physical realization of T↔S—Time and Space compose into a single manifold. Established in §4.5.

**Spatiality** · **S** · *Condition.* The formal Condition of Reality such that distinction is necessarily possible. It is not a container of locations, but the structural feature without which distinction could not run. Its three properties are *Extension* (positions separated by a real interval), *Exclusivity* (positions exclusively occupiable), and *Traversability* (the interval is crossable). Chapter 1 introduces the corresponding ordinary term, Space; Chapter 2 introduces and defends this formal register. Formal variable S. Established in §2.4.

***Spiritus*** · Latin for breath, spirit; the structural concept that the framework reads as a phenomenological description of Φ-persistence in self-modeling configurations.

**State–Realizer Instantiation** · *Constitutive Premise.* If a structural feature is actually instantiated in a concrete state, and that state is a state of realizer g, then g instantiates the feature in that state. This licenses the state horn of the encoding argument without transferring represented content to its bearer: only the structure of the concrete occurrence is inherited. Established in §2.6.7.

**Structural Individuation** · *Constitutive Premise.* Whatever individuates one concrete item from another is real differentiating structure. If an alleged qualitative property, relation, quiddity, or primitive thisness changes which concrete item is present, it belongs to the item’s complete structural profile; if it makes no difference, it does not individuate. The premise does not make every individuation spatial. Relational Distinctness supplies the narrower result that positional individuation requires relational extension. Established in §2.4.9; spent by Reality–Nature Identity and the unicity arguments.

**Structural Requirement** · *Theorem.* Under every modal evaluation, if Change is really possible, Reality is constituted by the three Conditions: □(◇C → T ∧ S ∧ Φ). The spine’s load-bearing theorem: discharged against the Necessary Possibility of Change (□◇C, §2.3) by modus ponens to yield the Necessity of Nature theorem (□(T∧S∧Φ)). Distinct from the *Structural Role* entry, which names what T, S, and Φ each are. *See* Necessary Possibility of Change; Necessity of Nature theorem. Established in §2.4.

**Structural Role** · *Definition.* A function any possible medium must perform for change to occur. T, S, Φ are the three structural roles. The roles are distinguished from their occupiers: any configuration that performs the role is the role for that configuration. Their joint field-level necessity is distinct from their operative co-requirement: under the Operative-Role Bridge, each role doing concrete change-realizing work requires the other two in that same realizer. The identity readings add their own no-surplus argument; thin roles considered in isolation do not cross-entail by definition.

**Subsistence** · *Political-structural definition.* Ordinarily, continued existence or the means by which it is maintained. Stipulated here in a political sense for a relation in which members and institutions maintain the shared conditions of agency-bearing life and effective participation—explanatory shorthand, not an inference from etymology and not a claim that a polity is literally an organism or a single subject. Distinct from **Subsistent Grounding**, the metaphysical result the political term rhymes with rather than restates. Established at the §6 chapter root; paired with Mutual Sustenance.

**Subsistent Grounding** · *Argument, §2.9.3 (renamed from “Why the View Is Not Fundamentality Physicalism”).* the three Conditions are co-constitutive rather than one-way grounded on Φ: none of the three is a privileged floor the other two rest on, each subsisting only because the other two do. Takes Aquinas’s own *ipsum esse subsistens* and earns it by composition and mutual dependence rather than by the simplicity classical theism required. The book’s central instance of a recurring pattern, mutual holding with no privileged floor, that recurs at other scales and registers without being the same claim at each: the bare modal vocabulary (§1.2.6), Reality’s own grounding (§1.1.3), the cosmological cycle (§4.6), bounded biological self-production (§4.8), collectively held knowledge (§5.4), the political register (**Subsistence**, above), and felt as awe in the phenomenological register (§5.16). Distinct from **Subsistence**, the Chapter 6 political term; the two are meant to rhyme, not to merge. Established in §2.9.3.

**Substance** · **Φ** · *Condition.* The persisting carrier that actually runs through change: that which holds and transmits causal properties across transitions. Chapter 1 introduces Substance as a member of the Time/Space/Substance triad; Chapter 2 formalizes its structural role as Substantiality (Φ). Established in §1.4.

**Substrate** · *Concept.* The conditions for life-as-agency: what the Right to Life protects at §6.1 and what Belonging carries across a boundary at §6.2. Distinguished throughout Chapter 6 from *content*—cultural expression, religious practice, language, custom, governance form—which doesn’t cross: what crosses a border is the substrate, not a culture. Takes the definite article and the compounds built on it (*substrate-only*, *the substrate register*). Not the ordinary descriptive uses at §6.1 (*bare biological substrate*, *the educational substrate*), which aren’t this term. Established at §6.2.

**Succession** · *Concept.* One of the three structural requirements of Change. Identified with T.

**Succession’s Realizers** · *Lemma.* Directed succession is biconditional with relational extension and persistent bearing in the same realizer: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ). Full T requires differentiated positions across its order and a bearer carrying direction between them; concrete crossable S occupied by a Φ-bearer supplies the ordered crossing that T names. Earned at §2.6.2.

**No Divine Addition** · *Theorem.* Any God claimed to be actual or necessary must be possible; any possible God must have a determinate way to be. Every determinate way belongs to Reality–Nature. By constitutive non-addition, the candidate is Nature itself, Nature in a determinate operation, or an abstraction of such an articulation—not an independently constituted being outside Nature or added inside it. Divine essence does not reopen either location because No Unconditioned Essence closes structural priority over Nature. If no determinate content answers to the description, no possible divine candidate has been specified. Earned in §11.10.

**No Outside Selector** · *Theorem.* No real selector stands outside Nature or constitutes an independently formed addition within it. A real selector and any determinate selection relation are aspects of Reality–Nature. They may explain which subconfiguration obtains, conditional on the selector and relation, but they can’t explain total actuality from an exterior or surplus position. A concrete selector or operation is the three Conditions in determinate operation; an abstract or atemporal selector remains an internal structure and must state its relation to concrete actuality; an unspecified selector supplies no selection. Earned in §10.4.

**No Unconditioned Essence** · *Theorem.* Any essence real enough to ground modal truth must have a determinate way to be. That way belongs to Reality–Nature and is the field, a determinate content of the three Conditions at the resolution appropriate to what it is, or an abstraction of such an articulation. Essence may be explanatorily prior to modal truths about a thing, but no essence is structurally prior or additional to Nature. An alleged essence with no determinate configuration specifies no possible ground. Earned in §7.2.1.

**No Supernature** · *Theorem.* No concrete act, change, experience, intervention, causal production, or selection occurs outside the three Conditions; a proposed deity performing such work is the Conditions in determinate operation. A set withdrawing every determinate feature and relation supplies no possible subject or ground. No Divine Addition closes an independently constituted divine remainder outside or added inside Nature; No Outside Selector closes exterior or surplus selection of total actuality; No Unconditioned Essence closes structural priority by divine essence. A determinate atemporal or analogical ground may remain meaningful only as an abstract structure of Nature whose personal predicates and relation to concrete actuality must be earned. Established in §11.10; previewed at §11.1.

***Sui generis*** · “Of its own kind” (Latin); belonging to no wider category, so not explicable as an instance of something more general.

**Supervenience** · *Concept.* One range of facts is fixed by another: A *supervenes on* B when there can be no difference in A without some difference in B. The supervenient (A) varies only as the subvenient (B) varies; the canonical case is the mental supervening on the physical. Established in §1.5.4.

**Temporality** · **T** · *Condition.* The formal Condition of Reality such that succession is necessarily possible. It is not a container in which events occur, but the structural feature without which succession could not run. Its three properties are *Asymmetry* (before/after is irreversible), *Transitivity* (ordering composes globally), and *Directionality* (before-states carry influence to after-states), the last a realization-tier question the modal derivations do not spend—they spend Asymmetry and Transitivity alone (§2.4.6), matching Substantiality’s own Transmission restriction below. Chapter 1 introduces the corresponding ordinary term, Time; Chapter 2 introduces and defends this formal register. Formal variable T. Established in §2.4.

**Three Conceptions of God** · *See* Classical God; Revised God; Scriptural God. For the method that generates a maximally-great candidate, *see also* Perfect-Being Theology; Maximally Great Being.

**Three Frustrations of Will** · *Corollary of Will.* A willing can fail to reach what it is directed at in three structurally distinct ways, and the difference is not one of degree. R cannot admit the line: the frustration is structural and permanent, since impossibility does not vary (§2.1.5). R can admit the line, but it is not locally reachable: global standing and local reachability are different relations, and the second varies while the first does not, so the frustration is real, contingent, and answerable by a change of position. Or R can admit the line and it is locally reachable but absent from this field: nothing outside the being forecloses it, it has simply not been mapped, so the frustration is a mapping failure rather than a modal one. Only the third is answerable by the being whose willing it is, and answering it is what modal depth consists in. Depth can’t alter what R can admit; mistaking which frustration is operating—treating a structural impossibility as a personal deficiency, or an unmapped option as a closed one—is its own failure. Established in §5.11; the two an agent can inflict on another are taken up as the Two Modes of Wronging (§5.14).

**Conditional Closure** · *Concept.* Given the defended role analysis, a determinate active-transcendent ground either retains predicates that instantiate the modal-core Conditions and is thereby located within Nature, or withdraws every differentiating feature and incurs the ∅-like specification failure. Rejecting the analysis challenges the premise rather than furnishing a third ontological horn. The strict zero-content conception is impossible under the analysis; not every description called *God* is declared contradictory. Established in §11.10.

**Through w* Argument** · *Concept.* A name the apparatus previously carried for a mirror-of-Plantinga route to □¬MGB. The book does not run that route. It reaches □¬CG₀ for the separately specified contentless-God description by specification failure at §11.10 and modal duality, never by asserting ◇□¬CG₀. *See* The Contentless God Has No Referent.

**Time** · **T** · *Condition.* The occupiable succession that actually runs: the order in which moments are distinct, directed, and lasting. Chapter 1 introduces Time as a member of the Time/Space/Substance triad; Chapter 2 formalizes its structural role as Temporality (T). Established in §1.4.

***tota simul*** · “All at once” (Latin); Boethius’s name for the eternal present in which God comprehends all time.

**Transition Closure** · *Theorem.* A state lacking local transition-capacity cannot produce or transition into a state that has it; local transition-capacity cannot switch on within a history from a state that lacks it. **The conclusion is one-way and local.** The converse does not follow from onset closure, and the result does not exclude a quiet stretch in which no change occurs while the capacity remains. Earned at §3.1.2.

**Triconditional Closure** · *Proposition.* The three per-Condition closures are one closure read three ways. A negation of any Condition from outside it describes no condition at all—a “before” Time, an “outside” Space, a “beyond” Substance name nothing—and each Condition draws its own conjunct of □(T∧S∧Φ). Each reading forecloses only the *from-outside* negation. Earned at §4.6.

**Triconditional Cross-Entailment** · *Theorem.* Under the Operative-Role Bridge, Nature read from the derived co-requirement among the three Conditions doing concrete work in one change-realizer: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ), S ↔ (T ∧ Φ), Φ ↔ (T ∧ S), with pairwise results T↔S, S↔Φ, T↔Φ. The route is not domain-construction, definition by mutual mention, or field-to-local inheritance. The succession, extension, and persistence pivots show in turn that operative T requires differentiated positions and a bearer, operative S requires an ordered crossing and an occupier, and operative Φ requires an ordered interval and differentiated states. Abstract order, geometry, or bearing that fails those criteria is not promoted into a Condition. It does not assert unrestricted entailment among thin modal-core predicates. The second of three readings composing the Triconditional Identity (§2.6.10). Established in §2.6.7.

**Triconditional Identity** · *Theorem.* Nature under three coordinated readings: the necessary field-level conjunction, the Operative-Role Bridge-indexed same-realizer co-requirement, and the ontological reading under the No-Surplus Criterion. The first does not entail the second, and neither by itself establishes identity; each reading carries its stated premises. Where those premises are granted, the generic identities are N ↔ □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ), N ↔ □◇C, and □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ) ↔ □◇C. *Fact of Nature* survives as a local descriptive phrase, not the theorem’s name. Established in §2.6.10; carried forward through the completed line at §2.9.6.

**Triconditional Necessity** · *Theorem.* Reality is necessarily temporal, spatial, and substantial, because the possibility of Change is necessary and requires those three Conditions. This stage establishes their joint necessity: □(T∧S∧Φ). It is a stage, not the terminus: Stage 1 establishes that the possibility of change is necessary, □◇C (§2.3); Stage 2 is reached here; Stage 3 is the Reality–Nature Identity, that Reality and Nature are one and the same. Established in §2.5.

**Truthmaker** · Whatever it is in the world in virtue of which a true claim is true. A truthmaker question asks what a truth answers to, not how the truth is known.

**Two Modes of Wronging** · *Corollary of Wrong.* No wrong alters whether R can admit a line, since impossibility does not vary and no agent confers it (§2.1.5). A corrosion of a subject against its own registered aversion therefore operates in exactly one of two modes, corresponding to the second and third Frustrations of Will (§5.11). *Against reach*: a really possible line is made unavailable from where the subject stands—coercion, confinement, deprivation, exclusion. *Against mapping*: the field the subject navigates by is corrupted along any axis it registers—a real line concealed, a line that is not there supplied, what a line requires misrepresented (X necessary for Y when it is not), or what a line leads to misrepresented (Y will follow from X when it will not). Both corrode the same thing, the subject navigating its own field, which is why they are one kind of wrong rather than two. Corruptions of the contingency axis are self-limiting under action, since compliance tests them; corruptions of the necessity axis are self-sealing, since obedience furnishes no counter-instance. Neither mode requires that the subject notice. Established in §5.14; inherited by §6 as the standard against which shared arrangements are assessed.

**The Two Axes of Participation** · *Conditional political proposition.* Nothing an arrangement does alters Range(R); what it can alter is a subject’s local *reach* among the configurations R admits and the subject’s *mapping* of what that reach affords. These are the second and third Frustrations of Will (§5.11) and they are independent—a line locally reachable but unmapped is as absent from selection as a line mapped but out of reach—so maximum possibility is evaluated across both axes rather than reach alone. An arrangement that widens reach while corrupting mapping has not moved toward it. The axes do not admit the same evidence: reach failures appear in what subjects can’t do and can report, while mapping failures on the necessity axis are self-sealing, since complying with a false requirement furnishes no counter-instance. Education, inquiry, and truthful public speech therefore belong to the political subject matter directly rather than as instruments of reach. The result supplies no cardinal measure and prices no trade between the axes. Established in §6.

**Type / Token** · *Definition.* Type: a structural pattern. Token: an instance of the pattern. The structural argument fixes the type; tokens are the locus at which novelty enters Reality (§4.7).

**Unity, Divine** · *Concept.* The classical attribute that God is one—not one among many, but uniquely one. *Unitas* unfolds in three classical sub-claims: simplicity (no metaphysical parts), uniqueness (no second God), and uniqueness-as-such (no possible second God). The argument honors the structural pressure each sub-claim reaches for and shows that none reaches a God. Simplicity, pressed honestly, names the absence of composability, which Nature itself instantiates as the necessary structural ground (§11.2.1). Uniqueness names the structural feature that the necessary structure has no contrast class outside itself (§1.1). Uniqueness-as-such is the modal claim that nothing else could occupy the role, which the Triconditional Identity theorem already establishes for Nature, leaving no role for a second occupant. The doctrine’s unity-language is exactly the structural feature Nature has been shown to instantiate; the relabeling move (‘the necessary structure is God’) changes the word while conceding the substance. *See also* Aseity Forfeiture. Established in §11.2.2.

**via negativa** · “The negative way” (Latin); apophatic theology, defining God by what God is not.

**Way–Possibility Convertibility** · *Lemma toward Triconditional Necessity.* For any P: P is possible iff there is a determinate way for P to be the case (◇P ↔ ∃ way(P)); equivalently, P is impossible iff there is no such way. Possibility and way are extensionally convertible—each ranges over the same candidates, and neither is reduced to the other. Determinacy supplies difference at role-resolution. Direction requires the separately defended directed-arrangement reading of *way*; bearing requires the separate realizer premise. The lemma therefore does not by itself yield T ∧ S ∧ Φ or transfer necessity from “□” to the Conditions. Used at §7.2.1 and §11.2.1 under that restricted reading. Established in §3.2.5.

**Witness** · An actual case offered to establish that something is possible. Since whatever is actual is possible, exhibiting one settles the possibility; the witness does that work by occurring, not by being described (§2.2).

# Dependency Map

This section is for **AI assistants** reading this single-file edition. It is **not**
part of the published book's argument and does not appear in the print or web chapter
list. It records each named result — what it states, where it lives, what it
**Depends On** / **Used By**, and (per row) a **Trace** blurb plus **Engages**
when the section argues *about* a rival rather than deriving *from* it.
**Depends On** is proof-upstream only; **Engages** is not a dependency.
Human readers may use it too; when it and the manuscript disagree, the
manuscript wins.

**Depends On is the primary direction; read it first.** *Used By* is its
inversion and carries no information *Depends On* does not — it exists to answer
propagation ("if this changed, what would break?") without walking the graph. In
this copy, rows with more than 12 dependents give a count instead of a list:
past that point the enumeration only restates that the result is foundational,
and the omitted rows were a quarter of this section's length. To trace a specific
path into such a result, walk **Depends On** upward from the downstream result
you care about. The vault copy of the dependency map holds the
uncapped graph.

For chapter-level presupposes/establishes cards, see **Appendix C: Derivation Map**
in the book above (the human-facing derivation map in the book itself).

### Parasitic Negation

- **Type:** Lemma  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 2010500
- **Section:** §2.1 (2.1 The S5 Pipeline)
- **Statement:** For each of T, S, and Φ, a claim that the Condition begins from its own absence presupposes that Condition in the proposed onset. The ground is general: an onset from domain-external absence is itself a change, and change requires all three Conditions, so the proposed onset presupposes the Condition it claims to introduce. Per Condition: a first moment requires temporal order, a first placing requires positional structure, and a first production requires a bearer across the transition. Domain-internal absence may be coherent; emergence of the domain from domain-external absence is not. **Feeds into:** Negation Seal (§2.1.5 The S5 Bottleneck)
- **Chapter:** 2 The Argument
- **Depends On:** Change (C); Temporality (T); Spatiality (S); Substantiality (Φ)

### Transition Closure

- **Type:** Theorem  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 2010600
- **Section:** §3.1.2 (3.1 Necessary Possibility of Change: Stress-Tested)
- **Statement:** A state lacking local transition-capacity cannot produce or transition into a state that has it. The temporal conclusion is unconditional: local transition-capacity cannot switch on within a history from a state that lacks it. The converse does not follow from onset closure: a final transition can be available from its source even if the resulting terminal state has no further local transition-capacity.

### A Quiddity Is Not a Residue

- **Type:** Proposition  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 2080015

- **Statement:** A quiddity offered as the concrete ground of role-occupancy faces a fork. If it supplies no differentiating structure, it does not individuate the realizers at all. Bare non-identity names no third way between making a difference and making none. The proposition does not refute categorical character; it establishes that categorical character cannot be both concretely individuating and nonstructural.

### The Movement Line

- **Type:** Argument  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 2040012
- **Section:** §2.4 (2.4 Structural Requirement)
- **Statement:** 1. *Movement.* Movement is really possible. ◇M. (§2.4.7) 1. *Necessary Possibility.* Whatever is really possible is necessarily possible. ◇P → □◇P. (§2.1.10) 1. From (1) and (2): □◇M. 1. *Containment.* A displacement occupies a before and an after (T), crosses an interval between positions (S), and is undergone by what persists across it (Φ). ### ∅ Reductio Boundary

- **Type:** Diagnostic  **Status:** Revised 2026-09-14  **Order:** 2070210
- **Section:** §2.7 (2.7 Nothing to Consider)
- **Statement:** 1. Suppose ¬□◇C. Then there is a possible world w₀ in which ◇C fails: change isn’t even possible at w₀. 1. By the Modal Identity (§2.6.6), □(◇C ↔ (T∧S∧Φ)), read at the **modal-core resolution** fixed in §2.4. So at w₀, ¬◇C entails ¬(T∧S∧Φ): at least one modal-core Condition fails. This isn’t yet the absence of generic directed order, difference, and bearing, and therefore not yet ∅. 1. The argument now stops. Mutual Containment (§2.6.5) says that when any one Condition operates in a concrete change-realizer, the other two are implicated in that same realizer. At w₀, however, no change-realizer is available. The theorem neither says that any one field-level failure entails all three failures nor licenses transfer from an empty operative domain to the modal field. 1. **Conditional continuation only.** Add Field Co-Failure: at field level, the failure of any one modal-core Condition entails the failure of all three. Then w₀ lacks Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality together. 1. Add the further no-free-standing-residue thesis: nothing abstract, analogical, or otherwise structured can stand when all three modal-core Conditions fail. Only then does w₀ collapse into ∅; the Incoherence of ∅ (§2.7.2) excludes it. 1. ∴ **Conditionally**, Field Co-Failure plus no free-standing residue yields □◇C. Without those added premises, no reductio follows.
- **Chapter:** 2 The Argument
- **Depends On:** Modal Identity; Mutual Containment (scope boundary); Incoherence of ∅; Field Co-Failure (unestablished); No-Free-Standing-Residue (unestablished)
- **Used By:** —
- **Established By:** §2.7 (2.7 Nothing to Consider)

### Grounding-Contact Trilemma

- **Type:** Disjunction  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 2080460
- **Section:** 10.4 What the Rivals Carried
- **Statement:** What does an ultimate ground supply that Nature doesn’t already? - **If it supplies only abstract or atemporal grounding content,** then it is an abstract structure within Nature, not an exterior ground. If it is invoked to explain concrete actuality, the relation between those resolutions is still owed. - **If it is concrete, or does concrete work,** then it is T, S, and Φ in determinate operation; neither route adds an independently constituted item to Nature. *Priced by* Necessary Occupancy (§2.9.7) for a concrete ground; Concrete-Entity Test (§2.4) for a concrete operation. - **If it supplies neither determinate content nor a determinate grounding relation,** then it supplies no ground at all. So the direct Thomist identification of classical *ipsum esse subsistens* with □(T∧S∧Φ) cannot be sustained while the classical type-level denials remain intact. Retaining determinate analogical content yields an internal abstract-grounding proposal, not a second source behind Nature. Dropping the denials yields a revised aspect of Nature. **Dependency routes:** exhaustiveness of the three horns—Ground-Candidate Partition (§3.5.5); abstract or atemporal grounding—The Grounding Conditional (§3.1.5) and No Unconditioned Essence (§7.2.1); concrete ground—Necessary Occupancy (§2.9.7) and Reality–Nature Identity (§2.8); concrete operation—the Concrete-Entity Test (§2.4); no determinate ground—Incoherence of ∅ (§2.7.2)
- **Chapter:** 10 Rival Ultimates
- **Depends On:** Grounding Conditional; No Unconditioned Essence; Necessary Occupancy; Reality–Nature Identity; Concrete-Entity Test; Incoherence of ∅
- **Used By:** Aimed or General; No Outside Selector; No Supernature; The Composer's Interface Burden; The Concreteness Ceiling; The Natural-Reach Fork
- **Established By:** 10.4 What the Rivals Carried

### No Outside Selector

- **Type:** Theorem  **Status:** Added 2026-08-31  **Order:** 2080470
- **Section:** 10.4 What the Rivals Carried
- **Chapter:** 10 Rival Ultimates
- **Statement:** No real selector stands outside Nature or constitutes an independently formed addition within it. A real selector and any determinate selection relation are aspects of Reality–Nature. They may explain which subconfiguration obtains, conditional on the selector and relation, but they cannot explain the actuality of the total configuration from an exterior or surplus position. A concrete selector or operation is T, S, and Φ in determinate operation; an abstract or atemporal selector remains an internal structure and must state its relation to concrete actuality; an unspecified selector supplies no selection. Selection can therefore be an internal explanation of configuration, not an external source of total actuality. **Dependency routes:** one totality—Reality–Nature Identity (§2.8); no external metaphysical layer—Metaphysics–Physics Continuity (§4.5.5); concrete selection—the Concrete-Entity Test (§2.4); abstract or atemporal selection—Grounding-Contact Trilemma (§10.4); prior modal availability—Modal Availability Cannot Be Tuned (§3.5.6)

- **Established By:** 10.4 What the Rivals Carried

### The Identity of the Totality

- **Type:** Theorem  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 2080540
- **Section:** 4.9 Synthesis
- **Statement:** Reality is Nature, exhaustively and without a real exterior remainder, and Nature necessarily instantiates T∧S∧Φ. Separately, the universe in the totality sense is this same Nature, not a container around it and not merely the present observed configuration described by cosmology. Reality, Nature, and the universe in the totality sense are therefore one reality under three names. The particular-arrangement sense of “universe” (this configuration of galaxies and matter) is expressly excluded. The identity stated here is plain identity; the modal theorem governs Nature’s structure rather than separately establishing necessary identity. *Scope.* This is closure of the totality’s *field*—nothing is outside to enlarge it. It is distinct from Modal Closure (§2.9.4), which says the necessary Conditions admit no unnecessary alternative standing apart from them, and from Modal Exclusivity (§7.2.1), which says no modal item within Reality confers Reality’s capacity from outside. The three are companions and are not interchangeable; cite each for its own claim. **Dependency routes:** identity and closure—Necessity of Nature (§2.9.6) and Reality–Nature Identity (§2.8); numerical unicity only—Structural Individuation (§2.4.9)
- **Chapter:** 4 Nature Alone
- **Depends On:** Necessity of Nature; Reality–Nature Identity; Structural Individuation
- **Used By:** Description, Disposition, or Reason; The Value-Contribution Fork
- **Established By:** 7.9 Synthesis

### Exclusivity of Nature

- **Type:** Theorem  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 2080600
- **Section:** §2.9 (2.9 The Whole Line)
- **Statement:** The necessary structural ground of any concrete change-realizer is uniquely T, S, and Φ together. Any proposed alternative *for that role* is either (i) functionally equivalent to T, S, and Φ, in which case it is structure under another description, or (ii) genuinely unable to supply the full Conditions, in which case it cannot ground concrete change-realization. A zero-content candidate is ∅; a thinly or analogically structured candidate is not thereby ∅, but inherits the independent burden of showing how its claimed grounding role reaches concrete change without reinstantiating the Conditions. Nature is not one change-ground among structural competitors. Nor does declining that role secure an outside: any real coexistent belongs to Reality and therefore, by the *Reality–Nature Identity*, to Nature. Chapters 10 and 11 test whether particular necessary-being descriptions remain coherent within that exhaustive identity.
- **Chapter:** 2 The Argument
- **Depends On:** Incoherence of ∅; Necessity of Nature; Reality–Nature Identity; Triconditional Cross-Entailment
- **Used By:** Greatness; Modal Availability Cannot Be Tuned; Modal Closure; Necessary Occupancy; No Supernature; Package Impossibility; The Contentless God Has No Referent; The Cycle (Proposition)
- **Established By:** §2.9 (2.9 The Whole Line)

### Way–Possibility Convertibility

- **Type:** Lemma  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 3020500
- **Section:** §3.2.5 (3.2 Triconditional Necessity: From Below)
- **Statement:** For any P, P is possible iff there is a determinate way for P to be the case: ◇P ↔ ∃ way(P). Convertibility fixes extension—possibilities and ways range over the same candidates—without reducing either vocabulary to the other. From *determinate way* alone, D (determinate difference) follows at the level of generic roles. A directional reading of *way* can add O (directed order); B (bearing or realization) comes from the separate account of what bears or realizes a determinate state. The full T ∧ S ∧ Φ result is not a consequence of convertibility or modal vocabulary. **Feeds into:** No Unconditioned Essence (§7.2.1 The Source of Possibility); The Way-Predicate Is Not Declinable (§10.2.1 Divine Simplicity)

### Constitutive Grounding Non-Propagation

- **Type:** Lemma  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 4040900
- **Section:** 8.2.5 The Modal Collapse Objection
- **Statement:** Two relations must be kept apart. □(T∧S∧Φ) and □◇C are not ground and grounded but one fact under two readings: by the Modal Identity, the necessity of the structural conditions just is the necessary possibility of change read modally, so □◇C carries its necessity by identity, not by transmission across a grounding relation. The structural conditions also ground particular changes, but only in part: to be a change at all is to instantiate T, S, and Φ, while what makes a given change occur rather than another—its initial conditions or outcome—lies outside the three roles. Configurational Necessitation fixes the full-ground conditional, □(P → Q); Strict Actualization yields actual Q from that conditional and actual P. Physical Invariance applies that boundary to complete physical profiles: $\Box\forall x(\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)\rightarrow Q(x))$ fixes what follows of an *M*-realization without establishing $\Box\exists x\,\operatorname{Realizes}(x,M)$. Only an independently established □P permits K to yield □Q. The necessary Conditions therefore constrain every change without making the complete antecedent of every change necessary. □(T∧S∧Φ) ⊢ □◇C, not □C. **Feeds into:** The Sustenance Fork (§10.1.5 The Cosmological Argument)
- **Chapter:** 8 Metaphysics
- **Depends On:** Modal Identity; Configurational Necessitation; Strict Actualization; Physical Invariance
- **Used By:** A Beginning Needs What It Would Begin; The Sustaining Relation's Own Dilemma; The Sustenance Fork; What the Rivals Carried (§8.4)
- **Established By:** 8.2.5 The Modal Collapse Objection

### No Divine Addition

- **Type:** Theorem  **Status:** Added 2026-08-31  **Order:** 5010018
- **Section:** 11.10 What Remains of God?
- **Chapter:** 11 Reclaiming Greatness
- **Statement:** Any God claimed to be actual or necessary must be possible; any possible God must have a determinate way to be. Every determinate way belongs to Reality’s one modal field, which is Nature. By constitutive non-addition, the candidate is therefore Nature itself, Nature in a determinate operation, or an abstraction of such an articulation—not an independently constituted being inserted within Nature or standing outside it. An alleged divine essence does not reopen either location: essence may explain modal truths about the configuration, but No Unconditioned Essence establishes that it is not structurally prior or additional to Nature. If no determinate content answers to the description, no possible divine candidate has been specified.
- **Depends On:** Actuality; Necessity entails Possibility; Way–Possibility Convertibility; Reality–Nature Identity; No Unconditioned Essence
- **Used By:** No Supernature; The Contentless God Has No Referent
- **Established By:** 11.10 What Remains of God?

### No Supernature

- **Type:** Theorem  **Status (as exported):** Stable  **Order:** 5010020
- **Section:** 11.10 What Remains of God?
- **Statement:** Given the Structural Requirement, no concrete act, change, experience, intervention, causal production, or selection occurs outside Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality. A proposed deity performing such work is T, S, and Φ in determinate operation and cannot be the concrete exception to Nature the classical exterior picture requires. A determinate atemporal or analogical ground is an abstract structure of Nature, not an exterior source; if it is invoked to explain concrete actuality, the relation between those articulations must be stated. A strict set withdrawing every determinate feature, truth condition, and relation supplies no specified subject or ground. No Divine Addition closes both alleged remainders: no independently constituted deity stands outside Nature or is added inside it. No Outside Selector adds that selection may explain an internal subconfiguration but not total actuality from an exterior or surplus position. There is therefore no supernature: no second domain, exempt concrete agent, additional divine bearer, exterior selector, unconditioned essence, or exterior source of determinate effects beyond Nature. **Dependency routes:** any divine candidate—No Divine Addition (§11.10); concrete operation—Concrete-Entity Test (§2.4) and Necessary Occupancy (§2.9.7); total actuality and selection—No Outside Selector (§10.4); no determinate content—Incoherence of ∅ (§2.7.2); determinate atemporal ground—Grounding-Contact Trilemma (§10.4) and No Unconditioned Essence (§7.2.1)
- **Chapter:** 11 Reclaiming Greatness
- **Depends On:** Structural Requirement (§2.4); Concrete-Entity Test; No Divine Addition; No Outside Selector; No Unconditioned Essence
- **Used By:** God Precluded (Verdict); Package Impossibility; The Contentless God Has No Referent; The Inversion (Proposition); Three-Horn Dilemma (Proposition)
- **Established By:** The no-way-possible argument (§11.10); Grounding-Contact Trilemma (§10.4); Structural Requirement (§2.4); Concrete-Entity Test
